wiki.aquarium: A public location where marine life and ecosystems are exhibited.
wiki.arcade: A place of wonder and merriment, based on various forms of coin-operated mechanical and electronic game machines. Most popular during the 1980's and 1990's as standalone establishments; now largely limited in the West to smaller areas within amusement parks. Still quite popular in Asia.
wiki.factory: A building or facility designed for the development, production or construction of certain kind of objects or products.
wiki.cathedral: A church that contains the cathedra (throne-like raised seat) of a bishop, thus serving as the central church of a diocese, conference, or episcopate.
wiki.cave interior: Posts that depict an interior of a cave. Cave interior does not count as indoors.
wiki.space station: An artificial man-made facility constructed in outer space that serves as a base of operations or as a relay station.
wiki.head grab: A character firmly grasping the head of another. Commonly seen in explicit oral sex such as irrumatio.
wiki.reverse fellatio: Fellatio where the giver is lying on their back, with their head upside-down relative to the other person's body, also known as "throat swabbing".
wiki.throat bulge: A bulge in the throat caused by something pushing against it from the inside, usually a penis during deepthroat fellatio.
wiki.licking ear: Licking someone's ear; when tongue makes contact with the ear.
wiki.clothes grab: Grabbing or holding on to one's own or someone else's clothes, without the intent to expose their body.
wiki.hand under clothes: A hand is reaching beneath someone's clothing. It doesn't matter if it is a person reaching under their own clothes, or one character doing it to another.
wiki.undressing another: When someone is taking off someone else's clothing.
wiki.blood on face: Blood on a character's face, whether due to blood splatters or bleeding.
wiki.blood on clothes: Blood anywhere on a person's clothes.
wiki.bite mark: The indentation left behind in something, usually skin, after having teeth bitten into it. Usually depicted as a circular dashed line.
wiki.lipstick mark: A lip-shaped print left on a solid surface by a kiss with lipstick.
wiki.lipstick mark on neck: A mark left on the neck with lipstick, typically by a kiss.
wiki.chopsticks: A common Asian eating utensil, consisting of two sticks that are handled between the fingers. Also considered a fashion item to wear in one's hair.
wiki.oil-paper umbrella: A many-ribbed umbrella traditionally used in China, Japan and across southeast Asia. It can be made out of oilpaper or silk.
wiki.chinese knot: A decorative knot made from a single length of cord that is woven into different shapes, with each shape having a symbolic meaning. The knots are usually double-layered and symmetrical.
wiki.uchiwa: Originally from China, the uchiwa is a round or oval hand fan made of paper or silk pasted over a framework of thin bamboo strips.
wiki.turban: The turban is a type of headwear based on cloth winding. Featuring many variations, it is worn as customary headwear primarily by Sikh men and women.
wiki.sparkler: A type of handheld firework. It's a long rod or stick held at one end while the other end burns. Senkou hanabi is a specific type of Japanese sparkler.
wiki.flower necklace: A necklace made from flowers or having flowers in its design.
wiki.bindi: A forehead mark that consists of a colored dot (or sticker) worn on the center of the forehead. It is worn by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists from the Indian subcontinent. The mark is always applied close to the eyebrows or in the middle of the forehead.
wiki.masquerade mask: Masquerade masks are face masks, commonly worn by the upper class at Masquerade balls with the purpose of hiding one's identity and expressing oneself.
wiki.lei: The distinctive Hawaiian flower garland, or slight variations therefrom.
wiki.hijab: An Islamic head covering for women.
wiki.sombrero: A wide-brimmed Mexican hat, often made of straw with an upturned, decorated brim. Most commonly, the one of the mariachi outfit, which is considered to have originated in the state of Jalisco and taken root in the state capital of Guadalajara.
wiki.celtic knot: A variety of knots and stylized graphical representations of knots used for decoration, used extensively in the Celtic style of Insular art.
wiki.kokoshnik: An arch-shaped headdress, similar to a dalachi (headdress). Part of a Russian traditional costume.
wiki.wine: A type of alcohol made from fermenting grapes. It is normally kept in a glass wine bottle and is served in a wine glass. Professionals who deal with wine are called sommeliers.
wiki.sake: An alcoholic drink made from fermented rice.
wiki.pizza: A round, baked flat bread that is typically covered in tomato sauce, cheese, and other toppings such as pepperoni and chili pepper according to preference or culture. Usually sliced into eight triangular pizza slices.
wiki.sushi: A Japanese dish of cooked and seasoned rice served with a variety of other ingredients, which usually includes fish (food).
wiki.ramen: A Japanese wheat-flour noodle soup dish popular in East Asian cuisine, derived from Chinese 'lamian' noodles.
wiki.curry: A food with a spicy sauce, initially in Indian cuisine, and eventually internationalized. Many curries are found in the cuisines of Southeast Asia and East Asia.
wiki.pasta: Italian noodles made out of unleavened dough of wheat flour mixed with water and sometimes egg.
wiki.champagne: A sparkling wine made out of grapes produced in the Champagne region of France.
wiki.mooncake: A Chinese pastry traditionally eaten during the Mid-Autumn Festival. Typically filled with red bean paste and a salted egg yolk.
wiki.lion dance: A form of traditional dance in Chinese culture and other Asian countries in which performers mimic a lion's movements in a lion costume to bring good luck and fortune.
wiki.taco: A popular and traditional Mexican antojito dish composed of a corn or wheat tortilla folded or rolled around a filling. A taco can be made with a variety of fillings, including beef, mutton, shellfish, vegetables and cheese, allowing for great versatility and variety.
wiki.goldfish scooping: A traditional Japanese game played during festivals. Players scoop up goldfish from a pool and take them home in a bag.
wiki.sunflower: A native flowering plant from the Americas, recognizable by their single large yellow flower, with an initially greenish center that turns yellow-brown and then blackish as it matures. They typically grow to heights of around 3 meters (10 feet).
wiki.autumn leaves: Leaves that fall from trees in autumn, usually red, brown, or yellow in color.
wiki.fireworks: Explosive or other pyrotechnic devices used for celebration or entertainment purposes. There are many forms of fireworks in the modern world.
wiki.maple leaf: The leaf of the maple tree, most likely of the Japanese maple variety (Kaede, "Acer Japonica"). A common feature of pictures set in the autumn.
wiki.plum blossoms: The blossoms of plum trees, especially of the genus Prunus mume. The petals are white, pink or red, and bloom in early spring.
wiki.print kimono: A kimono that has any type of stylized printed patterns on it, such as flowers, hearts, animals, and such. This includes other kimono-styled tops such as yukatas and furisodes.
wiki.floral print kimono: A print kimono with a floral print.
wiki.ancient egyptian clothes: Clothing based on ancient Egyptian culture, often featuring blue-and-yellow color themes, gold jewelry, and ancient Egyptian cultural elements, such as the Eye of Horus, Uraeus, ankh, snake and scarab.
wiki.korean clothes: Any variety of traditional Korean clothing.
wiki.german clothes: Any variety of traditional German clothing, as worn in Germany and Austria.
wiki.vietnamese clothes: Traditional clothing from Vietnam. Many feature come from the Nguyen dynasty.
wiki.roman clothes: Clothes of the Roman people until the fall of the Western Roman Empire in the late 5th century AD, or garments styled after those clothes.
wiki.flamenco dress: A dress used to dance flamenco.
wiki.sari: A simple feminine garment made of a length of unstitched samite. It is worn around the waist just below the navel, tucked and pleated, wrapping around the body twice, the remaining length folded and draped over the shoulder. It can also be raised to drape over the head for modesty and to conceal ones features.
wiki.tabi: Traditional Japanese split-toe socks with a division between the big toe and the other toes in order to be worn with sandals.
wiki.okobo: Japanese platform sandals that were traditionally worn by geisha during their apprenticeship. The most notable type in fanart are the black-lacquered kind with red straps.
wiki.cornrows: Hair that is braided very close to the scalp, resulting in rows of raised braids on the head.
wiki.facial mark: Markings on the face, simple in design. Either drawn on, tattooed, applied with makeup, or formed as a unique birthmark.
wiki.forehead mark: A facial mark on the forehead ranging from a simple dot, to more elaborate designs.
wiki.american flag: The flag of the United States of America, colloquially known as the Stars and Stripes. For images that only show patterns or other symbols representing the United States rather than the flag itself, use the United States tag.
wiki.rice bowl: A bowl specifically for containing an individual serving of rice. It is usually smaller and rounder than other bowls.
wiki.japanese flag: The national flag of Japan, consisting of a red circle on a white background.
wiki.german flag: The modern flag of Germany, consisting of three horizontal bars colored black, red, and yellow.
wiki.tribal tattoo: A tattoo with a tribal design.
wiki.french flag: The Flag of France, the famous Tricolor blue, white, and red flag. Historical variants have included the fleur-de-lis. The modern design is used as the pattern in the French flag bikini and French flag swimsuit.
wiki.russian flag: The national flag of Russia has three horizontal stripes of white, blue, and red respectively.
wiki.subway: An urban railroad system that is usually, albeit not always, underground. They are also commonly referred to as metro or rapid transit.
wiki.native american clothes: Clothes traditionally worn by Native Americans, such as the traditional Native American headdress.
wiki.gondola: A traditional passenger-carrying boat of Venice, Italy. It is often steered by a single person standing on the rear deck, with the oar resting on an oarlock. Gondolas with multiple rowers also exist, an example being the traghetto or ferry gondola.
wiki.rickshaw: A two-wheeled cart pulled by a person to carry passengers. The English word is a borrowing from the Japanese jinrikisha, literally "human-powered cart".
wiki.poncho: A blanket-like cloak with a hole in the center for the head, either laying on the shoulders and coming down to the chest, or reaching to the hips.
wiki.new year: An image relating to the first day of the new year on the Gregorian calendar.
wiki.desert: An arid, barren environment. Usually covered in predominantly sand or very loose soil with few animals and plants (e.g. palm trees and cacti) which can survive with very small amounts of water.
wiki.skyline: The outline created by a city over the horizon, usually against the background of the sky. Major real-world cities have distinctive skylines that can serve to identify a location without having to name it.
wiki.sunflower field: A flower field consisting exclusively of sunflowers, most commonly a farm of giant sunflowers. A very common motif for summer-themed illustrations.
wiki.summer festival: A general term for various festivals celebrated in summer in Japan.
wiki.easter: Easter, also called Pascha (Greek/Latin) or Resurrection Sunday, is a festival and holiday celebrating the resurrection of Jesus from the dead. In Christian faith, Jesus died on the cross on Good Friday and was buried. On Easter Sunday, He revived and returned to Heaven to be with the Almighty Father.
wiki.european architecture: Buildings and other structures constructed in traditional European design.
wiki.canal: A large flowing body of water made by mankind. The natural equivalent is the river.
wiki.tropical: Images that are themed after the tropics - the warm, hot areas located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. Common elements include the beach, market or jungle; a clear sunny sky; flowers, fruits, plants and animals native to the region; and characters wearing very light clothing.
wiki.lantern festival: The Lantern Festival is an event which marks the end of the Chinese New Year celebrations. It's Chinese name is Yuanxiao Festival, which refers to tangyuan, the food that is eaten on the festival.
wiki.eiffel tower: A wrought iron tower built in Paris by Gustave Eiffel for the 1889 World's Fair. It is a globally recognized cultural icon of France and the tallest structure in the French capital, standing 320 m (1,050 ft) high above the green expanse of the Champ de Mars The bronze-painted tower has two observation decks and restaur…
wiki.sphinx: In Egyptian mythology, a sphinx is a creature that has the body of a lion, while the head could be a human, ram, or bird. They are most commonly assigned to protect the sacred places.
wiki.savannah: A savanna or savannah is a mixed woodland-grassland ecosystem characterized by the trees being sufficiently widely spaced so that the canopy does not close. It is characterized by coarse grasses and scattered tree growth, especially on the margins of the tropics where the rainfall is seasonal, as in eastern Africa.
wiki.mid-autumn festival: The Mid-Autumn Festival (simplified Chinese: 中秋节; traditional Chinese: 中秋節), also known as Moon Festival or Mooncake Festival, is a traditional Chinese festival celebrated by China and many East and Southeast Asian people under the influence of China.
wiki.oktoberfest: Oktoberfest, or Wiesn, is a 16-day festival held annually in Munich, Bavaria, Germany, running from late September to the first weekend in October.
wiki.colosseum: Originally the Flavian Amphitheatre, an elliptical amphitheater in the center of the city of Rome (city), Italy, the largest ever built in the Roman Empire, built of concrete and stone. It is considered one of the greatest works of Roman architecture and Roman engineering and is also famous as a gladiatorial arena.
wiki.statue of liberty: The Statue of Liberty (Liberty Enlightening the World, French: La Liberté éclairant le monde) is a colossal neoclassical statue on Liberty Island in New York City Harbor.
wiki.igloo: A snow shelter built from blocks of packed snow. They're used as seasonal or long term structures, as opposed to temporary snow shelters like a quinzhee.
wiki.oasis: A fertile spot in an arid region (mainly deserts), where water is found. Usually vegetated.
wiki.black skin: Skin colored pure black, like coal or ebony. The opposite of white skin.
wiki.ink wash painting: A type of brush painting that uses washes of black ink, of the kind used in calligraphy. It is traditionally greyscale, using only shades of black, with an emphasis on brushwork.
wiki.flying: Moving through the air with the help of a propulsion system (usually wings, a magic broom or a mechanical device), or being hurled to the air for some distance by either a person or hit by something.
wiki.adjusting eyewear: Positioning eyewear on the face to see better, either by pushing them up onto the head or adjusting their position in line with the eyes.
wiki.praying: The act of addressing a deity for a blessing, a request, or to give thanks. Characterized with clasped hands or palms together, sometimes with closed eyes, and having a reverent expression.
wiki.adjusting gloves: The act of adjusting one's gloves, usually tugging them down for a better fit.
wiki.spinning: When something is either rotating continuously in 2D (where it just rotates itself) or in 3D (much like a spinning top).
wiki.walking away: When one or more characters are seen walking away from something, often the viewer or another character.
wiki.horizon: The horizon is the border between earth (planet) and sky. As the horizon is usually obscured by trees, mountains, buildings, etc., it is most visible in settings dominated by the ocean or other featureless terrain.
wiki.landscape: Scenery focusing on the natural environment, such as forests, fields, mountains, hills, rivers, or lakes. Will generally include a horizon.
wiki.colorful background: A background with a noticeable array of several colors.
wiki.arm up: A single arm is raised up, and the hand is around eye level or above.
wiki.arm support: When a character is using their arm(s) to support their own body weight.
wiki.hand on own face: When a character has a hand on their own face. Often overlaps with hand on own cheek.
wiki.hand in own hair: Characters with a hand in their own hair.
wiki.arms at sides: Both of a character's arms at rest right next to both sides of their body.
wiki.back-to-back: Two characters who are behind each other or facing back to back.
wiki.hand on own thigh: When a character has a single hand on their own thigh.
wiki.hand on own knee: A character is resting one hand on one of their own knees.
wiki.leaning to the side: A character is leaning their upper body off to one side. The lower body can either remain stationary, or tilt in a direction of its own.
wiki.leaning on object: Leaning against an object or a piece of furniture without being completely bent over.
wiki.sitting on stairs: A character is sitting on stairs.
wiki.hand on own neck: When one of a character's hands is on their own neck.
wiki.sitting on object: Someone is sitting on an object.
wiki.balancing: A person either balancing themselves or balancing an object so that it stays upright without falling.
wiki.handstand: Standing upside-down using the arms and hands for support.
wiki.holding own wrist: Holding one's own lower arm or wrist.
wiki.androgynous: A person with facial or bodily features that make it ambiguous whether they're male or female. Traps, bishounens, reverse traps and handsome ladies often display this trait.
wiki.old woman: A woman who is old, typically more than 50 to 60 years old. Common signs include grey hair and wrinkled skin.
wiki.trap: A male character who looks female. Also known as "femboy", or less frequently as "tomgirl".
wiki.otoko no ko: A male character who looks female. Also known as "femboy", or less frequently as "tomgirl".
wiki.isometric: A method of representing a 3D object on a 2D plane used in technical and engineering drawings. Unlike in perspective drawings or real life, parallel lines do not converge to a vanishing point and objects appear to be the same size regardless of distance.
wiki.6+girls: An image containing six or more female characters. Male characters may also be present in addition to the female characters.
wiki.4boys: An image depicting four male characters.
wiki.6+boys: Images depicting 6 or more male characters.
wiki.siblings: Two or more people who share at least one parent.
wiki.sisters: Two or more females who share at least one parent.
wiki.yaoi: Any romantic or sexual interaction between males, whether mutual or one-sided. If it's mutual, consider also adding the couple tag.
wiki.couple: Two characters who are in a romantic relationship with each other.
wiki.age difference: A pair (or more) of characters who are interacting with one another with a highly-visible apparent difference between their ages, based on visual cues such as physical maturity, size, etc.
wiki.twins: Two siblings from the same birth, often looking very similar if not identical.
wiki.brothers: Two or more males who share at least one parent.
wiki.husband and wife: When a married man and woman are together in an image.
wiki.family: A social unit composed of parents and their children. Use this tag when the complete family unit is shown, with all living parents and children.
wiki.group picture: A group of characters posing together for a picture.
wiki.paw pose: A hand pose imitating animal paws. Stereotypically the hands are held near the face, in a closed fist, with the elbows and wrists bent, similar to how a cat or dog might hold up its paw.
wiki.shushing: Placing the index finger vertically in front of the lips, with the other fingers curled inwards. Used to indicate a request for silence.
wiki.bored: An emotional state experienced when a character is left without anything in particular to do, and not interested in their surroundings.
wiki.confident: When a character is confident, perhaps even overconfident. This can be represented in a variety of ways. The most common expression is a smirk with v-shaped eyebrows.
wiki.facing viewer: A character facing the viewer but with their eyes closed, covered, is faceless or looking in another direction.
wiki.tomboy: A girl who displays boyish behaviors.
wiki.planet: A large spherical astronomical object that typically orbits a star (sky). The tag should be used when at least one planet is seen from outer space or from the surface of another nearby planet. This includes real and fictional planets.
wiki.lake: A large body of standing water, larger than a pond, that is completely surrounded by land.
wiki.earth (planet): Our home planet, the third closest planet to the sun between Venus (planet) and Mars (planet). Use this tag for depiction of the planet from outside.
wiki.lava: Rock that has been liquefied by extreme heat. Molten rock that is still underground is referred to as magma, while molten rock that is above ground is referred to as lava.
wiki.island: Any form of land that is surrounded by a watery body.
wiki.carousel: An amusement park ride that consists of toy horses spinning around in a fixed place, also known as a merry-go-round.
wiki.abandoned: Buildings, vehicles, or places that haven't been used or maintained in a long time.
wiki.dock: A structure built near the shore where ships or boats are moored to load and unload goods or passengers. It may have piers or jetties to provide access to ships.
wiki.volcano: An opening in a planet's crust where magma, gases, and volcanic ash escape from below the surface. Typically depicted as a mountain with smoke or lava coming out from the top.
wiki.asteroid: An asteroid is a metallic, icey or rocky body that in orbits a star (sky) and lacks any atmosphere.
wiki.scar on face: A scar on any part of a character's face.
wiki.cloudy sky: A sky filled with a significant amount of clouds. As a general rule, the sky is at least 50% covered by clouds. If the sky is completely covered by clouds, use overcast instead.
wiki.comic: Any sort of sequential art, including web comics, doujinshi, 4koma, etc.
wiki.painterly: Digital art that resembles a traditional painting.
wiki.cyberpunk: A science fiction genre characterized by its focus on "high tech and lowlife". Basic themes include the dehumanizing effects of technology, and the accompanying societal breakdown. Think dark and dirty, with lots of wires and neon lights.
wiki.steampunk: A genre of science fiction set in Victorian times when steam was the main source of machine power. Common visual elements include Victorian fashion, accessories such as goggles, pocket watches, belt pouches, and test tubes, and machines with industrial pipes, steam, and lots of gears.
wiki.art nouveau: An art movement popular during the late 19th and early 20th century that combined fine art, graphic and industrial design. Although Art Nouveau was not a single style, Le Style Mucha (The style of (Alphonse) Mucha), as characterized by bold lines, flat, rich colors, flowing curves and ornate circular patterns and borde…
wiki.neon palette: A palette predominated by bright, saturated, shiny and even glowing colors with an overall cool tone. Pink, purple, blue and aqua are the most common and iconic colors, but other colors such as red, green and yellow may be used as well.
wiki.messy room: A room with a lot of clutter.
wiki.infirmary: A nurse's office (typically in a school) or hospital room. Often contains a hospital bed surrounded by curtains.
wiki.public restroom: A bathroom in a public institution, which has multiple toilets surrounded by stalls for privacy.
wiki.restroom: A bathroom in a public institution, which has multiple toilets surrounded by stalls for privacy.
wiki.vehicle interior: The interior of any type of vehicle. Vehicle interior does not count as indoors.
wiki.closet: Either a built-in wardrobe or a room with a door used for storing things, specially clothes.
wiki.spacecraft interior: A scene set inside a spacecraft.
wiki.washitsu: A Japanese room with traditional tatami flooring, also known as a tatami room.
wiki.otaku room: A room filled with otaku merchandise, including but not limited to: figures, anime poster (object)s, manga (object)s, dakimakura (object), character dolls, computer equipment, game consoles, and electronics. They are typically messy and very crowded.
wiki.clubroom: A room within a school where students can engage in various club-related activities such as music, art and games.
wiki.garage: A building used for the storing of cars and other motor vehicles. Comes in residential and commercial variants, such as those found in homes and at mechanic shops.
wiki.dressing room: A backstage room where idols, actors, or musicians change their costumes and makeup before and after performances. Mirrors, chairs, and bright lighting are standard; expect to also see vanity tables full of cosmetics.
wiki.genkan: Traditional Japanese entryway area, where shoes are removed before entering the rest of the house.
wiki.dining room: A room in a residential home or apartment where food that was prepared in the kitchen is consumed.
wiki.warehouse: A large building for storing goods. They commonly have loading docks, cargo pallets, and many shelves. They may also have cranes or other large machinery designed to assist in loading or unloading goods.
wiki.backstage: The area behind the stage in a theater or concert hall.
wiki.cafeteria: A dining facility in large institution like a school, office, camp, hospital etc. where the members of that institution come to eat, although public cafeterias exist, mostly as a cheap dining option.
wiki.throne room: The room in a castle where the throne is located, upon which the designated ruler sits upon.
wiki.concert: A live musical performance done in front of an audience. Either by a band or a solo performer.
wiki.theater: A building intended to house and provide seating for dramatic and/or musical performances, most often plays, movies or concerts.
wiki.planetarium: A planetarium (plural planetaria or planetariums) is a theater built primarily for presenting educational and entertaining shows about astronomy and the night sky, or for training in celestial navigation.
wiki.shop: A small store or department in a large store selling a specific or select type of goods.
wiki.bakery: A shop that bakes sweets, cakes, and breads, then sells them fresh from the oven.
wiki.laundromat: An establishment with coin-operated washing machines and clothes dryers for public use.
wiki.maid cafe: A type of Japanese cafe that features waitresses dressed as French maids and performing various fanservices. Typically serves omurice along with various drinks.
wiki.flower shop: A shop that sells flowers and plants.
wiki.conveyor belt sushi: Also called kaiten-zushi, this is a sushi restaurant where the plates with the sushi are placed on a rotating conveyor belt or moat that winds through the restaurant and moves past every table, counter and seat.
wiki.skating rink: A frozen body of water and/or an artificial sheet of ice where people can ice skate or play winter sports.
wiki.sewer: A place where water and waste are drained.
wiki.water slide: A wet version of the slide.
wiki.empty pool: A swimming pool that has been drained of water.
wiki.yatai: A small, mobile food stand in Japan typically selling hot food, such as ramen.
wiki.gas station: A shop where gasoline is supplied and sold for automobiles and motorcycles.
wiki.porch: A platform-like structure attached to the front of a house with a roof. Porches typically have wooden floorboards, but are otherwise exposed to the outside. A common setting for summer pictures.
wiki.railroad tracks: The permanent pathway structure for trains, boxcars, locomotives, minecarts, railway guns or streetcars.
wiki.railroad crossing: An intersection where railroad tracks cross a road.
wiki.industrial: A setting depicting heavy industry or factory environment.
wiki.gazebo: A pavilion structure built for shelter or ornamental use, particularly in parks or gardens. Gazebos are typically eight-sided and open on all sides, with conical or dome-shaped roofs.
wiki.pedestrian bridge: A bridge built over a street for the purpose of allowing pedestrians quick and convenient access to either side. Common in urban areas.
wiki.clock tower: A clock tower is a tower specifically built with one or more (often four) clock faces. Clock towers can be either freestanding or part of a church or municipal building such as a town hall.
wiki.lighthouse: A tower, found near the ocean or large bodies of water, that emits light in order to provide navigational aid for sailors. It has a distinct room at the top, which contains the lamp and lens, and an exterior platform below it.
wiki.treehouse: A structure built within a tree or nestled amongst its branches.
wiki.shore: The border between land, such as a cliff, riverside, or beach, and a larger body of water, such as a river, lake, or ocean.
wiki.hill: A naturally raised area of land, not as high or craggy as a mountain.
wiki.stream: A flowing body of water smaller and shallower than a river.
wiki.floating island: A piece of natural land floating in the sky.
wiki.wetland: An ecosystem that is flooded by water and features plants and animals adept to surviving waterlogged environments.
wiki.coral reef: A reef composed mainly of coral and other organic matter of which parts have solidified into limestone.
wiki.canyon: A deep depression between cliffs carved from the landscape by a river. Often formed by a process of long-time erosion from a plateau level, and are very wide and meandering. Not to be confused with ravine, which is both more narrow and straight.
wiki.valley: An area of low-lying land between hills or mountains. Most valleys are formed by water erosion over an extremely long period of time, and often contain rivers.
wiki.glacier: A large, persistent mass of ice that formed on land over many years or centuries and that constantly moves under its own weight. The largest glaciers can span entire continents and are called continental glaciers or ice sheets, such as the one that covers the entirety of Antarctica.
wiki.boat: A relatively small, open watercraft. Boats come in a large variety of types and sizes, but unlike ships they are usually small, holding only a few people rather than a large crew, and usually used on rivers, lakes, and coastal areas rather than the open sea.
wiki.ship: A large seagoing vessel, as opposed to a boat which more commonly refers to smaller vessels.
wiki.spacecraft: A spacecraft is a craft or vehicle or machine designed for spaceflight. They are frequently depicted in many works of Science Fiction.
wiki.bus: A rectangular, oblong passenger road vehicle used as a mass/public transport.
wiki.airship: A type of fantasy aircraft or spacecraft from the fantasy or science fiction genres. Often, airships look similar to real ships, except flying in the air or space through magical or fantastical means. For reference, the Palanquin ship and the Space Battleship Yamato are the archtypical example of an airship.
wiki.train station platform: The platform of a train station where passengers are loaded onto the train.
wiki.steam locomotive: A train locomotive powered by coal-fired steam engine. Can be distinguished by the general bulkier appearance compared to a diesel or electric locomotive, and a prominent boiler and funnel at the front of the vehicle.
wiki.rowboat: A small boat meant to seat a few people, propelled by rowing with oars instead of by sails.
wiki.submarine: A submersible marine vessel. More often than not, they are also a military warship.
wiki.streetcar: A kind of rail vehicle that runs on public roads alongside cars. Known as a tram outside of North America.
wiki.shipwreck: The wrecked remains of a ship that has either sunk or beached.
wiki.subway station: An underground train station where subway systems load and unload passengers, most commonly found in urban areas.
wiki.hell: In religion and folklore, hell is a place of eternal suffering and torment, meant to punish evil souls in the afterlife. It is the place where demons and other vile creatures reside.
wiki.floating city: Either a city built on one or more floating islands or a collection of buildings floating in the air.
wiki.heaven: In religion and folklore, heaven is a higher realm where gods and angels, as well as those who committed good deeds reside after their death.
wiki.underwater city: A city that is located underwater.
wiki.tokyo: The capital of Japan and the most populated city in the world.
wiki.tokyo (city): The capital of Japan and the most populated city in the world.
wiki.mount fuji: The highest mountain in Japan at 3,776 m (12,388 ft), and one of the iconic images of the nation. Although it has not erupted in over 300 years, it is still an active volcano.
wiki.pyramid (structure): A monumental structure with a square or triangular base and sloping sides that meet in a point at the top, especially one built of stone as a royal tomb in ancient Egypt.
wiki.tokyo tower: A steel lattice communications and observation tower in Tokyo.
wiki.kyoto (city): A city located in the central part of the island of Honshu, Japan. It has a population close to 1.5 million. Formerly the imperial capital of Japan for more than 1000 years, it is now the capital city of Kyoto Prefecture located in the Kansai region, as well as a major part of the Kyoto-Osaka (city)-Kobe metropolitan a…
wiki.kyoto: A city located in the central part of the island of Honshu, Japan. It has a population close to 1.5 million. Formerly the imperial capital of Japan for more than 1000 years, it is now the capital city of Kyoto Prefecture located in the Kansai region, as well as a major part of the Kyoto-Osaka (city)-Kobe metropolitan a…
wiki.elizabeth tower: The iconic clock tower of Westminster Palace in London, United Kingdom. Simply known as the Westminster Clock Tower before 2012 when it was renamed during the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II. It houses the world famous bell Big Ben (the name of which is sometimes incorrectly used for the tower).
wiki.new york city: The largest city of the state of New York. It is also the largest city in the United States and a major commercial and cultural center.
wiki.tokyo skytree: A freestanding 634 meter (2,080 ft) tall broadcasting and observation tower in Tokyo, Japan. Construction was completed in February 2012. The tallest building in Japan and the tallest tower in the world, and also the third tallest structure in the world after the Burj Khalifa in Dubai and the Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpu…
wiki.taipei 101: Taipei 101 (Chinese: 台北101 / 臺北101, formerly the Taipei World Financial Center) is a landmark skyscraper located in Xinyi District, Taipei, Taiwan.
wiki.bookshelf: A piece of furniture designed for storing rows of books. Typically they have multiple rows of shelves for storing lots of books neatly.
wiki.kotatsu: A low table sandwiching a blanket and containing an electric heater underneath, with enough space to rest underneath for one or more people, depending on size. It is something of a wintertime necessity for the many Japanese homes that lack proper insulation for central heating systems.
wiki.crane game: A type of arcade game in which a player attempts to pick up prizes using a mechanical claw. The prizes are usually small toys, stuffed animals, or character dolls.
wiki.arcade cabinet: A traditional arcade machine where patrons can insert money for credits to play a video game. The upright cabinet is popular in North America.
wiki.purikura: Short for "Print Club", Purikura is a type of Japanese photo booth that takes pictures of people's faces or figures and prints them onto stickers with various effects applied. It produces what would today be called selfies with face filters applied.
wiki.road: A route that has been paved or otherwise improved for travel by foot or vehicle. Possible road surfaces include dirt, gravel, concrete, and asphalt.
wiki.path: A road or trail meant for foot traffic. Examples include hiking trails, paths worn by wildlife or livestock, or the approach to a Shinto shrine.
wiki.town: A medium sized settlement. Towns are generally larger and more modern than villages, but not as big or developed as a city.
wiki.crosswalk: A crosswalk, or pedestrian crossing, is a specially paved or marked path on a street or road for pedestrians to cross it.
wiki.sidewalk: A paved path for pedestrians at the side of a road.
wiki.urban: A scene that emphasizes the developed features of a large city. This includes elements such as asphalt streets, concrete walls, densely packed buildings, artificial lighting, graffiti, power lines, or industrial pipes.
wiki.dirt road: An unpaved road covered with dirt or gravel. Common in rural or sparsely inhabited areas.
wiki.hedge: Trimmed rows of bushes, found in variety of outdoor places such as parks and in front of houses.
wiki.fence: A barrier enclosing or bordering a field, yard, etc., usually made of posts and wire or wood, used to prevent entrance, to confine, or to mark a boundary.
wiki.brick wall: A wall made entirely out of brick.
wiki.power lines: Cables hung from utility poles or transmission towers to carry electricity across long distances.
wiki.utility pole: A pole, frequently made of wood, used to support overhead power lines and various other public utilities, such as electrical cable, fiber optic cable, and related equipment such as transformers and lampposts.
wiki.chain-link fence: A type of woven fence usually made from galvanized or LLDPE-coated steel wire. The wire runs vertically and is bent into a zig-zag pattern so each "zig" is quickly trapped on one side with the wire and each "zag" with the wire quickly traps the other.
wiki.graffiti: A decorated writing or a drawing made on a wall, vehicle, or other public surface, usually without permission. Graffiti is often made with spray paint.
wiki.vending machine: A machine that automatically dispenses items such as snacks, drinks, or alcohol after inserting money or coins into the machine.
wiki.traffic light: A traffic light (also known as a traffic signal or stoplight) is a signaling device positioned at road intersections, crosswalks, and other locations in order to control the flow of vehicular traffic.
wiki.billboard: A large sign typically found alongside busy roads, used to display advertisements.
wiki.phone booth: A small structure furnished with a payphone (and often a phone book) and designed for making calls. Usually the booth has a door to provide privacy and a window. This tag should ideally be used for glassed-in enclosures with a door, but at minimum should have at least privacy dividers and/or a weatherproof roof.
wiki.building: Any man-made enclosed, permanent and rigid structure used or intended for supporting, sheltering any use or continuous occupancy.
wiki.stairs: A device composed of elevated stationary platforms that takes a person or object from one place to another, either higher or lower.
wiki.architecture: An image that has structures with a definitive architectural style.
wiki.stone stairs: Stairs made out of stone or any stone-like material (concrete, cobblestone, etc.)
wiki.komainu: Lion-like statues often seen flanking the entrance to a shrine.
wiki.jizou: A buddhist statue commonly found along roadsides and in cemeteries in Japan.
wiki.rock: A stone; a natural object made of hard mineral.
wiki.palm tree: A type of tree that is characterized by a tall, branchless trunk crowned by large palm leaves. Palm trees grow in tropical climates and are often associated with beaches.
wiki.mountainous horizon: When the horizon's edge consists of a long mountain or a series of mountain tops.
wiki.puddle: A small pool of water on a surface, usually on a path or road. This accumulation can be caused by rainy weather.
wiki.overgrown: Vegetation that has overtaken the works of man, especially the ruins of a building or city.
wiki.stalactite: Icicle-shaped cave formations created by minerals building up from dripping water.
wiki.moon: A celestial body orbiting a planet. Please also tag with full moon, gibbous moon, or crescent moon as appropriate.
wiki.milky way: The galactic home of the Earth_(planet), the Sun, and between 100 and 400 billion other star (sky)s. It is roughly disc-shaped, with a diameter approximately 80 times its thickness, while the Solar System is roughly 60% of the way from the center to the rim.
wiki.science fiction: A genre of fiction which centers around futuristic science and technology.
wiki.post-apocalypse: The desolation left behind after a huge war or other major disaster on a global scale. The settings were often used in fictional works of varying genres. Usually involves the theme of "survival of the fittest", a fascination of the bygone civilizations, an attempt to restore the old worlds, as well as a "savior" who pr…
wiki.holding gun: A gun being held by a character.
wiki.holding knife: Holding a knife. If the knife is held pointing downwards, it's in reverse grip.
wiki.holding staff: The act of holding a staff.
wiki.pointing: The act of directing attention to something, usually by using one's index finger. Don't confuse with index finger raised.
wiki.index finger raised: The index finger of a character's hand is raised while the other fingers stay down, but the character is not pointing. A famous, paradigmatic example is the fgsfds meme.
wiki.reaching: Physically reaching out for something, either with the hands, legs, or other objects.
wiki.waving: The motion of waving one's hand or arm as if saying "Hi!", "Bye!", or "Over here!".
wiki.punching: Hitting someone with a clenched hand.
wiki.hand on another's shoulder: Resting a single hand on another character's shoulder.
wiki.hand on another's face: Resting a hand somewhere on another's face.
wiki.hand on another's cheek: When one of a character's hands is placed on another character's cheek.
wiki.feeding: The giving of food to an animal or another person. Often a sign of affection.
wiki.between fingers: Holding something between two fingers, such as a weapon, ofuda, card, cigarette, etc.
wiki.own hands together: When a single character touches their hands together.
wiki.dual wielding: Holding a weapon in each hand. Usually, the two weapons are of the same type. If the two weapons are different, it's asymmetrical dual wielding.
wiki.aiming: Aiming a gun, bow (weapon), or other ranged weapon at a target, or in a posture that otherwise suggests that they have their eyes on a target.
wiki.tying hair: Tying the hair to form a ponytail, twintails, or other similar hairstyle. This often involves reaching behind the head while holding a hair tie in the mouth.
wiki.licking: Passing the tongue over an object, surface, person, or body part.
wiki.kicking: Hitting someone with the leg or foot, or using the feet to strike an object, such as a ball when playing sports.
wiki.falling: The act of going down from the air to the ground by means of gravity.
wiki.wide-eyed: Having the eyes completely opened, to the point that the sclera is visible all the way around the iris.
wiki.laughing: An involuntary reaction to a humorous comment, story, joke or situation. It can involve producing sounds from the lungs while the face and body are contorted, and bearing a wide smile to express amusement or mirth.
wiki.yawning: Breathing while sleepy or bored. Characterized visually by opening one's mouth wide and having half- or fully-closed eyes. May sometimes include tears, since yawning can cause excess tears to spill out of the face. Often appears alongside stretching. May sometimes occur alongside the appearance of squeans.
wiki.raised eyebrow: Raising a single eyebrow, like this: 🤨. This can be out of confusion, smugness, or in a sexual fashion along with a naughty face.
wiki.letterboxed: A technique where horizontal bars are displayed at the top and bottom of the picture. This can be done to give the image a cinematic look, or to make it fit a certain aspect ratio.
wiki.perspective: An image that greatly emphasizes the three-dimensional aspects or depth of the subject, especially when the subject is viewed at a strong or unusual angle.
wiki.symmetry: An image that is symmetrical. This is usually when the entire image can be divided into two halves that look the same in some way, except they're rotated or flipped.
wiki.blush stickers: A blush that appears as solid circles or ovals sitting on the cheeks. It's often drawn with borders around the edges, a solid fill color, or other stylized shading, and may go past the edge of the cheeks.
wiki.veins: Large blood vessels bulging under the skin.
wiki.arm tattoo: A tattoo located on the arm.
wiki.leg tattoo: A tattoo located on the legs.
wiki.neck tattoo: A tattoo located on the neck.
wiki.scar on cheek: A scar on a character's cheek.
wiki.nervous sweating: Heavy sweat due to extreme nervousness, embarrassment, or fear.
wiki.nosebleed: Blood issuing from the nose, whether from being aroused or from a broken nose.
wiki.eyes visible through hair: When someone has their hair over one eye or hair over eyes, but the hair doesn't obscure the eyes completely and leaves them still visible, either through a gap in the hair strands or because the hair is depicted as translucent enough.
wiki.colored eyelashes: Eyelashes that have an unnatural color, anything other than the usual black or brown. Consider adding eyelashes if the eyelashes are prominent.
wiki.star-shaped pupils: When a character's pupils are shaped like a star (symbol). This tag is only for when the entire pupil is shaped like a star. Use star in eye for cases where there is a star present inside the eyes. Very often the pupils are bright.
wiki.narrowed eyes: Eyes that are narrow. Either because they have been closed half-way, doing jitome, or are naturally narrow, without any physical exertion.
wiki.biceps: The bicep is the large muscle that lies on the front of the upper arm between the shoulder and the elbow.
wiki.ribs: Ambiguous tag. • see visible ribcage for characters so skinny that their ribcage is visible through the skin • see exposed ribcage for the ribcage being exposed outside of the skin, such as in guro posts • see inside ribcage for a character depicted as inside a ribcage • see ribs (food) for the food
wiki.shoulder blades: The scapula, or shoulder blade, is either of the two flat bones, roughly triangular, found on the shoulder girdle. Their shapes are visible in the skin of the back of people.
wiki.buttons: Buttons on clothing. Typically used to fasten together shirts, pants, or sleeves, but sometimes they are purely decorative.
wiki.animal print: An article of clothing or an object that has a printed design of an animal, or is modeled after the fur or external appearance of an animal.
wiki.polka dot: A pattern composed of same-sized circles spaced equally.
wiki.pocket: A small bag or pouch sewn into a piece of clothing, meant to hold small items.
wiki.zipper: A popular device - designed with specially shaped metal or plastic teeth - for temporarily joining two edges of fabric. It's also on other daily used items: suitcases, backpacks, handbags etc.
wiki.breast pocket: A pocket on the chest of a shirt or other top.
wiki.cow print: A black and white pattern based off the pattern found on Holstein dairy cows.
wiki.bandages: A strip of material such as gauze used to protect or treat an injury.
wiki.crown: A ceremonial type of headgear traditionally worn by royalty.
wiki.brooch: A clasp or pin that typically has a gem attached, often secured to a piece of garment.
wiki.anklet: A piece of jewelry, resembling a bangle or bracelet, but worn around the ankle.
wiki.pendant: A piece of jewelry that hangs from a necklace, collar, or choker as the centerpiece.
wiki.gem: A smooth precious stone, often used to make jewelry. For faceted precious stones, see crystal.
wiki.buckle: A clasp used to fasten the ends of a belt or strap together.
wiki.belt buckle: A decorative buckle or clasp used to fasten a belt.
wiki.name tag: A name tag sewn or pinned on a piece of clothing, such as on a gym uniform, school swimsuit, or employee uniform.
wiki.lace-up boots: Boots with shoelaces that can be tied up like sneakers.
wiki.suspender skirt: A skirt that is held up by suspenders. Commonly known as a jumperskirt or "JSK" for short, especially when worn in lolita fashion with a petticoat beneath.
wiki.shoulder bag: A bag that one carries by the shoulder, as opposed to a handbag.
wiki.pouch: Broad term for various small containers usually made from leather, textiles, or plastic. Objects called pouches include: • A small non-rigid bag usually with a drawstring for holding or carrying things. • A small semi-rigid container closed with a zipper.
wiki.suitcase: A carrying case made of cloth, leather, or even plastic. It is used mainly for transporting clothes and other possessions during trips.
wiki.sword: A bladed weapon designed for cutting or thrusting. They are typically composed of a hilt and a blade with one or two edges that can be straight or curved; most, but not all, swords have a pointed tip. The hilt, in turn, consists of a guard, a grip, and in most designs a pommel.
wiki.katana: A type of Japanese sword, often called a "samurai sword" because of its historical associations with feudal-era Japan.
wiki.knife: A tool or weapon consisting of a short blade and a handle, used for cutting, stabbing, or slashing.
wiki.staff: A long stick usually for casting magic or fighting.
wiki.gun: A weapon that fires projectiles or bullets though a barrel by way of explosive propellant.
wiki.rifle: A long firearm designed to be fired from the shoulder, with a barrel that has a helical pattern of grooves ("rifling") cut into the barrel walls. The rifling causes the speeding bullet to spin, giving it more stability and penetrating power.
wiki.handgun: A short-barrelled firearm designed to be used with one hand or two hands and for shooting at short-ranged targets, while be more concealable to be holstered than a rifle or a submachine gun.
wiki.cup: A drinking vessel. This includes mugs, drinking glasses, Japanese-style sakazuki (sake cups), and anything else used to drink from.
wiki.mug: A tall cylindrical cup with a handle, used for drinking hot or cold beverages such as coffee, hot chocolate, or beer.
wiki.bottle: A typically glass or plastic container with a narrow neck and opening made to store liquids and drinks.
wiki.bell: A hollow metal musical instrument, that emits a metallic tone when struck.
wiki.candy: A confection that features sugar as the main ingredient. They are eaten casually, often with fingers, as a snack between meals. Candies come in numerous colors and varieties and have a long history in popular culture. Outside the United States, it is referred to as "sweets" or "confectioneries."
wiki.cake: A baked dessert made from a dough or thick batter usually containing flour and sugar and often shortening, eggs, and a raising agent. They're often covered in either icing or frosting and decorated with embroidery, figures, flowers, or other toppings.
wiki.lollipop: Hard candy mounted on a stick. The most common type are small spheres, while others are flat and circular.
wiki.popsicle: A frozen, flavored, ice-based snack on a popsicle stick. Also known as an ice pop, ice lolly, ice block, ice drop, ice gola, or ice candy.
wiki.strawberry: Juicy red fruit with tiny seeds.
wiki.ice cream: A frozen dessert usually made from dairy products, such as milk and cream, and often combined with fruits or other ingredients and flavors. Ice cream can come in scoops or as soft serve.
wiki.chocolate: Chocolate comprises a number of raw and processed foods that are produced from the seed of the tropical cacao tree.
wiki.apple: A fruit with red, yellow, or green skin and sweet to tart crisp whitish flesh.
wiki.red apple: A fruit with red, yellow, or green skin and sweet to tart crisp whitish flesh.
wiki.bread: Food made from a dough of flour, and baked in an oven.
wiki.donut: A donut (also spelled "doughnut") is a small, fried pastry typically glazed with sugar, chocolate, or other frostings. It often contains sweet fillings such as cream, jelly, or custard.
wiki.cookie: A small, flat-baked treat made from sweetened dough.
wiki.coffee: A hot drink that is made by filtering hot water through ground coffee beans, popular for its aroma and concentrated dose of caffeine. Use this tag when coffee itself (ordinarily a black or dark brown liquid) is visible in an image.
wiki.beer: A type of alcohol that is made by the brewing and fermentation of starches and is flavored by hops. Can be served in a bottle, can, mug, or a large beer glass.
wiki.onigiri: A snack of Japanese rice formed into triangle or oval shapes and often wrapped in nori (seaweed) (edible seaweed). May also refer to yaki onigiri, which are grilled.
wiki.bubble tea: Bubble tea (also known as "pearl milk tea", "tapioca tea", "boba tea", or simply "boba") is a type of tea-based drink invented in Taiwan. It consists of a mixture of tea, milk, or other flavorings, plus small black tapioca balls ("boba") that float at the bottom of the drink.
wiki.basket: A container used to hold or carry things. Some baskets may have a lid. Traditional wicker baskets are woven from natural fibers, while modern baskets are typically made of plastic or wire mesh.
wiki.key: A device used to open locks.
wiki.playing card: A card used to play traditional card games, such as poker, blackjack (game), solitaire, etc. Playing cards are also sometimes used in magic tricks.
wiki.scissors: Scissors are hand-operated cutting instruments. They consist of a pair of metal blades that is connected in such a way that the sharpened edges slide against each other. Scissors are used for cutting various thin materials, such as paper, cardboard, metal foil, thin plastic, cloth, rope and wire.
wiki.surfboard: A long narrow board used in surfing.
wiki.skateboard: A short narrow board with two small wheels fixed to the bottom of either end, on which a person can ride in a standing or crouching position, propelling themselves by occasionally pushing one foot against the ground.
wiki.dumbbell: A piece of equipment used in weight training and weightlifting. A short metal bar with weights on both ends. Designed to be lifted with one hand.
wiki.blanket: A large piece of woolen or similar material used as a bed covering or other covering for warmth. Most kotatsu are covered by a blanket to trap heat underneath.
wiki.glowing: An object or character that is radiating with light.
wiki.electricity: An electrical discharge generated by a character, weapon, or object.
wiki.lightning: An atmospheric discharge of electricity accompanied by thunder, which typically occurs during thunderstorms.
wiki.aura: The visible expulsion of inner energy. Usually associated with martial arts, the use of superpowers, or perhaps comedically, such as when expressing anger.
wiki.snowflakes: A flake of snow, especially a feathery ice crystal, typically displaying delicate sixfold symmetry.
wiki.ripples: Concentric, circular patterns of small waves caused by something impacting water or other fluids.
wiki.rainbow: An arc of spectral colors—often seen in the sky—caused by refection of the sun's rays.
wiki.magic circle: A circle made of magic, usually containing various writings or shapes (such as pentagrams or hexagrams), often drawn on the ground or cast in the air.
wiki.sparks: A small fiery particle thrown off from a fire, alight in ashes, or produced by striking together two hard surfaces such as stone or metal. It can be seen from pyrotechnics such as sparklers and from metalworking.
wiki.embers: The glowing things seen in the fire or that float up from a fire. Similar to light particles coming from something burning.
wiki.blue fire: Blue fire. Usually an indication of supernatural fire.
wiki.glitch: Visual artifacts reminiscent of the long gone analog days, and malfunctioning technology, such as blocky corruption and visual distortion. For actual glitches in games, use gameplay glitch.
wiki.shooting star: An object burning up on atmospheric entry, seen from far away as a streak of light in the sky. If the object appears as a fireball or is recognizable as a lump of rock or debris, use the meteor tag instead.
wiki.glowstick: A stick-shaped chemical light, usually called a "Cyalume".
wiki.penlight (glowstick): A hand-held light source used in concerts similar to a glowstick. Unlike a glowstick, penlights are battery-powered as opposed to being chemically-activated. As such, penlights often have a longer handle area where the battery is stored.
wiki.diffraction spikes: Multiple spikes of light radiating outwards from a bright source of light, such as the sun. Similar to a lens flare.
wiki.caustics: Patterns of light projected onto a surface by light rays reflected off or refracted through another object. These can be seen on underwater surfaces, when light passes through materials like water, glass, and the like.
wiki.floating clothes: Clothing that is blowing in the wind, floating in midair, or otherwise not being held down by gravity.
wiki.anger vein: A symbol used to represent anger or annoyance. It consists of three or four curved lines in a cross shape, representing a bulging vein or artery, like so: 💢.
wiki.clear sky: A sky that is nearly or completely devoid of clouds, regardless of the time of the day.
wiki.underlighting: When the source of lighting in a picture comes from beneath the subject. Often used to create a spooky or menacing atmosphere.
wiki.two side up: A hairstyle in which two locks of hair are tied up on both sides of the head while the back of the hair hangs normally. The amount of hair tied up doesn't matter, only that the back of the hair falls down loosely.
wiki.one side up: A hair style in which a portion of hair is tied up on one side, while the rest hangs normally. The amount of hair tied up doesn't matter, only that the untied hair falls down loosely.
wiki.double-parted bangs: Bangs that are distinctly parted or swept in two different spots, usually on the left and right side of the hair.
wiki.crossed bangs: Strands of bangs that overlap each other in a cross formation over the forehead.
wiki.spiked hair: A hairstyle in which the hair is formed into spikes. This hairstyle is largely seen on male characters from Shōnen manga and anime, though it is sometimes seen on female characters as well.
wiki.short twintails: Twintails that are short, around shoulder length or less.
wiki.side braid: A single braid hanging on the side of the face, anywhere other than in front of the ears. If it's in front of the ear, it's a single braided sidelock instead.
wiki.twin drills: Drill hair that is tied into two curled locks of hair, like twintails. Stereotypically associated with ojou-sama characters.
wiki.hair rings: A hairstyle where the hair is shaped into circular loops or rings, such as the Chinese feixianji (hairstyle) hairstyle.
wiki.hair behind ear: When a character's ear is used to keep some of their hair off of their face.
wiki.black eyes: A character with black colored eyes.
wiki.bright pupils: Pupils of the eyes that are lighter than the surrounding iris color.
wiki.white pupils: For when the pupils of a character are white instead of the normal black.
wiki.multicolored eyes: Eyes with more than one color in the same eye.
wiki.one eye covered: A character has one eye completely covered. Do not tag if the eye is still visible through hair.
wiki.v-shaped eyebrows: Eyebrows that are slanted inwards, forming a V shape. Often used to indicate a sense of mischievousness or smugness, or alternatively anger or annoyance.
wiki.upper teeth only: When only the upper teeth are drawn in the mouth.
wiki.wavy mouth: A mouth that consists of a wavy line or a wavy outline. This can indicate the character is scared, sad, nervous, or embarrassed.
wiki.shaded face: When the upper face or eyes are shadowed without a tangible light source.
wiki.flying sweatdrops: Sweatdrops that appear to be flying off a person's body, physics be damned. Often used to indicate nervousness or embarrassment.
wiki.light blush: A blush that is very faint.
wiki.skin fang: A skin-colored fang that is drawn as part of the outline of the mouth as opposed to being a separate, white protruding tooth.
wiki.fingernails: Fingernails that are noticeable in the image, i.e. the fingers aren't simply stubs.
wiki.black nails: Fingernails or toenails that are colored black.
wiki.blue nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored blue.
wiki.stomach: The frontal abdomen, specifically the area around the navel and above the groin.
wiki.colored skin: Skin that is any color that would be unnatural for a normal human. Often seen on fantasy races, furries, demon girls, demon boys, aliens, zombies, and other not-entirely-human characters.
wiki.hand up: When a single hand is raised to the upper torso or higher. When both hands are raised, use hands up.
wiki.hands up: When both hands are raised to the upper torso or higher. When a single hand is raised, use hand up.
wiki.outstretched arms: When both arms are stretched out, away from the body. They may be spread to the front, the sides, or above the head.
wiki.arm behind head: A single hand or arm held behind one's own head. If both arms are behind the head, use arms behind head instead.
wiki.clenched hand: A single clenched hand, in which all five fingers are brought very close together at the palm; the thumb is brought either over or within the other four fingers.
wiki.bare arms: When a character's arms are bare and not covered by any clothing. This includes from at least the upper arms to the wrists.
wiki.bare legs: When a character's legs are bare, not covered by pants, long skirts or dresses, thighhighs, or pantyhose.
wiki.cat ears: A character who has, or wears as a fashion accessory, cat ears (nekomimi) on their head.
wiki.rabbit ears: A character with rabbit-like ears, such as a rabbit girl or a Playboy bunny.
wiki.horse ears: A character who has, or wears as an accessory, the elongated and tall ears of a horse.
wiki.fox ears: When a character has fox-like animal ears. These are typically long, pointy, and lighter than wolf ears.
wiki.wolf ears: For when a character has wolf-like ears.
wiki.dog ears: A character who has, or wears as a fashion accessory, dog ears (on their head). Also known as Inumimi.
wiki.animal ear fluff: A distinct soft-looking fuzz that protrudes from the inside of animal ears. It is usually white in colouration, often resembling tufts of cotton, but can also take the form of swept fur that is faded in color.
wiki.cat tail: A long furry cat-like tail seen on cat girls and cat boys.
wiki.fox tail: When a character has a fox-like tail.
wiki.horse tail: A character that has the tail of a horse.
wiki.demon tail: A tail with a barbed or spade (shape)-shaped tip often seen on demons or demon girls.
wiki.rabbit tail: A character with a rabbit-like tail.
wiki.multiple tails: A character with more than one tail. A common example of this would be kyuubi (nine-tailed fox) type characters.
wiki.feathered wings: Wings that are covered by feathers.
wiki.bat wings: The wings of a bat (animal), typically associated with demons.
wiki.fairy wings: The wings of a fairy. Extremely diverse and can range from insect-like designs to those resembling specific shapes.
wiki.head wings: Wings that are attached to the head. A common feature on demon girls, but other creatures may have them, such as bird girls.
wiki.claws: Long pointed nails on the paws of an animal, or a person with animal-like claws.
wiki.mechanical arms: An android, cyborg, or other human-like character with mechanical arms instead of human arms.
wiki.horse girl: A human girl with horse features, such as horse ears or a horse tail.
wiki.fairy: A legendary creature, usually depicted as a mini person with translucent insect-like fairy wings, although this is not strictly necessary.
wiki.cyborg: An organism that is made up of both cybernetic and organic components. In anime, this generally refers to humans that have been altered to be partially robotic, with prosthetic limbs or other cybernetic enhancements.
wiki.sleeveless: A shirt, dress, or other top with a neck but without sleeves, often revealing bare arms.
wiki.striped clothes: A piece of clothing with a striped pattern. Stripes are typically wide, equally-sized bands of alternating colors.
wiki.clothing cutout: An intentional hole or opening in a piece of clothing designed to expose part of the body. For example, a cleavage cutout is a hole in the chest that exposes the breasts, while a navel cutout is a hole in the stomach that exposes the navel.
wiki.puffy short sleeves: Puffy sleeves that are also short.
wiki.puffy long sleeves: Long sleeves that loosely puff out along their entire length.
wiki.sleeves past wrists: Sleeves that reach past the wrists.
wiki.juliet sleeves: Long sleeves with a puffy shoulder, inspired by fashions of the Italian Renaissance and named after Juliet from Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.
wiki.strapless: A shirt, dress, or other top that doesn't have any straps, neck, or sleeves. The shoulders, neck, and usually the arms are left bare.
wiki.plaid clothes: Clothing featuring a plaid print. Plaid is a pattern made up of many perpendicular vertical and horizontal lines of two or more colors.
wiki.floral print: When there are flowers printed on any article of clothing. They can be abstract or realistic.
wiki.frilled sleeves: Sleeves, detached or otherwise, that end in frills.
wiki.ribbon trim: A ribbon threaded through slits in the edges of an article of clothing, usually recognizable as a dotted line along the edge of the clothes.
wiki.ribbon-trimmed clothes: A ribbon threaded through slits in the edges of an article of clothing, usually recognizable as a dotted line along the edge of the clothes.
wiki.lace trim: Any article of clothing that has lace trimmed around its edges.
wiki.high collar: A shirt or jacket collar that stands up high and straight instead of being folded down.
wiki.layered sleeves: When a character is wearing multiple layers of sleeves.
wiki.formal clothes: A scene characterised by characters wearing formal clothes such as suits, dress shirts, gowns, evening gowns, cocktail dresses, waistcoat, pants, and dress shoes.
wiki.fur collar: A collar or detached collar that is constructed entirely of fur. If the collar is only trimmed in fur, use fur-trimmed collar. The choker alternative is fur choker.
wiki.highleg: A garment with a high legline, where the leg opening or straps rest high on the hips.
wiki.frilled skirt: A skirt with frills. Don't confuse with frilled dress.
wiki.hooded jacket: A zip-up jacket with an attached hood. Often features a drawstring for the hood.
wiki.robe: A loose-fitting outer garment, covering the body completely, that usually reaches the knees or feet.
wiki.hood down: Wearing a hooded garment without the hood on the head (as opposed to wearing the hood up).
wiki.single thighhigh: A character wearing a thighhigh on only one leg.
wiki.ankle boots: Short boots that reach just past the ankle.
wiki.armored boots: Boots made out of metal, typically a part of armor.
wiki.bow: A knot generally featuring two loops and two loose ends. Bows will be seen on clothing (many serafuku have them), in hair, on panties and other lingerie, on shoes (shoelaces are usually tied in a bow), and pretty much any place that there is something that might be tied.
wiki.ribbon: A ribbon is a thin band of flexible material, typically cloth but also plastic or sometimes metal, used primarily for binding and tying. Often seen used in elaborate clothing and hair, and generally longer than it is wide.
wiki.hair bow: A bow tied into the hair in some way. It will often be used by girls with long hair to tie back a ponytail or twintails. It will also be used to keep loose hair back without a tail or as simple decoration.
wiki.hat bow: A bow attached to a hat, often appears alongside a hat ribbon.
wiki.hat ribbon: One or more ribbons tied to a hat of any type, often appears alongside a hat bow.
wiki.neckerchief: A piece of cloth worn around the neck and tied at the ends, leaving two separate tails resembling neckties.
wiki.headband: A strap worn across the forehead, such as a sweatband, a strip of cloth worn during martial arts or athletic events, or a piece of ninja armor (however apocryphal).
wiki.scrunchie: A fabric-covered elastic hair tie. Usually worn in the hair, but may also be worn on the wrist, arm or ankle as a fashion accessory.
wiki.hair bobbles: A hair ornament consisting of an elastic band with one or more bobbles, frequently two large balls, used to tie the hair. It works by wrapping the band around a bundle of hair and securing it by stretching the band over and around the bobble.
wiki.tassel: An ornament found at the end of a rope or cord composed of a tuft of hanging threads. Can be found in a variety of styles, and is most often found on the drawstrings of curtains, but can be found on clothing as well.
wiki.wristband: A band worn around the wrist. The material they're made of depends on the purpose of the band.
wiki.gauntlets: Metal armored gloves or mitts that protect the hands and wrists of a combatant.
wiki.pauldrons: A form of shoulder armor, usually made from metal. They often protect the armpit as well as the back and chest, either separately or as part of a large breastplate.
wiki.star hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairclip shaped like a star (symbol).
wiki.feather hair ornament: Feathers worn in the hair as a hair ornament. If the feathers are actually growing out of the head of a bird girl, use feather hair instead.
wiki.hair bell: A bell worn as a hair ornament.
wiki.santa hat: A floppy pointed red fur-trimmed hat with a white pom pom (clothes) at the point.
wiki.mask on head: When a character has a mask on their head, but not worn over the face.
wiki.fox mask: A mask in the shape of a fox's face.
wiki.holding phone: Holding a phone in the hands. If it is nestled between the cheek and shoulder, use cradling phone instead.
wiki.holding fan: Someone is holding a hand fan.
wiki.pantyshot: Non-deliberate view of a pair of panties underneath a skirt or dress. Should not be used for deliberate acts, like a skirt being actively lifted by the wearer or by other people nearby.
wiki.wind lift: Where the wind lifts up something, such as clothing (skirt, dress, etc.), parasols or other miscellaneous articles. May be used with dress lift, shirt lift and skirt lift as appropriate.
wiki.green background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly green color. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.purple background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly purple or lavender color. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.star (symbol): A symbol representing a star. The five-pointed (★) star is the most common example, but is not the only shape.
wiki.summer: A scene set in summer, or with a clear summer theme.
wiki.flower: The blossom of a tree or plant; the colorful part of a plant that produces seeds or fruits.
wiki.leaf: A flat green appendage that grows on a plant or tree.
wiki.feathers: The characteristic plumage of birds. Commonly seen on bird wings and angel wings, or used as decorations in hair and clothes.
wiki.chain: A series of metal loops linked together.
wiki.black hat: A hat that is colored black.
wiki.white hat: A hat that is colored white.
wiki.red hat: A hat that is colored red.
wiki.blue hat: A hat that is colored blue.
wiki.brown hat: A hat that is colored brown.
wiki.green hat: A hat that is colored green.
wiki.mini hat: A hat that's smaller in size than usual. It doesn't fit around the character's head, so it's more used as a hair ornament. It's often worn tilted to one side.
wiki.tokin hat: A small box-shaped Japanese hat, associated with tengu.
wiki.mob cap: A mob cap or mob-cap is a round, gathered, or pleated cloth (usually linen) hat consisting of a caul to cover the hair, a frilled or ruffled brim, and (often) a ribbon band to keep it in place (modern versions use elastic).
wiki.peaked cap: A hat worn by many military forces and uniformed civilian organizations, such as police agencies.
wiki.visor cap: A type of crownless "hat", consisting of an eyeshade and something to fasten it to the head, such as a rim or an elastic strap.
wiki.beanie: A tight-fitting knitted hat traditionally designed to keep the head warm in cold weather. Common styles of wear include hugging the head with a turned-up cuff, or leaving a few inches of the top unstretched to flop or stick up.
wiki.headdress: An ornamental covering or band for the head, especially one worn on ceremonial occasions.
wiki.missing headwear: A character who normally wears some form of headwear (a hat, a bandana, a helmet, etc.) is shown without their headwear.
wiki.unworn headwear: Any piece of headwear (a hat, a baseball cap, a helmet, a maid headdress, etc.) is present in the image, but nobody is wearing it.
wiki.unworn hat: A hat that currently isn't being worn.
wiki.hat ornament: An accessory worn on a hat for decoration or ornamentation purposes.
wiki.hat flower: A flower attached to a hat or cap as a hat ornament.
wiki.x hair ornament: A hair ornament in the shape of an X.
wiki.hair tubes: Cylindrical hair ornaments that separate strands of hair from the main body of hair. Often seen on Nagi (kannagi), Feena_(grandia), and Hakurei Reimu.
wiki.pom pom (clothes): A fluffy ball made of fiberous material such as cotton. It can be worn on any piece of clothing, whether it is headwear, body clothing or shoes.
wiki.spikes: Sharp, pointy protrusions on a surface or object used for stabbing those who come too close to them. Mainly used for defense.
wiki.jingle bell: A spherical metal ball containing an unattached clapper with only a small slit opening, for higher pitched ringing. This bell is largely associated with holidays like Christmas or seen on the collars of domestic pets.
wiki.fake tail: When an object is used to simulate having a tail. These may be glued directly on the skin, sewn onto clothes or attached to sex objects.
wiki.ear covers: Decorations most commonly worn over pointy ears or animal ears, ranging from full covers to partial attachments.
wiki.headset: A set of headphones with an attached microphone. The headphones are usually small and sometimes cover only one ear, while the microphone is usually a small flexible tube that sits in front of the mouth.
wiki.epaulettes: Ornamental shoulder pads seen on many military uniforms. Typically seen in soldiers from the Imperial era (1600s - 1800s). Frequently depicted with a fringe trim. The term is derived from a French word for "little shoulders".
wiki.armlet: A decorative band, usually made of precious metal and may feature precious gems, that is worn for ornament around the upper arm.
wiki.bridal gauntlets: A type of tight-fitting handwear, usually elbow-length, that is secured by a ring or loop around one finger, rather than having separate finger-holes. Commonly worn as part of a wedding dress, hence the name.
wiki.white sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored white. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.black sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored black. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.blue sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored blue. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.red sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored red. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.purple sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored purple. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.pink sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored pink. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.green sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored green. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.grey sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored grey. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.ribbon-trimmed sleeves: Sleeves (usually detached) with ribbon trim around the edges. Usually recognizable as a dotted line along the sleeve cuffs.
wiki.sleeve cuffs: A sleeve cuff is a layer of fabric at the lower edge of the sleeve of a garment (shirt, coat, jacket, etc.) at the wrist. Use this tag for cuffs distinct and notable from the garment they are a part of. If the cuffs are plain and non-distinct this tag is not warranted.
wiki.fur-trimmed sleeves: Sleeves with fur trim at the ends.
wiki.striped sleeves: A set of shirt sleeves, detached sleeves that have stripes running along them. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently patterned from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.torn sleeves: A pair of sleeves that have been torn, regardless if it's inherently designed as such or something happened to rip them apart.
wiki.short over long sleeves: A short-sleeved garment worn over a long-sleeved garment to get a nice color (or pattern) combo. This type of layering was largely popular in the 1990s.
wiki.single sleeve: A shirt, jacket, or similar garment with only one sleeve.
wiki.single detached sleeve: When only a single detached sleeve is being worn.
wiki.sleeves pushed up: When a character wears his or her clothes with both or one of its sleeves pushed or pulled up. This can be either to cool themselves off, to prevent the sleeves from getting dirty or wet or getting in the way of what they are doing, or simply due to the characters' taste in fashion.
wiki.gold trim: An article of clothing or armor that has a golden trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.lapels: The folded flaps of cloth on the front of a blazer, suit jacket, or coat. Usually they are formed by folding over the front edges of the jacket or coat and sewing them to the collar, an extra piece of fabric around the back of the neck.
wiki.legwear garter: Garters worn on the leg to hold up socks or thighhighs via straps. Also known as sock suspenders.
wiki.sleeves past elbows: Sleeves that are roughly mid-forearm length. Long enough to cover the elbow, but not the wrist.
