wiki.sleeves past fingers: Sleeves that reach past the fingers, covering the entire hand. Even longer than sleeves past wrists.
wiki.puffy detached sleeves: A pair of puffy sleeves that are not attached to the upper garment the character is wearing, but are rather detached and worn on the upper arm.
wiki.hakama short skirt: A shortened hakama skirt. Length can be anywhere from knee length to microskirt length. At miniskirt length, it can be used to exploit the "zettai ryouiki" effect.
wiki.shorts under skirt: A pair of shorts worn beneath a skirt or dress.
wiki.bubble skirt: A type of skirt where the hem is tucked back under at the bottom to create a 'bubble' effect. Popular in the 1950s, 1980s, and the mid-2000s. Good examples are Cure Muse, Medicine Melancholy, Hata no Kokoro and Kaname Madoka's dresses.
wiki.overskirt: A skirt that is intended to be worn on top of another skirt, shorts or pants, often has an open front.
wiki.capri pants: Pants that end somewhere below the knee to slightly above the ankle. This does not include pants that are rolled up to some point along the shins.
wiki.toeless legwear: Legwear that covers the foot while leaving the toes uncovered.
wiki.mismatched legwear: Thighhighs, socks, or pantyhose that have two different colors or patterns. For differences in length, use uneven legwear.
wiki.uneven legwear: Legwear of different lengths. For differences in color or pattern, see mismatched legwear.
wiki.stirrup legwear: Legwear (normally thighhighs, but more rarely socks) that have a stirrup around the sole of the foot, leaving both the toes and heel uncovered. Referred to in Japanese as trenckers.
wiki.bobby socks: A type of sock that was especially fashionable in the 1940s and 1950s. Commonly ankle length, the cuff of the sock is lengthened and then flipped downward, either flaring out over the ankle bone or fitting snugly onto it.
wiki.bow legwear: Legwear that is decorated with a bow.
wiki.pantyhose under shorts: When pantyhose are worn beneath a pair of shorts.
wiki.no legwear: A character who normally wears pantyhose or thighhighs is shown without their legwear, with bare legs instead.
wiki.rubber boots: Waterproof boots made from rubber, to protect the wearer's feet and legs from rain, water, mud or snow.
wiki.fur-trimmed coat: A coat with fur trim along the edges.
wiki.long coat: A coat that hangs lower than the knees.
wiki.winter coat: A heavy coat worn in winter. Winter coats can come in a variety of styles, but are often padded or fur-trimmed for extra warmth.
wiki.letterman jacket: A sports jacket commonly worn by American high school/college students and athletes. Traditionally, the wearing of such a jacket indicates that the student has met a specified level of participation or performance on a varsity team.
wiki.sleeveless jacket: A jacket without sleeves. The easiest way to differentiate a sleeveless jacket from a vest is that the jacket comes with a collar and are often more protective against weather, vests also seldom come with a hood compared to sleeveless jackets. Amano Hina is commonly depicted wearing a hooded, sleeveless jacket.
wiki.suit jacket: A jacket worn with a suit. Oftentimes features lapels.
wiki.side cape: A cape that is fastened around the neck and worn off only one shoulder.
wiki.open robe: A robe that is unfastened, revealing the body underneath.
wiki.short kimono: A kimono where the hemline stops at or above the knee.
wiki.sleeveless kimono: A kimono that does not have attached sleeves.
wiki.armored dress: A dress adorned with combat armor, or an entire suit of armor stylized into a dress.
wiki.track suit: Trousers and jacket used in sports. Including track jacket and track pants.
wiki.skirt suit: A woman's suit of clothing consisting of a skirt (usually a pencil skirt) and a matching or coordinating coat or jacket.
wiki.plugsuit (evangelion): A distinct kind of mecha pilot suit worn by the mecha pilots in Neon Genesis Evangelion.
wiki.dress flower: At least one flower that is used to decorate a dress or skirt.
wiki.striped shirt: A shirt with two or more different colored stripes that become a pattern. The white and black variation is the most famous one, often used for robbers (when horizontal), and referees (when vertical).
wiki.off-shoulder shirt: A shoulder-less shirt with a wide low-cut neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders. The sleeves must be attached to the shirt.
wiki.sleeveless turtleneck: A sleeveless garment with a turtleneck. Often a turtleneck sweater.
wiki.aran sweater: A bulky woolen sweater with cable knit patterns (often of various patterns), traditionally cream-colored or off-white.
wiki.sleeveless sweater: A sweater that is sleeveless. It may have detached sleeves.
wiki.transparent background: An image with a transparent background.
wiki.brown background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly brown color. Also applies to Tan or Beige backgrounds. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.orange background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly orange color. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.aqua background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly aqua, cyan or turquoise color. For shades of blue that are close to ultramarine, navy or darker, use blue background. For shades of baby blue or sky blue, use blue background. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.grid background: A typically single-color background formed into a square grid by a series of thin lines.
wiki.dark background: A background that is dark but not solid black unless the subject is dimly lit.
wiki.photo background: When a real-world photo (medium) is used as the background for a drawing.
wiki.checkered background: A completely or predominantly checkered background, consisting of exactly two, evenly spaced colors. The most common pairing is black and white.
wiki.greyscale with colored background: A common composition where a greyscale subject is on a colored background, usually also a simple background.
wiki.heart background: One or more hearts are in the background.
wiki.argyle background: A background that completely or predominantly consists of diamonds.
wiki.patterned background: A background that has a repeating pattern on it.
wiki.star (sky): Cosmic bodies that can be seen during the night sky.
wiki.fire: A state, process, or instance of combustion in which fuel or other material is ignited and combined with oxygen, giving off light, heat, and flame.
wiki.sun: The star_(sky) that is central to our solar system.
wiki.shade: Under the shade, including headwear casting a shadow over the eyes. Doesn't include people's shadows.
wiki.dark: Poorly lit surroundings which obscure some details.
wiki.stage lights: Bright lights that are shone upon the stage and/or audience during any type of performance art such as singing, dancing, concerts, plays and such.
wiki.nature: When scenery with wild plants is clearly visible.
wiki.house: A building for residential dwelling, typically for a single family.
wiki.^ ^: Closed eyes with an upward peak. Almost always paired with a smile, but iconic enough to be indicative of one even when the mouth is hidden or missing.
wiki.> <: Eyes tightly closed in a literal >_< shape. This usually indicates extreme happiness, but it can also be used to indicate pain, embarrassment, or sadness.
wiki.@ @: Swirling eyes which represent embarrassment, confusion, dizziness, being hypnotized, being overwhelmed, or being knocked unconscious. More rare, a character who is drunk or angry can be shown with these eyes.
wiki.+ +: When a character's eyes light up in excitement, with yellow four-pointed sparkles in the center of their eyes replacing their pupils. Sparkles may also appear around their head.
wiki.= =: A smiley that is used to represent a face with squinted eyes (mouth shape is often varied).
wiki.o o: Eyes drawn as solid white circles with a thick black rim. Used to express surprise.
wiki.;o: Having one eye closed with the open mouth in a round :o shape. Common when winking, wincing, or yawning.
wiki.black sclera: The sclera, also known as the "white of the eye," is the fibrous, protective, outer layer of the eye.
wiki.yellow sclera: Where the sclera—the white part of the eye—is yellow.
wiki.white eyes: A character with white colored eyes.
wiki.two-tone eyes: Eyes that have two distinct colors in the same eye, but aren't close enough in shade to be called gradient eyes.
wiki.blank eyes: Eyes that are missing both the irises and pupils; only the sclera are present. Often used to show surprise, gloom (expression), or a state of death. Sometimes used to show a character of overwhelming power.
wiki.one-eyed: A character with only one eye. This includes both characters who have lost an eye and those who naturally have only one (such as a cyclops).
wiki.extra eyes: A character with more than the standard two eyes. The extra eyes must be part of the body to count, so no disembodied linked eyes like Komeiji Satori, or other disembodied eyes.
wiki.no eyes: When a character is drawn without eyes, or the eyes are hidden in the shadow of a shaded face. Often done for dramatic effect.
wiki.gradient eyes: Eyes having a smooth and gradual color shift, commonly seen on Shenhe (Genshin Impact) or March 7th (Honkai: Star Rail).
wiki.third eye: A person with a third eye on their head or body instead of the usual two. The extra eye does not have to be located on the head, but it should still be part of their body.
wiki.solid oval eyes: Eyes drawn as solid black ovals. Often seen in chibi characters.
wiki.eyeball: An organ that detects light, and gives visual stimulation.
wiki.red pupils: Pupils that are red instead of the standard black.
wiki.pink pupils: A character has pink pupils in their eyes instead of the standard black.
wiki.no pupils: Eyes that lack pupils. The iris is a solid color.
wiki.constricted pupils: Pupils that are noticeably smaller than usual, sometimes almost dot-like. Can indicate extreme fear, surprise, craziness, or simply a reflex from exposure to bright light.
wiki.cross-shaped pupils: When a character's pupils are shaped like a cross symbol, + or †.
wiki.diamond-shaped pupils: Use when a character's pupils are shaped like a diamond_(shape). → diamond (shape), star-shaped pupils, cross-shaped pupils, diamond in eye, symbol-shaped pupils
wiki.mismatched pupils: When the pupils are different in each eye, or have different colors, often seen with symbol-shaped pupils.
wiki.sanpaku: Eyes that noticeably show the whites around most of the iris during a state of rest. Can also indicate anger, exhaustion, or a dangerous demeanor. Sometimes referred to as "Dead fish eyes" among Western speakers.
wiki.hair over eyes: Long bangs that hang over both eyes. For the asymmetric version of this where only one eye is covered, use hair over one eye.
wiki.looking afar: When a character is looking off into the distance. Can be used with looking ahead when the character's gaze is seen to be directed straight ahead, but not at a subject that is visible in the image close-by (ie. an object or person in the same room).
wiki.colored tips: A type of multicolored hair where the hair is abruptly colored differently at the very ends, as if it was dipped in dye. Also known as dip dye or tip dyeing.
wiki.alternate hair color: A character whose hair is drawn in a color different than the usual color.
wiki.roots (hair): A type of multicolored hair where the hair at the top of the head (the roots) is a different color from the rest. This is typically visible where the hair parts on the head.
wiki.short hair with long locks: A hairstyle consisting of short hair in back with long sidelocks in front of or behind the ears, with the locks at least shoulder length.
wiki.low-tied long hair: Long or very long hair that has been tied down low, at the middle or the bottom of the hair.
wiki.short ponytail: A ponytail that is atypically short, often stopping above the wearer's neckline.
wiki.half up braid: A braid that loops around the back of the head, in the same manner as a half updo.
wiki.crown braid: A braid which wraps around the top of the head in the way a hairband or a crown would, as the name suggests.
wiki.low twin braids: Twin braids where the braids are tied low, below ear-level, instead of near the scalp. Usually this means the back part of the hair is in braids, rather than the sidelocks.
wiki.cone hair bun: Cone-shaped hair buns. This includes both double buns and single hair buns.
wiki.braided bun: A hair bun made out of a twisted braid.
wiki.topknot: A hairstyle in which some or all of one's hair is tied up in a tuft atop the head.
wiki.multi-tied hair: A ponytail, twintails, sidelocks, etc. tied in more than one vertical spot, almost resembling a line of sausages.
wiki.huge ahoge: Ridiculously large ahoge. Should be at least as tall or as long as the character's head to qualify. Often seen on Inu Sakuya (nejikirio), Miki, Me-tan, and Nyaruko.
wiki.heart ahoge: A type of expressive hair where a character's ahoge bends to form a heart, often to indicate that the owner is happy or in love. Distinct from heart antenna hair, which is made from multiple ahoge.
wiki.single sidelock: A single sidelock in front of one ear.
wiki.single hair intake: Like hair intakes, but instead of two scoops of hair, there's only one.
wiki.alternate hairstyle: A character drawn with a hairstyle different from any of their usual styles. This also includes changes in hair length.
wiki.blunt ends: A hairstyle where the tips of a character's hair are cut in a sharp straight line. Not to be confused with blunt bangs, although they are sometimes seen together.
wiki.curtained hair: When a fringe of hair briefly arches upward then hangs back down while the bangs part to the side.
wiki.flipped hair: Hair that is curled outward at the ends.
wiki.asymmetrical hair: Hair with a significant element of asymmetry in its styling.
wiki.big hair: Hair that is unusually thick or voluminous.
wiki.convenient hair: Long hair positioned so that it covers the nipples or the crotch, often as a form of convenient censoring.
wiki.hair pulled back: Hair that is pulled back, usually into a ponytail or hair bun, revealing their forehead. The hair is usually tight against the scalp.
wiki.hair down: An alternate hairstyle where a character who normally styled their hair "up" in place is drawn with their hair let "down" kempt.
wiki.hair up: An alternate hairstyle in which a character wears their hair up when they would normally wear it down. This include hair buns, folded ponytails, and more.
wiki.asymmetrical bangs: A hairstyle where half the bangs is worn combed back / short, and the other half long resulting in a distinctly asymmetrical hairstyle.
wiki.long bangs: Unusually long bangs that go past the eyes, at least. Will likely also include hair over eyes, hair over one eye, or hair between eyes.
wiki.braided bangs: Braided front hair or braid positioned at the forehead. The braided part doesn't need to be all of the bangs.
wiki.center-flap bangs: Bangs that are cut or combed back at the temples leaving a distinctive "flap" over the forehead. The bangs must be parted/cut/combed on both sides.
wiki.outstretched arm: When one arm is stretched out, away from the body. If both arms are stretched out, use outstretched arms instead.
wiki.arm at side: When one arm is at rest on its side of the body, while the other arm is doing something else such as being spread out, reaching out, on the hip, behind the head, and so on.
wiki.knee up: A single knee is raised into the air. For kneeling on only one knee, use on one knee.
wiki.arm behind back: A single arm held behind the back, either by the subject or another character, in sexual and non-sexual situations. If the arm is bound in some way see bondage.
wiki.legs apart: Legs that are apart while in the standing position.
wiki.knees together feet apart: Legs that are held together at the knees but not at the feet.
wiki.fighting stance: A stance that is taken to intimidate an opponent, and to ready one's self for any sort of attack.
wiki.hugging object: Hugging an inanimate object such as a book, doll, pillow, stuffed animal, etc.
wiki.yokozuwari: A Japanese term for a feminine informal sitting posture, on the knees as in seiza but with the legs folded out to one side. If the legs are folded out to either side, it's wariza.
wiki.split: A gymnastic position wherein the legs slide into opposite directions away from the body, causing them to be either parallel or perpendicular to the ground.
wiki.pigeon-toed: A stance where the toes point inwards when standing, sitting, or walking. Also called in-toeing, often caused by genu valgum, or "knock-knee".
wiki.midair: A character fully in the air, not touching the ground or any support.
wiki.twisted torso: A character's torso turned to a high degree, sometimes even beyond human limits. This can occasionally result in bad anatomy.
wiki.crossed ankles: Having one's legs crossed at the ankles, as opposed to crossed legs or watson cross, where the legs are crossed at calf-, knee-, or thigh-level.
wiki.knees to chest: When the knees are pulled in so that they are close to the chest.
wiki.toe scrunch: When the toes are pushed or curled down relative to the foot. The opposite of toes up.
wiki.head back: Tilting the head backwards so that the area under the chin is visible to the viewer.
wiki.flexing: When a character is striking a pose or moving in a way that shows off their muscles.
wiki.plantar flexion: Flexing the foot in a downward direction, away from the shin. The opposite of dorsiflexion.
wiki.head rest: Resting one's head or chin on something, such as on the hands, another person, or an object.
wiki.own hands clasped: A character clasping their own hands together, often with interlocked fingers.
wiki.v over eye: Holding a v-shaped hand sign over the eye, with the eye between the fingers.
wiki.rabbit pose: A pose where a character holds both their hands up to the top of their head, fingers together and palm flat, to mimic the appearance of rabbit ears. Most commonly done as a cute or sexy gesture. Prominently featured in the memetic Caramelldansen (meme) video and derivative images.
wiki.watson cross: Standing with the legs crossed at the calf-, knee-, or thigh-level.
wiki.sitting on person: When a character is sitting on someone else.
wiki.locked arms: One arm hooked around another's, so that inner elbows (cubital fossa) are directly touching each other.
wiki.cropped torso: When a character is only drawn from the waist up, and their legs or lower body appear to be cut off inside the image.
wiki.cropped legs: When a character's legs appear cut off inside the image, i.e. there is a visible gap between the end of the legs and the edge of the image.
wiki.cropped shoulders: When an image fades out around the neck or upper shoulder area (above the chest), such that the character's torso isn't drawn.
wiki.out of frame: When one or more character (identifiable or not) is only visually present in an image so far as to show a limited number of details.
wiki.foot out of frame: Like full body, except one of the character's feet are outside of the image. Part of the character's shins may be cropped out as well, but their knees should be within the image. Compare with cowboy shot.
wiki.eyes out of frame: A subset of head out of frame in which the eyes are cropped out of frame, but the lower portion of the head remains visible.
wiki.fake screenshot: When the picture is drawn to look like a screenshot from a video game, user interface, a software menu, a TV series and so on.
wiki.fake phone screenshot: A fake screenshot of a cellphone screen.
wiki.viewfinder: A camera frame. A set of lines in the corners of an image, used by a camera to frame a person being photographed.
wiki.foot focus: When a character's foot or feet are the main subject or focus of the image, especially when the feet are close-up to the camera or being presented to the viewer.
wiki.hip focus: When a character's hips are especially noticeable, or otherwise a major focus of the image. Do not use this tag simply because a character's hips are visible.
wiki.animal focus: One or more animals are the subject of the image, e.g., cat animal focus, rabbit animal focus.
wiki.food focus: A post with a major focus on one or more items of food or drink.
wiki.vehicle focus: A post where a vehicle is the primary focus of the image.
wiki.:d: A wide, open-mouthed smile or grin. If the character also has one eye closed, it's also ;D.
wiki.:o: An open mouth in a round circular shape. The mouth can be all the way open, or only slightly parted. Can express surprise, amazement, or awe.
wiki.:3: The facial expression where the mouth looks like a 3 on its side. Likened to the face of a cat, and commonly used to portray innocence, cuteness, or mischievousness in an anime or manga.
wiki.;d: A wide, open-mouthed smile or grin like :D, but with one eye closed.
wiki.:p: Sticking the tongue out along the bottom of a closed mouth.
wiki.:<: A closed mouth frown shaped like an upside-down V. Often indicates mild annoyance.
wiki.:q: Running the tongue along the upper lip in a "licking lips" sort of way.
wiki.:t: Pouting with one cheek puffed out, forming a :T shape with the lips. Typically representative of jealousy or indignation, or unamusement.
wiki.;): Smiling with a closed mouth while having one eye closed.
wiki.:>: A closed mouth smile shaped like the letter V.
wiki.:/: The mouth is closed with single corner of mouth dropped, so the mouth looks like a slash (/).
wiki.>:): A smile with v-shaped eyebrows and a closed mouth. May indicate smugness, confidence, or may even be an evil smile.
wiki.d:: An unhappy, displeased, or distressed face with a flat-bottomed open mouth. The opposite of :D.
wiki.split mouth: An artistic style where the line representing a character's mouth isn't fully connected. The mouth is usually closed but can also be open.
wiki.triangle mouth: An open mouth in the shape of a triangle.
wiki.chestnut mouth: An open mouth shaped like a chestnut: pointed up at the top and rounded at the bottom or pointed down at the bottom and rounded at the top. Often includes round upper teeth. Similar to a rounded triangle mouth.
wiki.sideways mouth: A quirk of manga/anime art where a character's face is viewed from the side, yet their mouth is drawn on the side of their face, rather than on the front.
wiki.no mouth: A character drawn without a mouth. It is usually done for deformation.
wiki.wince: An expression of involuntarily flinching or shrinking away, as from pain, distress, surprise, or cringing from extreme embarrassment. May be accompanied by one eye closed or clenched teeth.
wiki.glaring: A look of anger or disgust, often accompanied by a frown, with the eyes narrowed.
wiki.faceless: A character with a defined head whose facial features (mainly the eyes) don't appear, either because they're hidden, covered, in shadow, or not drawn at all.
wiki.dot nose: A nose that is drawn as a small dot. In anime, it's extremely common to draw the nose as a simple dot or line rather than as a full nose.
wiki.nose: A character drawn with a more prominent nose than is typical for anime or manga styles. The opposite extreme is a dot nose or even no nose.
wiki.no nose: When a character has no discernible nose projecting from their face.
wiki.raised eyebrows: When a character's eyebrows are elevated from the usual resting position. Often indicates surprise.
wiki.raised inner eyebrows: Eyebrows with only the inner ends raised, forming a kind of peak shape. Often an expression of sadness, smugness, embarrassment, pain, relief (expression) or fear.
wiki.eyebrows hidden by hair: When a character's eyebrows are fully or partially hidden behind bangs or any form of hair. They should not be showing through, as if the hair is translucent, in any way.
wiki.^^^: A pointed, crown-like symbol drawn next to a character's head to represent surprise, understanding or shock. Depending on the style, it may have the appearance of a crown, a series of hash marks or some variation thereof. Usually there are three points, though there is some variation.
wiki.full-face blush: A blush that covers the whole face, rather than just the cheeks. Occurs when a character is really embarrassed.
wiki.multiple expressions: Several variations of the same character doing different facial expressions and emotions. This is often in the form of an expression chart, or in a series of small portraits in a character profile showing a character's different expressions.
wiki.mouth drool: When drooling is represented as a dip in the outline of the mouth, rather than as actual saliva leaking from the mouth.
wiki.food: A source of edible nourishment for humans, animals, and plants.
wiki.fruit: The edible part of a seed-bearing plant, typically sweet (or sour) and edible raw. Common fruits include apples, bananas, grapes, lemons, oranges, and strawberries.
wiki.plant: Vegetation, such as trees, grass, or bushes, that grows in the ground and needs sunlight and water for growth. Plants often have flowers, leaves, or branches, and reproduce using seeds.
wiki.drink: A beverage or liquid intended for human consumption. Common types of drinks include water, milk, juice, coffee, tea, alcohol, and soda.
wiki.alcohol: Any drink that contains ethanol, a psychoactive drug that has a depressant effect. Drinking too much of it can cause drunkenness. Possible health effects can include the increased risk for cancer, alcoholism, liver cirrhosis, depression, ataxia, and many more.
wiki.plate: A flat serving platter for many different types of non-liquid dishes. Usually but not always circular.
wiki.tray: A small platform used for placing and carrying items - such as food and dishes.
wiki.bowl: A hollow serving dish for soup, cereal, ramen, rice, salad and many other meals.
wiki.spoon: A piece of cutlery that has a rounded end to assist in eating liquid or non-solid foods such as cereal, soup, and porridge. It's also used for stirring one ingredient into another, or mixing together a flavoring/sweetener into one's beverage.
wiki.fork: A pronged utensil made to gouge through the desired food item for consumption. Long noodles like ramen and spaghetti can also be twirled around a fork.
wiki.can: A cylindrical container for drinks such as soda and coffee, and canned food such as fish_(food) and vegetables.
wiki.drinking straw: A plastic tube used to transfer a liquid to one's mouth.
wiki.pocky: A long, thin, chocolate-covered snack popular in Japan similar to a biscotti. There are other Pocky flavors that are shipped throughout the world. In Europe it is available under the name Mikado.
wiki.carrot: A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, orange, sweet root.
wiki.pumpkin: A vegetable in the squash family, popularly associated with Halloween, where people carve faces on pumpkins to create Jack-o'-lanterns.
wiki.tea: A brewed drink made from the buds and young leaves of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis). This also includes herbal teas made from other plants.
wiki.burger: A food item consisting of at least a patty of ground meat sandwiched between two halves of a bread bun. May also include condiments, cheese, an extra patty or bread, and/or certain vegetables. A popular fast food item.
wiki.mushroom: A common type of fungus. They range from edible to lethally poisonous.
wiki.cherry: A small fruit, usually red, black or yellow, with a smooth hard seed and a short hard stem.
wiki.watermelon: A large, roundish melon with a hard, green-striped rind and sweet, watery and red (occasionally yellowish) pulp. A tasty summer treat.
wiki.peach: A soft-skinned fruit with a yellowish-orange outside and yellow or whitish flesh.
wiki.noodles: A staple food made from dough (whether made with bread wheat, durum wheat, buckwheat, rice, etc. and may or may not include eggs), which is prepared in various ways depending on the type of noodle (one example being rolled flat and made into long thin strips), then boiled in water until done (whether al dente or not).
wiki.dango: Japanese dumplings made of rice flour, often served skewered and with green tea.
wiki.orange (fruit): Round yellow to orange fruit of any of citrus trees.
wiki.heart-shaped chocolate: A piece of chocolate in the shape of a heart, often reserved for Valentine's Day.
wiki.macaron: A colorful sweet pastry traditionally made in France, they are sandwich-like with cream between the middle of the two halves.
wiki.parfait: A dessert, similar to a sundae, made up of layers of ice cream or cream and fruit and/or fruit gelatin, served in a tall parfait glass that makes all layers visible.
wiki.sandwich: A food item consisting of two pieces of bread with one or more fillings between them. Different from a burger because sandwiches don't have a beef patty between them, instead using cold cut meats or warmed slices of meat.
wiki.pancake: Flatbread prepared from a sweet batter that is cooked on a hot griddle or in a frying pan. Also known as hotcakes.
wiki.cupcake: A type of smaller sized cake that is baked in a tray with cup-sized indentations, then cooled and decorated with frosting and other decorations.
wiki.wagashi: Traditional Japanese confectionery that is often served with tea, especially the types made of mochi, adzuki bean, red bean paste, and fruits.
wiki.rice: A cereal grain and the staple food of over half of the world's population. The seed of the plant Oryza sativa, of the grass family (Poaceae).
wiki.ice cream cone: An edible wafer- or waffle-like cone-shaped pastry to place ice cream on so it can be eaten without a bowl or spoon.
wiki.coffee mug: A type of mug designed to hold hot beverages, most commonly coffee. Typically cylindrical in shape, with a handle, and made of ceramic or glass. Designed to be thick enough to allow holding a hot beverage in the hands.
wiki.beer mug: A tall mug, usually made of glass or sometimes metal, used to serve beer.
wiki.birthday cake: A decorated cake that celebrates one's birthday. Typically written with the words, "Happy Birthday" followed by the person's name. May include candle(s) to give the person being celebrated a chance to make a wish upon blowing then out.
wiki.bouquet: A collection of flowers in a creative arrangement.
wiki.hibiscus: A flowering plant in the Malvaceae family. Arguably the most popular tropical flower.
wiki.lily (flower): A flower of the genus Lilium in the family Liliaceae.
wiki.spider lily: A poisonous flower (species Lycoris radiata) commonly associated with death.
wiki.hydrangea: A genus of flowering plants of the Hydrangeaceae family, native to southern and eastern Asia. Most species are shrubs, but some are small trees. Commonly called hortensia.
wiki.rose petals: Petals that originate from a rose.
wiki.happy birthday: Use this tag when the phrase "Happy Birthday" (or variations such as "HBD") is written in the image in English or other languages. → Birthday, english text, Congratulations
wiki.birthday: A celebration of the anniversary of the day someone was born. In addition to birthday parties, it is common for people to receive gifts. There is also cake to eat at the gathering.
wiki.anniversary: A day that celebrates a past event, usually associated with marriages. On Danbooru, anniversaries are associated with how long a series has been around, with most milestones marked annually for new series, then about 5 or 10 year increments afterwards.
wiki.valentine: Posts related to Valentine's Day, especially in the making and giving of gifts and chocolates.
wiki.happy new year: The message "Happy New Year" written somewhere, in English or any other language.
wiki.merry christmas: The message "Merry Christmas" written somewhere, in English or any other language.
wiki.jack-o'-lantern: A vegetable lantern commonly carved from a pumpkin, typically as a Halloween decoration. The pumpkin has a face or image carved into it, and the insides are usually scooped out so that a candle can be placed inside to illuminate the carving.
wiki.airplane: An aircraft that flies by using fixed wings to generate lift.
wiki.scarlet devil mansion: The setting of stages 4-6 and the extra stage of the Touhou game Embodiment of Scarlet Devil.
wiki.cable: A coated cable or cord used to conduct electricity or carry signals for electrical equipment or science fiction-related machinery. This includes, but is not limited to, audio cables, power cables, video cables, data cables, and coated wires.
wiki.stool: A seat without a back or arm rests.
wiki.cushion: As opposed to a pillow, a cushion's use is not limited for sleeping but can be found on beds, couches, chairs, floors etc. Can be for decoration or comfort.
wiki.armchair: A chair with side supports for a person's arms.
wiki.ball: A round object, especially one that is often used in sports and games, such as soccer or basketball (sport).
wiki.beachball: A big inflatable ball and very light weight. Colorful, can have images print on them (e.g. A watermelon print)
wiki.cosmetics: Cosmetics are products or objects used to apply makeup, such as makeup palettes, lipstick tubes, nail polish bottles, etc.
wiki.hand mirror: A small handheld mirror with a handle.
wiki.world war ii: The Second World War (abbreviated "WWII" or "WW2") was a major worldwide war that was first set off by the Japanese invasion of Manchuria and then officially began when Nazi Germany attacked Poland on September 1st of 1939 and ended after Japan surrendered on August 15th of 1945.
wiki.explosion: A large cloud of fire, gas, dirt, and shrapnel that is caused by some sort of explosive such as a grenade, nuclear weapon, or a chemical reaction that went horribly wrong.
wiki.burning: An object being consumed by fire.
wiki.pyrokinesis: Fire that is generated/controlled by magical, telekinetic, or otherwise supernatural ability.
wiki.purple fire: Fire that is predominately purple in color.
wiki.breathing fire: When a character or creature exhales fire to create a trail of fiery breath. In comical works, characters are sometimes depicted as breathing fire and suffering in response to eating extremely spicy food.
wiki.fireflies: The visual effect of numerous glowing balls or streaks of light, used to represent fireflies.
wiki.aerial fireworks: A type of firework that consists of large, often colorful explosions in the night sky (when it's most visible). Often used during festivals and celebrations.
wiki.hitodama: A spirit in the shape of a glowing ball with a flowing tail resembling blue or white fire.
wiki.darkness: Elemental or magically altered darkness (a lack of light). Usually swirling around in dark clouds or forming inky tendrils.
wiki.tree shade: Shadows cast by trees, commonly used to escape the sun on hot days. Often results in dappled sunlight.
wiki.flashlight: An artificial, handheld light source that relies on a battery or some other way of storing energy (magic et al).
wiki.window shadow: Shadows cast by a window frame, or by window blinds or shutters in the window. Typically involves sunlight or moonlight.
wiki.colored shadow: A shadow in any color that isn't black. If it's black, just use shadow alone.
wiki.crescent moon: The waxing (☽) or waning (☾) crescent moon.
wiki.gradient sky: A sky with a smooth gradient between different colors.
wiki.purple sky: A body of sky that is colored purple.
wiki.white skin: Skin colored pure white, like milk or snow, having no pigment at all. The opposite of black skin.
wiki.grey skin: Skin that is colored grey. Not to be confused with pale skin.
wiki.red skin: Skin that is colored red. Often associated with demon girls or red onis.
wiki.yellow skin: Skin that is colored yellow. Not to be confused with pale skin.
wiki.orange skin: Skin that is colored orange. Should not be confused with a tan or dark skin.
wiki.metal skin: Some or all of of a character's skin is made of metal. A common feature of many cyborgs and androids that aren't designed to look convincingly human, but it may also be the case with non-mechanical beings such as certain golems or elementals.
wiki.multicolored skin: When a character has two or more distinct colors making up their skin. All skin colors present should be tagged, if possible.
wiki.two-tone skin: A colored skin that is two-toned (comprised of only two colors). Normally occurring colors like tan, bruises etc don't apply.
wiki.colored extremities: Hands, feet, or limbs that are differently colored than the rest of the body. This can be a gradual fade or a sharp transition, and it can be anything from only the fingers or toes, or extending up to the arms or legs.
wiki.patchwork skin: For when a character has skin that has been stitched together in multiple places, possibly from multiple sources.
wiki.albino: Complete or partial absence of skin and hair pigment due to an absence of melanin. Albinos appear very pale-skinned and typically have red eyes because while there is no pigment in the irises, the blood vessels can still be seen.
wiki.body fur: Fur on a character's body that isn't part of their clothing. Commonly found on furry (anthropomorphic) characters.
wiki.scales: Scaly skin, as seen on reptiles and fish. Scales are small rigid plates that grow out of an animals' skin to provide protection.
wiki.sticker on face: A sticker on a character's face.
wiki.lipstick mark on face: A lipstick mark left on the face, typically by a kiss.
wiki.mouse ears: A character who has, or wears as a fashion accessory, mouse ears on their head.
wiki.cow ears: A character who has, or wears as a fashion accessory, cow/bull ears (ushimimi) on their head.
wiki.tiger ears: Animal ears based off of a tiger, seen on a human rather than the actual animal.
wiki.raccoon ears: Ears that mimic raccoon or tanuki ears.
wiki.bear ears: Small round ears found on bears.
wiki.lion ears: Animal ears based off of a lion, seen on a human rather than the actual animal.
wiki.deer ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a deer.
wiki.sheep ears: Animal ears on a human character resembling those of a sheep.
wiki.goat ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a goat.
wiki.squirrel ears: Use when a character has ears of a squirrel. → squirrel, squirrel tail
wiki.chipmunk ears: Use when a character has ears of a squirrel. → squirrel, squirrel tail
wiki.bat ears: Animal ears based off of a bat (animal), seen on a human rather than the actual animal.
wiki.panda ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a panda.
wiki.extra ears: A character possessing both human ears and animal ears.
wiki.floppy ears: Long animal ears that hang limp against the head, unable to perk up on their own. The ears must be completely limp, or almost completely limp, unless they are being lifted by another source, like the wind or someone's hand.
wiki.kemonomimi mode: When a character who doesn't normally have animal-like features (such as ears or a tail) is drawn with animal ears or a tail.
wiki.long pointy ears: Pointy ears that are significantly longer than usual.
wiki.tail wagging: When an animal or a person moves their tail back and forth, such as to signal a warning or to display emotions, often shown as afterimages. Note that dogs wag their tails when they're happy, and cats wag their tails when they're angry.
wiki.mechanical wings: Wings made of metal. Hydraulic parts, screws, cables and glowing LEDs are a plus, as are clockwork parts like gears.
wiki.energy wings: Wings made of some form of energy, typically magical. Often detached, but can also be attached to the character.
wiki.crystal wings: Wings made of or featuring crystals in their design. Might be entirely formed from crystals, or might be wings similar to Flandre Scarlet's - thin wings with floating crystals instead of feathers.
wiki.bird wings: Wings resembling those of a bird.
wiki.low wings: Wings that are positioned lower than the usual shoulder area, such as near the hips.
wiki.detached wings: Wings that are floating detached from the body.
wiki.asymmetrical wings: Wings that have differences in size, shape, or color.
wiki.transparent wings: Wings that are partially or completely see-through. Not to be confused with doodled-on wings, in which use drawn wings instead.
wiki.single wing: When a character has only one wing. It may either not exist or be cut off.
wiki.multiple wings: Having more than one pair of wings.
wiki.monster: A big, scary fictional animal or non-human beast.
wiki.dragon: A mythical large, flying reptilian creature.
wiki.eastern dragon: A dragon with the serpent-like features seen in East Asian mythology.
wiki.western dragon: A dragon with wings, a long neck, tail, and four legs. Usually walks on all fours but is sometimes seen standing or even walking on only two. A staple of any fantasy series.
wiki.angel: Spiritual beings usually viewed as messengers and guardians to living beings, typically originated from heaven.
wiki.giant: A giant person, humanoid being, or monster. Giants are typically much larger than their surroundings, often even larger than buildings.
wiki.jiangshi: A Chinese undead. Often called a "Chinese hopping vampire". They drain people's life energy, hence being called "vampires", although they are more similar in concept to Western zombies.
wiki.slime (creature): A common enemy in many RPGs. Usually represented as a blob, possibly with eyes. Sometimes, it is depicted with a core, which functions similarly to the brain/heart.
wiki.unicorn: A mythological white horse with a single horn on its forehead.
wiki.tengu: A Japanese traditional youkai, thought to take the forms of birds of prey and traditionally depicted with human, monkey, and bird characteristics. They are associated with conceitedness and trickery.
wiki.centauroid: A centaur-like creature that has a human or human-like torso where the head of the animal would be.
wiki.robot: An autonomous mechanical or electronic machine.
wiki.nekomata: A traditional youkai in the form of a cat or cat-like spirit with two tails or a single forked tail. A nekomata can be humanoid or a cat.
wiki.kyuubi: A fox (or fox girl/fox boy) with nine tails.
wiki.lips: The fleshy folds that surround the opening of the mouth.
wiki.long fingernails: Fingernails that protrude past one's fingertips, at least 1 cm beyond.
wiki.toenail polish: Nail polish worn on the toenails.
wiki.pink lips: Pink mouth lips. Usually because they have pink lipstick applied to them.
wiki.purple lips: Lipstick that is colored purple. It can either be worn on a character's lips, or in its original cosmetic form in a lipstick tube.
wiki.black lips: Someone is wearing black-colored lipstick on their lips.
wiki.blue lips: A character or person depicted has blue colored lips.
wiki.green lips: A character or person depicted has green colored lips.
wiki.facepaint: Painted marks or symbols on a person's face. Often used by tribal cultures.
wiki.hikimayu: A traditional Japanese cosmetic practice of shaving off the eyebrows and painting on new ones, often resulting in distinctive short eyebrows placed high on the forehead.
wiki.runny makeup: Mascara, eyeliner, lipstick or other makeup which has started to smudge due to tears, rain, etc.
wiki.aegyo sal: The small, puffy fatty deposits under the eyes that are considered attractive in East Asia, often associated with a youthful and cute appearance.
wiki.blinking: A character blinking both eyes in an animated image.
wiki.traditional nun: A traditional nun's habit, specifically a traditional Christian style (Catholic, Orthodox, etc), as opposed to the fetishized, non-traditional nun habits typically seen in anime and fanart.
wiki.cowboy western: The Western film genre. These are depictions of the Wild West and its characters.
wiki.spacesuit: A suit worn by astronauts while in space.
wiki.half gloves: A type of short glove that doesn't cover the wrists.
wiki.paw gloves: Gloves that are modeled after animal paws. Often worn with animal ears, or the entire animal costume.
wiki.fur-trimmed gloves: Gloves with fur trim along the edge.
wiki.single glove: A glove worn on only one hand.
wiki.mittens: A covering for the hand that encases the thumb separately and the four fingers together. Often worn with winter clothes during cold weather.
wiki.partially fingerless gloves: A variant of fingerless gloves where some of the fingers on the gloves are missing while others are present.
wiki.black choker: A choker that is colored black.
wiki.white choker: A choker that is colored white.
wiki.red choker: A choker that is colored red.
wiki.frilled choker: A choker that has frills trimming its edges.
wiki.ribbon choker: A type of choker where a ribbon is tied around the neck and wrapped into a bow, either in front or at the nape of the neck. A ribbon choker can't be worn over clothes, it must have direct skin contact.
wiki.red necktie: A necktie that is colored red.
wiki.green necktie: A necktie that is colored green.
wiki.red bowtie: A bowtie that is colored red.
wiki.blue bowtie: A bowtie that is colored blue.
wiki.pink bowtie: A bowtie that is colored pink.
wiki.white bowtie: A bowtie that is colored white.
wiki.red neckerchief: A neckerchief that is colored red.
wiki.yellow neckerchief: A neckerchief that is colored yellow.
wiki.blue neckerchief: A neckerchief that is colored blue.
wiki.black neckerchief: A neckerchief that is colored black.
wiki.yellow ascot: A yellow ascot, most commonly worn by Hakurei Reimu.
wiki.white ascot: An ascot that is colored white.
wiki.red ascot: An ascot that is colored red.
wiki.red scarf: A scarf that is colored red.
wiki.neck bell: A collar decorated with one or more bells. They are usually used on small domestic pets (such as cats) as a way of listening to their location if they wander too far from their home.
wiki.lanyard: A rope, cord, or other fastener worn around the neck, wrist or belt and attached to an item that you do not wish to drop or have taken from you (e.g. binoculars, a camera, ID card, weapon or whistle). Not to be confused with eyewear strap.
wiki.pearl necklace: A necklace made out of pearls lined together on a string and clipped at the nape of the wearer's neck. If the size of the beads are bigger, it becomes bead necklace instead.
wiki.chain necklace: A necklace composed of chain links. This tag applies whenever the links can be visually distinguished or when the material (e.g. gold) would demand that it be made in this fashion.
wiki.magatama: A curved, comma-shaped bead or gem, usually worn on a necklace. Sometimes worn for its religious meaning, sometimes just as a fashion accessory.
wiki.round eyewear: Eyewear that have pronounced circular or oval lenses.
wiki.semi-rimless eyewear: Eyewear (glasses, monocles, or sunglasses) that only have rims only over the top or under the bottom of the lens, leaving the other half rimless. Also possible are eyewear that have rims only along the sides, leaving both the top and bottom rimless.
wiki.red-framed eyewear: Any eyewear (glasses, monocle or sunglasses) with red-colored frames.
wiki.under-rim eyewear: Semi-rimless eyewear that has a broad lower frame and a rimless upper frame; the opposite of over-rim eyewear.
wiki.rimless eyewear: Eyewear (glasses, monocles, or sunglasses) that have no rims around the lenses. Sometimes they may have a thin outline tracing the outside of the lens, which still counts as rimless eyewear.
wiki.monocle: A single framed lens used to correct the vision of just one eye. It is usually attached to a monocle chain with the other end attached to one's clothing to avoid loss.
wiki.bespectacled: When a character who normally does not wear glasses, wears glasses. Sunglasses do not count.
wiki.earphones: Small speakers that are worn directly in or on to the ears, instead of being attached to a headband like headphones.
wiki.head wreath: A wreath made of flowers, foliage, or any ornamental work, worn on top of the head.
wiki.print shirt: A shirt that has printing on either the front, the back, or both sides.
wiki.print bow: A bow that has any kind of stylized print designs on it.
wiki.egasumi: The traditional Japanese style of drawing clouds as long horizontal oval-ish shapes linked together.
wiki.seigaiha: A traditional Japanese pattern of stylized waves.
wiki.yagasuri: A traditional Japanese pattern of tiled arrow (projectile)-feathers which is usually monochrome.
wiki.sakuramon: The sakuramon (桜紋) is a stylized depiction of a five-petaled cherry blossom. The tips of the petals often feature an indent.
wiki.kikkoumon: A hexagon pattern used in traditional Japanese art. Literally "tortoise shell design". Kikkoumon are used in family crests as well as repeated in different combinations to form various patterns.
wiki.asa no ha (pattern): Asa no ha (lit. "hemp leaves") is a traditional Japanese pattern resembling overlapping six-pointed stars (hexagram), referred to in mathematics as the triakis triangular tiling.
wiki.meandros: A decorative border, formed by a continuous line that meanders in a repeating fashion.
wiki.pinstripe pattern: A clothing pattern consisting of very thin vertical lines (the "pins") with wide gaps between them.
wiki.camouflage: A protective coloration or pattern meant to disguise animals, people, or military equipment through deception and reducing visibility against a particular environment, backdrop or terrain.
wiki.tiger print: Clothing with a tiger-like print (i.e. black marks of varying length on orange or yellow). Oni often wear tigerskin loincloths as a reference to how they were rumored to come from Northern (ushitora) Japan.
wiki.flag print: Clothing or an item that is designed with printings resembling a nation's flag.
wiki.food print: An article of clothing or an object made out of fabric that has a printed design of food.
