wiki.plaid: A pattern made up of many perpendicular vertical and horizontal lines of two or more colors. Compared to the uniformity of a checkered pattern, plaid features distinct irregularity in the width of its lines, and the colors used may not be divided neatly by said lines.
wiki.argyle: A pattern that is made of plaid diamonds in a diagonal orientation.
wiki.serval print: Deprecated tag. See Serval (Kemono Friends) instead.
wiki.multicolored stripes: Clothes that have stripes with 3 or more colors.
wiki.colored stripes: Stripes of only two colors, with neither stripe being white. For more than two colors, use multicolored stripes.
wiki.wolf tail: When a character has a wolf-like tail.
wiki.fish tail: A character with a fish-like tail growing from the base of their spine.
wiki.cow horns: The horns of a cow or a bull.
wiki.sheep horns: The horns of a sheep or ram. Sheep horns are often curled.
wiki.furry: An anthropomorphic animal; a character based on an animal but with human traits. Body fur, feathers, or scales are common. Anthro animal characters without body fur, like birds, bugs, and reptiles, still count as furry.
wiki.raccoon girl: Girls with intrinsic raccoon or tanuki (raccoon-dog) features. Confusion between the two species means that characters who are meant to be tanuki girls have features more pertaining to the raccoon (like a ringed tail) and vice versa.
wiki.mouse girl: Girls with intrinsic mouse (animal) features, such as mouse ears and mouse tail.
wiki.mouse: See mouse (animal) for the animal or computer mouse for the computer peripheral.
wiki.arthropod girl: A girl with insectoid qualities such as antennae, wings, and any sort of appendages related to a particular bug or other arthropod.
wiki.creature: Any fictional, tiny, nondescript creature that isn't monstrous, especially not "big and scary". Think of the small helper characters from magical girl shows, or the mascot for a company or series.
wiki.doll joints: A living character with doll-like bodily joints. Usually seen on Rozen Maiden-style dolls, although there are other examples such as various kinds of cyborgs or androids.
wiki.butterfly wings: Having wings like those of a butterfly.
wiki.ambiguous gender: When a character's gender cannot be determined due to their face or body not being clearly visible. For example, a character wearing full armor or bulky clothing with no obvious male or female traits, or someone who's mostly out of frame, viewed from a great distance, or hidden in shadow.
wiki.dark persona: An alternate, "darker", and possibly evil version of a character, with an alternate costume and/or other distinguishing characteristics.
wiki.pilot suit: See mecha pilot suit for mecha pilots, flight suit for Air Force pilots, and pilot uniform for commercial pilots.
wiki.ahoge wag: When a character wags their ahoge in a manner similar to a dog wagging its tail.
wiki.armpit hair peek: When armpit hair is slightly visible under arms. Usually in arm at side poses, sometimes with a slight backward rotation of the arm(s).
wiki.artificial eye: For mechanical eyes, see mechanical eyes. For glass eyes, see glass eye.
wiki.beach chair: Ambiguous tag referring to either of two types of outdoor furniture. Use lounge chair or deck chair instead.
wiki.brushing own hair: Brushing one's own hair (as opposed to another character's).
wiki.bulging eyes: Eyes bulging from a character's eye sockets, possibly from surprise, awe, or being squeezed.
wiki.crystal hair: Hair that is made of crystal-like gems or has crystalline texture.
wiki.detached ahoge: An ahoge which is drawn separated from the head, as opposite of the normal ahoge.
wiki.detached hair: Hair that is part of a character's design, but not attached to their head, instead somehow magically floating in the air or otherwise detached from their body. Commonly seen on Akaza Akari or hololive's Aki Rosenthal.
wiki.drying hair: Drying one's own or someone else's wet hair, typically with a towel or hair dryer.
wiki.extra pupils: Eyes that have more than one pupil per eyeball.
wiki.eye black: Eye black is a grease or strip applied under the eyes to reduce glare, although studies have not conclusively proven its effectiveness. It is often used by American football, baseball, softball, and lacrosse players to mitigate the effects of bright sunlight or stadium floodlights.
wiki.eyes in shadow: When the eyes of someone or something can be seen while the surrounding area is in total darkness. Think "glowing eyes peering out of a cave" level of darkness.
wiki.feet on chair: Resting one or both feet on the same chair one is sitting on.
wiki.folded hair: Ambiguous tag. → folded ponytail, folded side ponytail, folded twintails, folded braid, folded untied hair, hair rings
wiki.hair over face: Hair that drapes down over a character's face, obscuring the majority of their face. If the hair only covers one eye or both eyes, it's hair over one eye or hair over eyes instead.
wiki.heart hair: Hair in the shape of a heart.
wiki.liquid hair: Hair is made of liquid. Bottle Miku is an example.
wiki.living hair: Hair that seems to take on a life of its own, especially in snake hair-like fashion.
wiki.long eyebrows: Eyebrows that extend past the forehead.
wiki.mismatched eyelashes: Use this tag for when eyelashes have a mismatched color from the hair, or when two eyelashes have different colors (particularly in cases of heterochromia, or weird instances like post #639207 or post #672047). → heterochromia, colored eyelashes
wiki.mole above eye: A mole located just above the eye.
wiki.severed hair: When hair is present as an object detached from anyone's head.
wiki.solid eyes: Eyes that are a solid color, without distinct iris, pupil, and sclera. If the color is white, see blank eyes instead.
wiki.starry hair: When a character has star (sky)s in their hair, normally on the inner part.
wiki.unworn hairband: When a character that normally wears a hairband has it removed, but it's still in the image.
wiki.wide oval eyes: Eyes drawn as horizontal solid white ovals. Used to express surprise. Most often used with chibi art.
wiki.alternate wings: When a character who canonically has wings is depicted with a different or uncommon depiction of their wings.
wiki.bat girl: Girls with intrinsic bat (animal) features, such as bat ears and bat wings.
wiki.bear girl: A girl with bear like traits.
wiki.bee girl: A monster girl with bee attributes such as a stinger, antennae, large insect-like eyes, and translucent bee wings.
wiki.bird girl: A girl with bird-like features, such as bird wings, bird ears, feathers, or a bird tail, but without monster girl features, such as winged arms, bird legs, or talons.
wiki.cow boy: A male dressed as a cow or with cow-like features. Common features include cow ears, cow horns, a cow tail, cow print clothing, a cowbell, ear tags, and large pectorals.
wiki.dinosaur tail: Use when a character has a tail of a dinosaur.
wiki.drawn ears: Animal ears drawn over a character's face.
wiki.fiery tail: A tail that is, or appears to be, made of fire.
wiki.fiery wings: Wings that are, or appear to be, made of fire.
wiki.forked tail: One tail that splits into two around midway. Espeon is the one of the best examples of this feature.
wiki.frog girl: A girl with frog characteristics, such as a long tongue and webbed hands and feet.
wiki.glowing horns: One or more horns that are glowing.
wiki.glowing wings: When a pair of wings are emitting light, or glowing. For wings without substance, tag energy wings.
wiki.goat girl: A female human, monster or anthropomorphic creature that features goat-like characteristics.
wiki.hugging own tail: A character is hugging their own tail.
wiki.implied extra ears: When an animal-eared character is implied to have hidden human ears.
wiki.large wings: Wings that are exceptional large; as large as the character's body or larger.
wiki.leopard boy: A boy with leopard traits such as leopard ears or a leopard tail.
wiki.leopard ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a leopard.
wiki.leopard tail: Use when a character has a tail of a leopard. → tail, leopard, leopard ears
wiki.lifted by tail: A tail lifting a skirt, dress, or other article of clothing. Not to be confused with tail raised.
wiki.lizard tail: A character with a lizard-like tail.
wiki.long tail: The vast majority of posts under tails are long tails, so this tag is useless.
wiki.monkey boy: A boy with real monkey characteristics, such as monkey ears or a monkey tail.
wiki.moose ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a moose.
wiki.moth girl: A type of arthropod girl that has characteristcs of a moth. They are frequently depicted having a thing for lamps.
wiki.multicolored tail: An animal tail that has two or more distinctive colors present. This must not include greyscale colors like white, grey and black, unless one of those colors is present in a set of three or more colors, like post #2541737.
wiki.no tail: A character who normally has a tail is depicted without it. Often (but not always) an artistic error.
wiki.no wings: When a winged character is depicted without wings. This can be an artistic error (e.g. a character is drawn with wings in all but one panel of a comic) or a stylistic choice by the artist.
wiki.otter tail: Use when a character has a tail of an otter. → tail, otter, otter ears
wiki.owl girl: A bird girl with owl-like features, such as feathers or an owl ears/owl tail.
wiki.penguin tail: Use when a character has a tail of a penguin.
wiki.sheep girl: A girl who has sheep traits, such as sheep horns or sheep ears.
wiki.sheep tail: Use when a character has a tail of a sheep. → tail, sheep, sheep horns, sheep ears
wiki.spider girl: A spider-themed monster girl. Spider girls often have extra eyes or extra arms. If they have spider legs instead of human legs, then they are additionally an arachne.
wiki.squirrel girl: A girl with squirrel-like features, such as squirrel ears or a squirrel tail.
wiki.torn wings: Wings that are torn or damaged in some way.
wiki.weasel girl: A girl with real weasel characteristics, such as weasel ears or a weasel tail.
wiki.weasel tail: A character with a tail of a weasel.
wiki.wing ears: Wings present where are human's ears usually are.
wiki.above clouds: When the point of view is positioned in the sky above the clouds.
wiki.against fourth wall: When a character is pressed up against the fourth wall, that is, the screen between the viewer and the character. Also counts if it's the view from below / the "fourth floor" or "fourth seat".
wiki.alternate muscle size: Ambiguous tag. See one of the following: • fatter than canon • more muscular than canon • thinner than canon
wiki.animal around neck: An animal, either alive or dead/skinned, worn around a character’s neck like a stole as a piece of fashion.
wiki.animal on hand: An animal sitting on a character's hand.
wiki.ankle bow: A bow tied at either one or both of a character's ankles. Often connected to an ankle strap.
wiki.ankle garter: A frilly elastic band worn around the ankle.
wiki.ankleband: A band or strap worn around the ankle.
wiki.aqua halo: A halo that is colored cyan
wiki.arms around waist: One character has both arms around another's waist.
wiki.bad food: Food meant to be tasty, but capable of causing severe illness or is just plain disgusting. An otherwise benevolent character's secret weapon.
wiki.bandaged chest: When bandages are visibly wrapped around a character's chest.
wiki.bandaged fingers: When a character's fingers are wrapped in bandages, but not the hands as well.
wiki.bandaid on head: A bandaid on top of a person's head.
wiki.bandaid on neck: A bandaid on a person's neck.
wiki.barcode: A machine-readable representation of data relating to the object that is attached to it, mostly made up of thick and thin parallel lines that are designed to be unique to every purchasable product.
wiki.baseball: Ambiguous tag. See baseball (sport) for the sport or baseball (object) for the ball itself.
wiki.basketball: Ambiguous tag. → basketball (object), basketball (sport), basketball uniform, basketball jersey
wiki.beach volleyball: A variant of volleyball (sport) played on the beach. Unlike regular volleyball, there are usually only two players on a team.
wiki.beaker: A container for stirring, mixing and heating liquids commonly used in laboratories. Beakers are generally cylindrical in shape, with a flat bottom.
wiki.bear hood: A type of animal hood that features fake bear ears.
wiki.bird on arm: A bird resting on someone's arm.
wiki.black jumpsuit: A jumpsuit that is colored black.
wiki.blood in mouth: Includes a visibly red mouth and/or blood trailing down the corner of the mouth. A character physically coughing blood, however, warrants that tag instead.
wiki.blood on bandages: Bandages that are covered in blood.
wiki.blue brooch: A clasp or pin that typically has a gem attached, often secured to a piece of garment.
wiki.blue jumpsuit: A jumpsuit that is colored blue.
wiki.box tie: Bondage technique where a person's arms are bound behind their back, wrist to elbow.
wiki.broken armor: Any armor that is visibly broken or damaged.
wiki.broken sword: A sword that has its blade broken off the hilt.
wiki.brushing teeth: When a person in the image is brushing their teeth — or, as is perhaps more common nowadays, getting their teeth brushed by someone else.
wiki.cameo: For posts where copyrighted characters appear as inconspicuous background characters or when they appear in various media such as poster (object)s, figures, charm (object)s, cellphone straps, etc.
wiki.cheek rest: Resting the cheek on a surface, most commonly one's own hand.
wiki.chicken leg: The leg of a chicken (food). Also commonly referred to as the "drumstick".
wiki.christmas lights: A string of colorful lights wrapped around Christmas trees and strung around fixtures to produce colored illuminations during the holidays.
wiki.claw foot bathtub: A portable bathtub that has distinct feet at the bottom.
wiki.cloth: A small piece of fabric for a particular purpose, usually related to cleaning.
wiki.cocktail shaker: A device for shaking and mixing alcoholic drinks. Filling the shaker with ice allows the drink to be quickly chilled before serving.
wiki.coffee cup: See either coffee mug or disposable coffee cup.
wiki.coffee table: A low table, typically placed in front of a couch.
wiki.compass: A device that shows the direction of magnetic north.
wiki.contrast: When two differing (most likely visual) aspects of a work clearly contrast with each other, and it appears to have been intentional on the artist's part.(e.g. bright foreground characters, dark background)
wiki.corpse: A dead human body. For the cadaver of an animal, see dead animal.
wiki.cream puff: A puffy pastry filled with flavored cream.
wiki.creature on head: A creature is resting on top of a character's head.
wiki.creature on shoulder: A creature resting on someone's shoulder.
wiki.cupping hands: Pressing one's own hands together to form a "cup". Commonly used to hold liquids, or something small.
wiki.daisy: For the flower see daisy (flower). For the character from Mario (series), see Princess Daisy.
wiki.dark clouds: Clouds that are distinctly dark rather than white or light grey, regardless of what color is used to darken them.
wiki.dark halo: A halo that represents darkness, corruption, evil, or unholiness. Designs vary, but they tend to be dark in color, non-luminous, and spiky or sinister-looking.
wiki.dark room: A room that has no light or very dim lighting.
wiki.diadem: A diadem is a type of crown, specifically an ornamental headband worn usually by women as a badge of royalty.
wiki.digital media player: Ambiguous tag, please use one of the following: • CD player • CD Walkman • MP3 player • Digital Walkman • iPod • Media player interface • Minidisc player
wiki.disembodied head: When a character's head is removed from their neck, but the rest of the body is also present in the image.
wiki.dorsal fin: A flat thin part on the back of many fishes and some marine mammals.
wiki.drill ponytail: A ponytail in drill hair style.
wiki.ear chain: A type of ear piercing consisting of a thin chain connecting 2 different portions of the of the ear, usually going from the upper ear to the earlobe.
wiki.ear scrunchie: A scrunchie worn on the ear.
wiki.ancient egyptian: A post that depicts ancient Egyptian elements, whether they be cultural or otherwise.
wiki.extra mouth: A character having more than one mouth on their body.
wiki.face punch: A punch in the face. May or may not be fatal.
wiki.fake halo: A halo that is supported by a visible rod, as opposed to a "real" halo that floats in midair.
wiki.fake nails: Use a more specific tag, such as: • long fingernails • very long fingernails • nail polish • nail art • unworn fake nails
wiki.fanning face: Using a hand fan, other objects, or just the hands on one's face to cool oneself.
wiki.feet on table: Propping the feet atop a table, desk, or other similar furniture.
wiki.fingers to cheeks: The character is putting multiple fingers to the cheeks.
wiki.fingers to mouth: Placing multiple fingers towards one's own mouth.
wiki.flaming hand: When a burst of fire is engulfing a character's hand or fingers. May be the result of a pyrokinetic using their powers, or someone channeling a tremendous amount of energy to create fire on their hand.
wiki.flashback: The recalling of past events involuntarily. Could stem from outer or inner stimuli; eg: a loud sound, a familiar smell for the former. Thinking about someone could be the latter. If the recollection is voluntary, use remembering.
wiki.food on hand: Food on a person's hand or fingers.
wiki.fourth wall: The imaginary "wall" that separates a piece of fiction from the real-life audience.
wiki.frilled straps: A garment with frilled shoulder straps.
wiki.fruit on head: A fruit on someone's head. Mandarin oranges and apples are common examples.
wiki.full mouth: A mouth full of food that is being eaten, chewed, or swallowed, especially when the mouth is so full that the cheeks bulge.
wiki.fur choker: A choker made entirely out of fur.
wiki.fur cuffs: Wrist or ankle cuffs that are made of fur.
wiki.gesture: A motion of the limbs or body made to express or help express thought or to emphasize speech.
wiki.glass door: A door that is either entirely or partially made out of glass.
wiki.glass table: A table that's comprised of a glass top and legs made out of a supporting material like metal or wood.
wiki.glowing flower: Used when the image depicts a flower that is glowing.
wiki.glowing hand: When a character's hand is emitting light, or glowing.
wiki.glowing tattoo: A tattoo that is emitting glowing light. This light may artistically depicted as a halo around the tattoo or may be reflected by other surfaces.
wiki.golden arms: Arms made out of gold. One of Phosphophyllite (ll)'s most distinctive features.
wiki.gradient skin: Gradient skin is not a significantly taggable concept and has been deprecated in favor of alternate options. • Colored extremities (red hands) • Colored extremities (including feet) • Two-tone skin • Patchwork skin
wiki.green feathers: Feathers that are green. Don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.green fire: Fire that is predominately green in color.
wiki.green jumpsuit: A jumpsuit that is colored green.
wiki.green rose: A type of rose that does not occur in nature. Symbolism for this flower is not widely identified but could be associated with common themes for green, such as fertility and jealousy.
wiki.grey bag: A bag that is colored grey.
wiki.grey cat: A cat that has grey fur (or grey skin, for hairless cats).
wiki.grey cloak: A cloak that is colored grey.
wiki.gun on back: A gun worn on a person's back.
wiki.hand over face: Ambiguous tag. → hand up, arm up, covering face, covering own face, covering another's face, covering own mouth, covering own eyes, covering one eye
wiki.hands in pocket: When both hands are in the same pocket, usually a kangaroo pocket on a hoodie or sweatshirt. The pocket is open on both sides and sits on the lower front section of the shirt.
wiki.happy facial: Images of characters looking happy about being on the receiving end of facials.
wiki.head: See portrait, disembodied head or severed head.
wiki.head on head: Putting one's head or chin on top of another's head. A sign of endearment.
wiki.head steam: Steam billowing out of a character's head, as if their embarrassment, anger or other emotion has reached a boiling point.
wiki.headlight: A powerful light at the front of a motor vehicle or railroad engine.
wiki.holographic interface: A display consisting of a holographic control device projected into space (or otherwise displayed as a free-floating 3D image) for the user to view.
wiki.huge moon: When the moon appears much larger than usual.
wiki.humanoid robot: A robot that has a humanoid shape (bipedal with distinct arms and legs), but cannot pass for a human like an android. The robot should be clearly distinguishable from a human, and it should not appear to have an actual human face.
wiki.invisible: When a character is completely transparent and cannot be seen by either the viewer or another character. Their clothes may or may not be invisible as well.
wiki.jet: See fighter jet or jet airliner.
wiki.kappa: A kappa (河童 (かっぱ), lit. river child) is a type of water sprite found in Japanese mythology. It is famous for its love of cucumbers and also its odd eating habits, such as feeding on hapless victims by sucking out the entrails through the anus; this leads to its other name: shirikodama (anus) vampire.
wiki.knees out of frame: Images where the subject's whole body down to and including the upper legs are in the frame, as are the character's lower legs, but the knees are mostly or entirely outside of it.
wiki.knives between fingers: Holding knives between the fingers, usually in preparation to throw them. Izayoi Sakuya is a frequent practitioner of this.
wiki.leaning on table: A character is leaning on a table. See against table if their arms are on the table, or on table if the character is fully on the table.
wiki.lights: Ambiguous tag. Please tag the specific kind of light, or light source, instead: • sun (sunlight) • moon (moonlight) • fire • fireworks • flashlight • lantern • spotlight • torch • lamp • lamppost • glowstick • stage lights • christmas lights
wiki.looking at food: When a person looks at food.
wiki.loose thighhigh: When a character is wearing thighhighs, and one of them has been loosened or fallen down. This can be a quirk of fashion sense, or mere accident.
wiki.lying on water: A character is lying on a body of water.
wiki.mall: A large indoor shopping center, usually anchored by department stores.
wiki.merchandise: A product based on a media franchise, such as anime, video games or music, especially one displayed or collected by fans of that franchise. Often, though not always, a depiction of actual real world merchandise that exists.
wiki.muffin: A healthier variant of the cupcake baked with bran or wheat instead of flour, and can be mixed with raisins, spices, and/or fruits.
wiki.muffin top: When the belly fat bulges slightly over the top of the clothing waistline. Named after the appearance of a muffin when it has been baked in a muffin tin.
wiki.multiple scars: Having more than one scar, often in different places on the body.
wiki.nail: See either fingernails, toenails or nail (hardware).
wiki.nail polish bottle: A small container that holds the liquid cosmetic product called nail polish.
wiki.neck: Deprecated, see one of the following instead: • neck focus, for posts where the neck is the focus or particularly detailed • nape, for necks viewed from behind • long neck • bad neck • Adam's apple • Tag group:Neck and neckwear
wiki.neck garter: A garter worn around the neck.
wiki.no halo: When a character who normally has a halo is depicted without one.
wiki.noses touching: Two characters touching the tips of their noses together. Usually interpreted as a friendly greeting gesture in various cultures.
wiki.note: Text or a drawing (object) on a piece of paper, which may or may not have been ripped out of a notebook or similar. Often stuck on walls with tape or nail (hardware)s, sometimes just left on surfaces like beds or tables.
wiki.ofuda on head: An ofuda taped on a character's head, usually a jiangshi.
wiki.orange goggles: The lens color of the goggles is orange.
wiki.pants around one leg: Pants that have been partially removed and are wrapped around only one leg.
wiki.party: A social gathering for celebration and recreation.
wiki.patterned: An article of clothing that has a distinct pattern woven into the fabric. Some specific patterns are tagged on Danbooru, but this tag can cover unique patterns that may or may not have a name for them.
wiki.person on head: A person on top of someone's head, generally in chibi form.
wiki.pink arm warmers: Arm warmers that are colored pink.
wiki.pointing melee weapon: Holding a weapon in a way so that the dangerous part of the weapon (barrel of gun, blade, etc) is pointing at someone or something.
wiki.police car: A police car is a car utilized by police officers to patrol and respond to several incidents.
wiki.print socks: Socks printed with a unique pattern of shapes or images. Common patterns include hearts, stars, and animal prints.
wiki.puffy cheeks: When both cheeks of a character are puffed out or bulging out. This is may be caused by something pushing the cheeks out, such as food when eating or air when pouting, but may also be a design element to make the character to appear childish.
wiki.purple cloak: A cloak that is colored purple.
wiki.purple robe: A robe that is colored purple.
wiki.rabbit on head: A rabbit located on someone's head.
wiki.red curtains: Deprecated. Use stage curtains or curtains if applicable.
wiki.red star: Any star which is coloured red. The five-pointed one is often associated with the Soviet Union, communism, and left wing politics.
wiki.ring necklace: A necklace with a ring attached to it.
wiki.runny nose: A character's nose is running, producing snot.
wiki.scar on hand: A scar located somewhere on a character's hands.
wiki.scar on leg: A scar located on a person's legs.
wiki.school of fish: Any dense assemblage of similar-looking fish that swim together as a group. The number of fish making up a school may range from the tens to the tens of thousands.
wiki.scratching: The act of using the fingers to lightly claw at a surface of skin, usually to get rid of an itch. The marks left behind are scratches.
wiki.scratching cheek: A character scratching their own cheek with one finger, usually out of embarrassment, shyness, and/or uncertainty.
wiki.scratching head: Scratching the head. In fiction, it's often associated with confusion or embarrassment.
wiki.screen light: A monitor or other electronic screen that is also a light source, illuminating whatever or whoever it faces.
wiki.severed head: A head that has been severed from its body.
wiki.severed limb: Tag applicable when severed limbs (limbs detached from the rest of the body) are visible in an image.
wiki.shaking head: When a character moves their head, usually side-to-side, often meaning "no."
wiki.shark fin: A character with a fin of a shark.
wiki.shield on back: When a shield is placed on someone's back, often together with a weapon.
wiki.short sidetail: A side ponytail where the hair is notably shorter than normal. Usually stops halfway between the top of the head and the chin.
wiki.short yukata: A short variety of yukata, analogous to short kimono.
wiki.shoulder guard: A piece of armor worn on the shoulder.
wiki.side drill: Hair tied into drill hair on one side of the head, like a side ponytail.
wiki.side-tie peek: When the side-ties of a pair of side-tie panties peek out beneath a character's skirt or dress, or through a hip vent. Only the strings should be visible, not the rest of panties.
wiki.single bare leg: When one of a character's legs is not covered by any kind of legwear or clothing, while the other leg is covered. Footwear does not count against this tag.
wiki.skeletal arm: An arm that consists exclusively of bone, while other parts of the body consist of flesh or even mechabare.
wiki.skull on head: A real skull (often an animal skull) worn on the head like a hat.
wiki.sky print: Clothing or an object that has the printing of the sky on it. Other things such as clouds, the moon, and/or flying birds among other things should indicate that the sky is being represented.
wiki.slim legs: Legs that are a little bit more slim than usual.
wiki.snake print: Clothing or an object with the printed motif of a snake's skin.
wiki.spread navel: When a character's navel is spread open, by themselves or by someone else.
wiki.square: A shape with four equal sides and four right angles. It is a popular shape used for window displays, record albums, etc.
wiki.stitched leg: When one or both character's legs is either attached to the rest of the body with stitches or has a significant amount of stitches on it, commonly seen on zombies
wiki.striped fur: Body fur with a striped pattern.
wiki.surprised arms: When someone raises their lower arms in front of their upper arms during a surprised reaction, since it is a reflexive response to something unexpected. Might involve clenched hands as well.
wiki.sword behind back: Holding a sword behind the back.
wiki.tall: Ambiguous tag. Use the following instead: • height • height mark • height chart • height conscious • height envy • height difference • size difference • stadiometer, height-measuring instrument • tall female • tall male • giant • giantess • giant male • giant monster • oversized animal • long legs
wiki.team skull: A villainous team from the Pokemon series based in the Alola region.
wiki.toggles: Large button-like fasteners that typically consist of a (usually) wooden peg that fits into a string loop to hold a coat together.
wiki.torn: When something that is supposed to be in one piece has been ripped apart and left in tatters.
wiki.towel around waist: A towel worn wrapped around the waist. If the character is holding the towel open behind themselves, use open towel instead.
wiki.tri braids: A hairstyle that consists of three braided lengths of hair.
wiki.twintails day: A day to celebrate twintails, held on February 2. Promoted by the Japan Twintail Assocation since 2012, when it was also approved by the Japan Anniversary Association.
wiki.tying: Tying an article of clothing together. Examples include bowties or ribbons on many school uniforms, side-tie bikinis or side-tie panties.
wiki.under tree: A character is under a tree, regardless of whether they are standing, sitting, lying, etc.
wiki.unworn bowtie: A bowtie is present in the image but is not being worn.
wiki.unworn goggles: Goggles are present in the image, but not being worn.
wiki.unworn necklace: A necklace that is present in the image but is not being worn.
wiki.unworn pants: A pair of pants are present in the image, but are not being worn.
wiki.user interface: Posts depicting a tangibly visible user interface, that is, a visual layout of various elements that a user might need in order to interact with software or some other technological product. Often features buttons, overlaid text, and/or a list or menu of choices.
wiki.veiny hands: Hands that show visible veins. This tag does not apply to veiny forearms or biceps. Use veiny arms in those cases.
wiki.very long tongue: A tongue with length equal to or longer than the length of the character's face. Often prehensile.

wiki.training corps (emblem): The emblem of Shingeki No Kyojin's trainee characters, before their advancement to another branch. Generally found emblazoned on the sleeves and back of the characters' uniforms. Resembles a pair of crossed swords over a shield.
wiki.super soaker: A water gun which usually features a very large water reservoir and often a shotgun-style pump action for manual pressurization. This allows for much longer playtime between reloads and more soaking; hence, the moniker.
wiki.paralyzer: A stun gun in the form of a handgun used by Samus Aran while in zero suit form featured in the Metroid and Super Smash Bros. series.
wiki.duel disk: A device used for playing Duel Monster card games in the Yu-Gi-Oh! manga and anime. Typically takes the shape of a forearm-mounted contraption with foldable blades that is used to place cards on it. The device utilizes "Solid Vision" technology to generate hologram of monsters and cards played by both players.
wiki.z-ring: A bracelet that allows a Trainer and their Pokémon to gather the Z-Power required to perform Z-Moves.
wiki.hook: Any type of curved weapon with a sharp point at the end attached to a rope. The weapon pierces the target and ensnares them, and then drags them toward the weapon user.
wiki.masu: A masu is a square wooden box originally used to measure rice. Today it is used to drink sake, and to carry beans for mamemaki.
wiki.vacuum cleaner: A cleaning device that uses powerful suction to suck up dirt and dust inside the house.
wiki.qingxin flower: An item from Genshin Impact that is a Local Specialty from Liyue. A white flower that grows exclusively on mountains and peaks throughout Liyue, notably Minlin and Wuwang Hill. Best-known as Ganyu's favorite food.
wiki.beretta 92: A series of 9×19mm handgun designed and manufactured by Fabbrica d'Armi Pietro Beretta of Brescia, Italy in 1975. It can be recognized by the large slide cutout exposing much of the barrel and the slide-mounted safety/decocking lever (the original model had a frame-mounted safety).
wiki.knight (chess): A chess piece shaped like a horse's head, meant to represent the knight in the game of chess. May also (rarely) be shaped like a helm. The knight moves on an extended diagonal from one corner of any 2×3 rectangle of squares to the furthest opposite corner.
wiki.nintendo 3ds: A handheld game console released by Nintendo in February 2011. Successor to the Nintendo DS.
wiki.bishamonten's spear: In Touhou, the spear of Bishamonten is an artifact belonging to Toramaru Shou. It is usually depicted as spear, but also as a trident, lance or halberd.
wiki.bamboo shoot: The edible sprout of any of several species of bamboo.
wiki.roasted sweet potato: A roasted sweet potato, popular as a winter treat in Japan.
wiki.miracle mallet: A small magic mallet from Japanese folk tales. It is said that swinging the mallet grants its holder’s wishes.
wiki.stuffed dog: A stuffed animal in the shape of a dog.
wiki.battleship: A type of large late 19th century to mid 20th century oceangoing warship characterized by its heavy armor and large guns that was ultimately rendered obsolete by advances in airplane and missile technology.
wiki.clothes pin: A clamped pin used for hanging laundry on a line, or for holding up hair.
wiki.scouter: A small, single-lens eyepiece that is worn wrapped around the side of the head, its name here originating from Dragon Ball Z. The device typically sports a heads-up display that provides its wearer with statistics or information on their surroundings, similar to a head-mounted display.
wiki.stakes of purgatory: Characters from Umineko no Naku Koro Ni, seven stakes capable of taking human form, each representing a deadly sin. In keeping with Umineko's various shout-outs to the Divine Comedy, their ages follow the ordering of the terraces in Purgatorio.
wiki.ashtray: A receptacle for ash from cigarettes and cigars.
wiki.bipod: A two-legged stand attached toward the front of a gun (usually a machine gun or sniper rifle). It supports the weapon on the ground (or some elevated structure) and reduces fatigue when the shooter must remain in a stationary position. Commonly collapsible or foldable to save space when not in use.
wiki.beer bottle: A glass bottle that contains beer.
wiki.walther: Ambiguous tag. Please use these tags for specific models of weapons designed and manufactured by Carl Walther GmbH in Germany. → weapon, Handgun, Walther LP53, Walther P22, Walther P38, Walther P5, Walther P99, Walther PDP
wiki.year of the dog: The Year of the Dog is not any particular year in history, but a recurring position in the 12-year zodiac cycle. Years of the Dog include 1934, 1946, 1958, 1970, 1982, 1994, 2006, 2018, and 2030.
wiki.dream soul: A pink, blob-like substance frequently associated with Doremy Sweet.
wiki.shamoji: In Japanese cuisine, an extra-large paddle-shaped spoon used for stirring and serving rice and mixing vinegar into it. It may also be used to crush vegetables. Traditionally it is made out of non-metallic material such as bamboo, lacquerware or bare wood. Mass-produced plastic ones may be packaged with a rice cooker.
wiki.year of the pig: The Pig is the last of 12 animals representing the Chinese zodiac. The following are years of the Pig: 1935, 1947, 1959, 1971, 1983, 1995, 2007, 2019, 2031.
wiki.grimoire of alice: The demonic tome Alice Margatroid used as a weapon in the Extra Stage of Touhou Mystic Square and continues to keep on her person in later appearances. Using the book appears to unlock Alice's full potential, but due to her cowardly inner nature and her fear of the implications if she lost a fight at full power, Alice…
wiki.laundry basket: A basket used to hold laundry. Often made of plastic with small holes in the sides.
wiki.broccoli: A green vegetable with numerous florets. Can be eaten raw or blanched.
wiki.through screen: Going through a television or computer screen, Sadako-style. A type of through medium.
wiki.stiletto (weapon): A stiletto is a kind of dagger, optimized to function as a stabbing weapon exclusively. Generally it has little to no cutting edges, being essentially a long, thin spike with a needle-like point mounted to a handle.
wiki.floating rock: A rock that appears to be floating.
wiki.cabbage: An edible plant, eaten as a vegetable.
wiki.canned coffee: Brewed coffee dispensed in steel or aluminum can similar to soda, seen a lot in Japan.
wiki.chess: A board game in which pieces of different powers are moved around a checkered chessboard. The object of the game is to attack the opponent's king, and put him in a position wherein it's impossible to escape ("checkmate").
wiki.eel: A type of fish with an greatly elongated body. They may or may not possess fins.
wiki.materia: Variously colored, translucent spheres in the Compilation of Final Fantasy VII. In-story, condensed mako energy, derived from the Lifestream, granting powers based on its type. The white materia is smaller than normal, about marble-sized, while the black materia is larger than most fists.
wiki.jolly roger: A symbol drawn using a skull and crossbones, a skull and crossed swords, or much less commonly a skeleton holding an hourglass and a dart striking a heart.
wiki.firelock: An antique firearm that uses an external mechanism to ignite the gunpowder, instead of using a modern self-contained ammunition.
wiki.oonusa: A Shinto ritual purification wand which resembles a gohei except with much more paper streamer decorations attached to a wooden staff or sakaki branch. If the staff is hexagonal or octagonal it is a haraegushi. The oonusa is waved over the person, object or offering in order to transfer the sins and pollutions to it.
wiki.groceries: Groceries are food items bought from a supermarket or grocery store.
wiki.window (computing): An artwork containing a software window.
wiki.smartphone case: A case put on a smartphone.
wiki.kickboard: A flotation device used as a guide to develop the kicking action in swimming.
wiki.honda: A major Japanese-based manufacturer of automobiles, motorcycles, gasoline generators, snow blowers, garden equipment and other items involving internal combustion engines. They are also involved in robotics/AI and aerospace.
wiki.carton: Ambiguous tag. • For drink cartons, see drink carton, milk carton, alcohol carton, or juice box. • For any cubic or rectangular container used to hold something inside it, use box or cardboard box. • For a container used for holding eggs, use egg carton.
wiki.ooarai (emblem): Emblem from the series Girls und Panzer signifying the Ooarai Girls Academy team.
wiki.ray gun: A pistol-like energy weapon of the kind seen in classic 1950s science fiction, such as the Flash Gordon (series) series. They usually fire lasers, heat rays, death rays, or some other type of energy ray.
wiki.bolt: Ambiguous. See bolt (hardware), lightning bolt symbol or crossbow bolt.
wiki.bolt (hardware): A fastener that is not tapered, and can be held in place with a nut, using a wrench. Sometimes similar in appearance to a screw.
wiki.trash: Food wraps, paper scraps, empty cans, etc. Rubbish small enough to throw in a trash can.
wiki.chili pepper: A very spicy fresh or dried fruit. Comes in a variety of colors, red being the most known.
wiki.tambourine: A percussion instrument composed of a frame with pairs of small jingles attached to it. It may or may not have a striking pad or drumhead on one side of the frame. It is played by striking with the hand, shaking, or rattling.
wiki.jam: A condiment made by boiling down fruit and adding sugar, honey, or pectin. Also called a fruit preserve because it is canned for long-lasting storage.
wiki.biwa lute: The biwa (琵琶) is a Japanese short-necked fretted lute (instrument), often used in narrative storytelling. The biwa is the chosen instrument of Benten, goddess of music, eloquence, poetry, and education in Japanese Shinto.
wiki.craft essence (fate): Images bearing the flourishes and decorations of Fate/Grand Order's Craft Essence card_(medium)s, including star (symbol) rarity and HP/ATK values. Official art also bears the copyright name and company name, while fan-made ones ought to be tagged as card parody.
wiki.sprinkles: Tiny pieces of colored candy used to top ice cream, chocolate, cake, cupcake and other desserts.
wiki.phoenix: A mythical sacred firebird originated from Greek mythology; a fire spirit with a colorful plumage and a tail of gold and scarlet. According to legend the creature always rises from the ashes of its own previously deceased form. It symbolizes immortality and the eternal cycle of death and rebirth.
wiki.canteen: A small bottle used to carry water, especially by soldiers or campers.
wiki.croissant: A buttery, flaky Vienna-style pastry named for its well-known crescent shape.
wiki.cork: A stopper used to seal a jar or bottle.
wiki.lance of longinus (evangelion): An alien weapon in the Neon Genesis Evangelion series.
wiki.cupboard: Furniture for enclosing dishware or grocery items that are stored in a home.
wiki.orca: The Orca (Orcinus orca) is a black and white carnivorous marine mammal. Commonly known as the killer whale and also known as orca whale. The orca is the largest species of dolphin, being part of the family Delphinidae.
wiki.fern: Ferns (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta) are a group of flowerless and seedless plants. They do not have fronds and roots, and reproduce via spores. Their foliage formation is triangular.
wiki.war hammer: A late medieval melee weapon consisting of a long handle with a blunt-faced hammer head, often with a spike to pierce armor. It was designed to deliver heavy damage against well-armored opponents through sheer blunt force.
wiki.sauce: Referring to any liquid or cream served on top of or mixed in with different foods. Popular sauces include tomato sauce, bechamel sauce, pesto sauce, and soy sauce, to name a few.
wiki.casing ejection: The act of ejecting shell casings from a firearm. Most modern, self-loading weapons eject casings automatically after rounds are fired.
wiki.coffee pot: A container designed for serving coffee. This may mean: • A small pourable pot, usually glass or metal, that is placed under a coffee brewer to capture the finished product and dispense it into a coffee mug.
wiki.m16: An American-designed 5.56×45mm NATO assault rifle, developed in 1957 by Eugene Stoner at ArmaLite and based on his previous AR-10 design. The rifle had initial bad notoriety due to the original design's tendency to jam with dirt or in some weather conditions and different ammunition powder types.
wiki.yumi (bow): A type of traditional Japanese bow (weapon) with asymmetrical limbs, the upper limb being considerably longer. The bow is used in kyuudou (traditional Japanese archery).
wiki.star wand: A wand or staff that has a star affixed to the end.
wiki.kadomatsu: A kadomatsu (literally "gate pine") is a traditional Japanese decoration of the New Year placed in pairs in front of homes to welcome ancestral spirits or kami of the harvest. They are placed after Christmas until January 7 (or January 15 during the Edo period) and are considered temporary housing (shintai) for kami.
wiki.paint can: A metal can containing a large amount of paint, particularly used for painting a large surface.
wiki.raspberry: Red or black edible aggregate berries.
wiki.musket: A muzzle-loaded, smooth bore long gun, fired from the shoulder. Generally identified by the presence of a lock on the side of the gun.
wiki.temari ball: A thread ball used both as an ornament and a toy. It originated in China and became popular in Japan in the mid-7th century.
wiki.microwave: A kitchen appliance that uses dielectric heating to warm up food.
wiki.weights: Heavy objects designed for lifting, often made out of metal. Dumbbells are one-handed bars with weights, while barbells are two-handed bars with weights.
wiki.wafer stick: A cylinder of rolled wafer, typically with brown spiral pattern. Often added to ice cream.
wiki.container: An object that can be used to hold or transport something, sometimes featuring a separate lid for closure.
wiki.ak-47: The AK-47 (Russian: Автомат Калашникова образца 1947 года) is a 7.62×39mm assault rifle of Soviet origin, developed between 1944–1946 by Mikhail Kalashnikov. The AK platform has a reputation for its ruggedness, reliability, simple mechanism and ease of manufacture.
wiki.pitcher (container): A container with a handle and large open mouth designed for pouring drinks into a cup or a drinking glass.
wiki.coin purse: A small handbag with no shoulder strap, designed for carrying coins or small objects.
wiki.dollar sign: The dollar sign, also known as the peso sign, is a currency symbol consisting of a capital "S" crossed with one or two vertical strokes, used to indicate the unit of various currencies around the world, including most currencies denominated "peso" and "dollar". Ex: US$, CA$, MEX$.
wiki.crescent rose: Ruby Rose's signature weapon, a red mechanical scythe with a blade at the edge of the handle that can transform into a bolt action sniper rifle or an even more compact form for transportation. The blade can also turn positions without turning the whole scythe.
wiki.stuffed panda: Stuffed animal that resembles a panda.
wiki.holographic monitor: A type of monitor that is also hologram as opposed to being made of solid matter.
wiki.cello: A large bowed string instrument with four strings that is similar in shape to a violin. A cello requires a player to be seated to be played; it is supported by a single spike at its end and also the player's body.
wiki.scalpel: A small and extremely sharp knife used for surgery, anatomical dissection, and various arts and crafts (called a hobby knife). Double-edged scalpels are referred to as "lancets".
wiki.whip sword: A combination sword and whip. Usually, this is a sword that splits into sections connected by an internal string, but can also apply to an extremely flexible sword.
wiki.wanted: A poster distributed by police to warn the public about a criminal who is wanted for arrest. A wanted poster usually has the word "WANTED" at the top, and the fugitive's name and picture on the bottom. Sometimes a bounty or a list of their crimes is included.
wiki.wanted poster: A poster distributed by police to warn the public about a criminal who is wanted for arrest. A wanted poster usually has the word "WANTED" at the top, and the fugitive's name and picture on the bottom. Sometimes a bounty or a list of their crimes is included.
wiki.pawn (chess): A chess piece with a bead on top, meant to represent the pawn in the game of chess. Normally a pawn moves by advancing a single square, but the first time a pawn is moved, it has the option of advancing two squares.
wiki.popsicle stick: A thin, flat wooden stick used to hold popsicles.
wiki.anti-aircraft: A weapon designed for shooting down aircraft.
wiki.hashitsuki nata: A usually double-handed striking tool with a sharp rectangular blade used to cut and split wood. It looks like an oversized cleaver with a blunt or pointed nose.
wiki.keyblade: Weapon type from the Kingdom Hearts JRPG series. True to name, it is a sword-like weapon in the shape and general function of a key.
wiki.chessboard: A square board divided into 64 alternating dark and light squares, used for playing chess or checkers.
wiki.saury: Saury are long, slender silver fish. The Pacific saury, or mackerel pike, is known as sanma (秋刀魚) in Japanese.
wiki.digital clock: A clock that tells time through a digital display, commonly a seven-segment display.
wiki.saint quartz (fate): The currency used to summon Servants in Fate/Grand Order. Has the shape of a stellated octahedron.
wiki.vertical foregrip: A vertical bar accessory which facilitates a shooter's two-handed grip on a submachine gun or rifle (typically but not exclusively an assault rifle). It is found toward the front of the weapon somewhere beneath the barrel, e.g. hanging from the forestock.
wiki.aegis sword (xenoblade): A sword wielded by Pyra (xenoblade), Mythra (xenoblade) and Pneuma (Xenoblade) in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. All three incarnations have their own version. • Pyra's Aegis Sword is uniquely asymmetrical, referencing her status as the weakest aspect of the three. When active, it sprouts a large blade of flame.
wiki.poke ball (legends): An older type of Poké Ball used in Pokémon Legends: Arceus.
wiki.bridle: A piece of headgear that's normally used to control a horse, consisting of buckled straps to which a bit and reins are attached.
wiki.coconut tree: A type of palm tree that coconuts grow on.
wiki.baton (weapon): A blunt weapon often wielded by police officers or martial artists.
wiki.pregnancy test: A small stick-like object used to determine whether or not a woman is pregnant, determined by matching (usually) pink lines after a urine sample. Usually two lines means pregnant and one line means not pregnant.
wiki.anti-aircraft gun: A stationary, emplaced weapon system designed to shoot down aircraft. It may consist of an artillery piece like the 8.8 cm Flak, or mounted machine guns like the ZPU series.
wiki.drum magazine: A type of cylindrical-shaped gun magazine_(weapon) which stores ammunition in a spiral layout (bullets aligned with the barrel), typically resulting in much greater capacity as compared to standard box/stick magazines. Usually associated with automatic firearms such as the iconic Thompson submachine gun and PPSh-41.
wiki.fried rice: A type of food consisting of rice stir-fried on a wok or frying pan, typically with additional ingredients. Commonly found in Asian cuisine.
wiki.mg42: The MG42 (Maschinengewehr 42) is a German World War II-era open-bolt machine gun that fires the 7.92×57mm Mauser round. It supplanted the earlier MG34 in 1942 due to lower manufacturing cost thanks to dominant stamped metal parts.
wiki.red carpet: A long stretch of carpet leading generally synonymous with high profile events, such as film premieres, fashion shows, and award ceremonies. To "roll out the red carpet" means to go all out in welcoming someone.
wiki.bacon: A cut of meat taken from the sides, belly, or back of a pig (or any other animal), and then cured, smoked, or both. It is a popular breakfast protein, a topper in hamburgers and sandwiches, and wrapped around steaks or grilled vegetables.
wiki.shogi: A chess variant in which the pieces resemble arrows and have the same color; they are distinguished by their direction (pointing towards the opponent). It is the most popular chess variant in Japan.
wiki.banana peel: The yellow outer skin of a banana. A common gag is for a person to slip on a banana peel.
wiki.senbei: Japanese rice crackers. Like onigiri, they are often wrapped in nori_(seaweed).
wiki.jump rope: A rope designed for jumping. Two people stand at either end of the rope and rotate it in unison, while a third person jumps over the rope when it reaches ground level. Single-user jump ropes also exist, where the person holds the rope in both hands.
wiki.bc freedom (emblem): Emblem from the series Girls und Panzer signifying the BC Freedom High School.
wiki.jug (bottle): A large bottle with a narrow opening designed to pour drinks into a cup. Milk and water commonly come in jugs.
wiki.oar: A long object consisting of a flat blade attached to a shaft or two blades, attached to either end of a shaft, which is held by the user. By rowing, they can be used to move boats across bodies of water.
wiki.hawk: A medium-sized bird of prey in the Accipitridae family.
wiki.audio jack: A connector commonly used for audio equipment. Sometimes called a headphone jack, jack plug, phone jack, or phone connector.
wiki.minigun: A gatling gun used as a personal portable weapon.
wiki.oven: A chamber or compartment, as in a stove, for baking, roasting, heating, drying, etc.
wiki.soy sauce: Thin brownish sauce made of fermented soy beans, used to season food.
wiki.bull: Colloquially: a male bovine. They often have distinct horns protruding from the sides of their head. More accurately, a male bovine that hasn't been castrated (which would be an ox, but treated synonymously on Danbooru)
wiki.tripod: A three-legged stand used to stabilize another object. Commonly used for photography, where it supports a camera.
wiki.year of the rooster: Every 12 years there is a Year of the Rooster, beginning at Chinese New Year. Years of the Rooster include 1933, 1945, 1957, 1969, 1981, 1993, 2005, 2017, and 2029.
wiki.piano keys: Use this tag when piano keys are shown, but appear to be "disembodied", or if it is not clear to what type of keyboard instrument they are attached to, and also if they are a major focal point of the image. → piano, instrument, keyboard (instrument)
wiki.cockroach: Common insect pest, often censored for comic effect. In Japan, the word for them is "gokiburi", sometimes shortened to G -- especially by terrified girls who don't even want to speak their name.
wiki.flying button: Buttons flying off an article of clothing, often due to being popped off by bursting breasts.
wiki.bald eagle: An eagle found in North America. As an adult they feature dark brown feathers with white head and tail feathers. Their beaks, feet, and irises are bright yellow. The bald eagle has a body length of 70–102 cm (28–40 in) and typical wingspan between 1.8 and 2.3 m (5 ft 11 in and 7 ft 7 in).
wiki.rag: A piece of fabric that is used to clean, polish or wipe areas and things such as the floor, tables, windows, etc.
wiki.cleaning rag: A piece of fabric that is used to clean, polish or wipe areas and things such as the floor, tables, windows, etc.
wiki.pocari sweat: A brand of soda / sports drink popular in Japan and manufactured by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. Recognizable by its logo of a white swirl in a blue background.
wiki.flail: A medieval weapon, made of a weight attached to a handle with a hinge, rope, or short chain. They originated from farming flails, which were used to thresh grain.
wiki.log pose: A valuable object from the One Piece series. A special kind of compass for navigating the treacherous seas of the Grand Line. Similar in design to a wrist watch, only with an orb sitting on top and a floating needle.
wiki.dirigible: A type of aircraft, usually cigar-shaped, that floats by means of a large balloon, usually filled with hydrogen or helium.
wiki.fleur-de-lis: The fleur-de-lis (⚜) is a a stylized lily (flower) (in French, fleur means flower symbol, and lis means lily) or iris (flower) that is often used as a decorative design or in heraldry.
wiki.price tag: A tag or sticker that is attached to a product to show its price.
wiki.crutch: A mobility aid stick used for people who cannot use their legs to support their weight.
wiki.pet food: Food for a pet, such as kibble for a cat or dog. Usually in a pet bowl.
wiki.doorknob: A knob (rounded fixture) used to release the catch when opening a door.
wiki.worm: For whenever there's worms in the picture.
wiki.nissan: A major Japanese automobile company founded in 1933. Operated in export markets under the Datsun marque until 1984. In 1989 they opened Infiniti (company) to sell their luxury vehicles in America under new branding.
wiki.brass knuckles: A small metal weapon worn over the knuckles to strengthen the power of punching with one's fists.
wiki.tofu: A food made by coagulating soy milk and then pressing the resulting curds into soft white blocks.
wiki.dualshock: The line of game controllers designed by Sony for the PlayStation series of consoles, used by the PlayStation 1, PlayStation 2, PlayStation 3, and PlayStation 4.
wiki.depth charge: An explosive designed to sink submarines by exploding underwater at a certain depth, creating an underwater shockwave.
wiki.desert eagle: A gas-operated semi-automatic handgun designed by Magnum Research and Israel Military Industries from 1979 to 1982. It is available in .357 Magnum, .44 Magnum or the proprietary .50 AE chambering. The Desert Eagle is recognizable by its bulky size, triangular barrel profile and variety of finishes.
wiki.chocolate banana: An iced banana coated in chocolate, usually with a covering of sprinkles.
wiki.tuanshan: A type of Chinese hand fan, they're often somewhat transparent. It's a common accessory to accompany hanfu or a qipao, sometimes used to cover one's mouth.
wiki.dusk ball: A type of Poké Ball with an increased catch rate when used at night or in caves.
wiki.chibi on head: A chibi character on someone's hat or head. Use person on head or animal on head as appropriate.
wiki.vodka: A type of strong alcoholic beverages originating from Eastern Europe. They are traditionally distilled from potatoes or wheat.
wiki.fish tank: A small square-shaped glass container where fish and aquatic animals are kept at home or at a restaurant.
wiki.mauser 98: A series of bolt action rifles that was initially designed and manufactured as the final and definitive weapon of the Mauser rifle lineage, the rifle utilized cock-on-open action to chamber the 7.92×57mm cartridge and a 5-round internal magazine.
wiki.fluorescent lamp: A type of electric lamp which produces light by the fluorescence of mercury vapors. Fluorescent lamps generally take the form of long glass tubes that produce a white or bluish-white light. They are widely used in non-residential applications such as classrooms, offices, and shops.
wiki.flintlock: A firelock mechanism where a hammer holding flint strikes a piece of steel and produces sparks. The sparks fall into a pan of gunpowder and ignites the powder. A small hole from the pan to the barrel allows flame to travel and ignite the powder in the barrel.
wiki.too many cats: When there are at least six cats in the image, especially if there are too many to count.
wiki.flagpole: A pole used for flying a flag.
wiki.duct tape: Heavy-duty tape, usually wide and silver or grey in color.
wiki.ketchup bottle: A glass or plastic bottle that dispenses ketchup. There tend to be two distinct ketchup bottle designs - a clear bottle where the product is visible, sold in supermarkets; or a thin red cylindrical tube with a narrow tip, seen in restaurants and diners in both red and yellow varieties to signify ketchup and mustard res…
wiki.daikon: A mild flavored, very large, white East Asian radish.
wiki.tart (food): A delicious baked dish with a pastry base and an open top, usually filled with fruit or custard. Examples of tarts include Bakewell tart, tarte tatin, and treacle tart.
wiki.windsock: A windsock is a conical textile tube that resembles a giant sock. Windsocks can be used as a basic guide to wind direction and speed, or as decoration.
wiki.persimmon: A type of tomato-looking orange fruit that is slightly sweet and tangy.
wiki.signpost: A post with one or more signs giving information about directions and distances.
wiki.stick poster: A poster (medium) that is usually longer and more slender than many pin-up posters, being more like an illustrated version of a vertical rectangular banner.
wiki.toothpick: A small pointed stick used to removed particles from between one's teeth after eating. They can also be used for picking up small appetizers or decoration as a cocktail stick.
wiki.hanging scroll: A hanging scroll, called by the generic terms 立軸 (lìzhóu) in China and 掛軸/掛け軸 (kakejiku) in Japan, is an illustration or piece of calligraphy affixed to a scroll of cloth or paper.
wiki.toyota: A major Japanese car manufacturer, currently the largest automobile company in the world. Toyota offers a wide range of vehicles, ranging from small kei cars to a large trucks.
wiki.bonsai: A miniature tree or shrub growing in a pot or container. Some people practice the art of bonsai trimming purely for long-term cultivation and visual pleasure.
wiki.magnet: A type of object or material that creates its own magnetic field. Commonly found in bar and horseshoe shapes, with one end painted red and the other end painted blue. May also be found in novelty designs used to hang things on a refrigerator.
wiki.golden apple: An apple that is colored gold, or at least yellow.
wiki.centipede: A predacious bug with a flattened body having anywhere from 15 to 173 body segments, each with its own pair of legs. The first pair of legs are modified to catch prey and inject it with venom.
wiki.flat screen tv: A television with a thickness usually under 10 cm (~4 in.). This is opposed to cathode-ray tube televisions or rear-projection televisions whose designs required rather thick housing.
wiki.kitten: A young cat, under a year old.
wiki.stuffed unicorn: A stuffed plush of a unicorn (Basically, a pony with a single horn on its head)
wiki.blue innertube: A type of recreational swim ring used to float in the water, especially by young children and people who cannot swim. So called because it resembles (and in earlier times, usually was) the inner tube of a car tire.
wiki.super mushroom: The most iconic power-up from Nintendo's Mario (series) series of games. It makes the user grow twice as large, stronger, and more resistant to damage. Its most common depiction is a mushroom that has a red cap with white spots (resembling an immature Amanita muscaria) and a beige stem with black eyes.
wiki.rattle: Handheld baby toy that produces sound when shaken.
wiki.spray bottle: A bottle (usually plastic) with a built-in mechanism with a trigger intended to allow the liquid within to be sprayed evenly as a fine mist. This is common with cleaning products. They are also sometimes used with water to discipline pets.
wiki.sleigh: An open usually horse-drawn or reindeer-drawn vehicle with runners for use on snow or ice. Used most commonly to transport people, as opposed to transporting objects or items.
wiki.mousetrap: A spring-loaded contraption designed to catch mice, rats, and other rodents.
wiki.christmas wreath: A wreath made or designed specifically for Christmas. Typically made out of pine branches, decorated with items like ribbons or baubles.
wiki.udon: Thick Japanese wheat-flour noodles, usually served in noodle soups. They are thicker than their Chinese-style ramen counterpart.
wiki.spray paint: A pressurized can filled with paint that can be sprayed over a surface by pressing down on a nozzle.
wiki.ball and chain (weapon): A weapon that consists of a heavy ball, often spiked ball and chain, swung by a long chain like a whip to strike the target. The chain may or may not be attached to a handle.
wiki.drain (object): A conduit through which water is allowed to exit (e.g. from a sink, or a bathroom).
wiki.grenade pin: A grenade pin which is separated from the grenade.
wiki.stuffed frog: A stuffed animal based on a frog.
wiki.gingerbread man: A gingerbread cookie that has been cut with a cookie cutter to resemble a humanoid figure. It can be decorated with icing to add facial features and simple clothes. Often associated with Christmas, but not always.
wiki.furoshiki: A cloth traditionally used to wrap things for transport. Stereotypically used by Japanese burglars to haul their loot.
wiki.hanafuda: Traditional Japanese playing cards. They are composed of 48 cards with flowers representing the months of the year. The word "Hana fuda" literally means "flower cards." The pictures used for them represent the beauty of Japanese nature.
wiki.hylian shield: Shield in the The Legend of Zelda Franchise. It bears the Hylian Crest. A Hylian Shield is the traditional shield borne by the knights of Hyrule and is commonly used by Link.
wiki.hatsumoude: Hatsumoude (初詣) is the first shrine visit of the New Year in Japan.
wiki.evoker: A special gun used by Persona users in Persona 3. In order to summon a Persona (summon), the user must point the gun to their head and pull the trigger when ready.
wiki.stapler: A device used for buckling a staple to several pieces of paper in order to keep them together and organized.
wiki.slug: A shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusk. If it has a shell, then it's a snail.
wiki.twig: Small branch removed from a plant. Can be seen in a character's mouth in place of a cigarette, used as a makeshift flag post for decoration, held like a sword for extended reach, stuck on a character literally "out of the woods", or just tinder/kindling you would find laying on the ground.
wiki.madoka runes: A runic alphabet within the world of Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica.
wiki.ginkgo tree: A hardy, long-lived dioecious tree with fan-shaped leaves. The sole surviving species of ginkgo is Ginkgo biloba.
wiki.yakisoba: Fried noodles with their origin in Chinese chow mein with many variations flavored with Worcestershire sauce, salt and soy sauce. The most common variety is sauce yakisoba flavored with Worcestershire sauce and it has especially deep associations with summer festivals and seaside restaurants called 海の家 (Umi no Ie).
wiki.fly: Bugs of the order Diptera, which use only a single pair of wings to fly, the hindwings having evolved into sensory organs.
wiki.sharing food: The act of sharing food is depicted (often as a sign of affection).
wiki.tarot (card): A physical tarot card used to play the card game and perform divination. Tag legible card designs where applicable as seen on the tarot wiki.
wiki.shakujou: A ceremonial staff with dangling rings, commonly associated with Buddhism and used for religious rituals.
wiki.usb: Standard connector used to connect devices together to transfer data or power. Stands for Universal Serial Bus.
wiki.water yoyo: A kind of water balloon on a string. You win them at Japanese festivals by participating in yo-yo fishing, similar to how you get bagged fish from goldfish scooping.
wiki.plumeria: A genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae. Most species are deciduous shrubs or small trees that grow in tropical regions. One of the most commonly depicted species is Plumeria rubra, also known as frangipani.
wiki.balance scale: A device for weighing. It has a balanced beam and two pans. When the pans contain exactly the same mass, the beam is in balance. One can place an object in one pan and standard weights in the other to find what the object weighs.
wiki.seal impression: The impression made after an ink stamp is pressed in ink and then onto the image. Historically, seals have taken the place of signatures all across East Asia. The impression usually is rectangular or square, with the characters of the author's name in red ink.
wiki.control rod: What Reiuji Utsuho wears on her right arm. It resembles a cannon, but is based off of a nuclear control rod. ZUN stated that he gave Utsuho an arm cannon to compensate for the three-legged Yatagarasu instead of using an actual third leg.
wiki.control rod (touhou): What Reiuji Utsuho wears on her right arm. It resembles a cannon, but is based off of a nuclear control rod. ZUN stated that he gave Utsuho an arm cannon to compensate for the three-legged Yatagarasu instead of using an actual third leg.
wiki.welsh corgi: A breed of dog originating from Wales, defined by two types of Corgis: the Cardigan Welsh Corgi, and the Pembroke Welsh Corgi. They generally have long bodies, short stubby legs, and long erect ears.
wiki.koinobori: Koi-shaped windsocks used as part of celebrations on Kodomo no Hi (Japanese Children's Day), a Japanese national holiday held annually on May 5th.
wiki.bident: A two-pronged spear resembling a pitchfork, historically used both as a weapon and as a fishing tool. In folklore it is associated with demons and the underworld. Compare with the trident, its three-pronged counterpart.
wiki.kantele: A traditional plucked string instrument native to Finland. It is part of the zither family.
wiki.undersized animal: An animal or creature that is much smaller than usually depicted.
wiki.manta ray: A very large oceangoing ray that feeds on plankton and small fish. Flat and having large "wings" like its other brethren, it sports two projections on either side of its head (called cephalic lobes) that help guide food into its mouth.
wiki.hoshi no tsue: Kinomoto Sakura's "Star Wand," from Cardcaptor Sakura. •
wiki.pickup truck: A light-duty truck that has an open cargo area (bed) with low sides and tailgate, used to carry light to medium sized loads.
wiki.erlenmeyer flask: A type of laboratory flask which features a flat bottom, a conical body, and a cylindrical neck.
wiki.wax seal: A drop of wax solidified on an envelope to seal it, usually has text and symbols printed on it using a wax stamp.
wiki.rubik's cube: A cube-shaped twisty puzzle, the objective of which is to have each of all six sides having a single color. This is done by twisting the cube's faces.
wiki.orange juice: A type of fruit juice that is squeezed out of orange (fruit)s.
wiki.gorilla: A ground-dwelling great ape native to Africa. Well known for its black hair, imposing muscular body and chest-beating behavior.
wiki.fishbowl: A type of round glass bowl that small aquatic pets, such as goldfish, are sometimes kept in.
wiki.large syringe: A syringe that is much larger in size. They're not really meant for injecting into a patient.
wiki.turkey (food): Cooked turkey (bird), served during Thanksgiving, Christmas, or at a generally exquisite feast.
wiki.chisel: A chisel is a wedged hand tool with a characteristically shaped cutting edge on the end of its blade, for carving or cutting a hard material (e.g. wood, stone, or metal). The tool can be used by hand, struck with a mallet, or applied with mechanical power.
wiki.ring-con: A game controller for the Nintendo Switch resembling a black pilates ring. It is used to play Ring Fit Adventure.
wiki.artillery: A weapon or war machine able to fire munitions beyond the effective range of personal weapons. This includes mortar (weapon)s, cannons and rocket launchers. Other personal artillery pieces, such as mortars carried by troops, may fall into this category.
wiki.tiger i: A German heavy tank developed in 1942 and used in World War II. The final official German designation was Panzerkampfwagen VI Tiger Ausf.E, often shortened to Tiger.
wiki.water lily flower: For the leaves of Water Lily, see lily pad. Please note that these flowers are not actually lilies. → lily pad, lotus, bud, lotus pod, lotus leaf
wiki.energy weapon: A directed-energy ranged weapon that emits energy focused in an aimed direction to destroy a target without the means of a projectile. Frequent in many science fiction works.
wiki.trowel: A small single-hand implement for digging, scooping, spreading, or otherwise manipulating dirt or other bulk materials, such as mortar, cement, and plaster.
wiki.food insertion: Insertion of a piece of food (typically a carrot, banana, cucumber or other phallic object) into the vagina or anus.
wiki.angelfish: Any of three species of fish in the genus Pterophyllum, commonly kept as aquarium fish. They have triangular bodies with elongated fins.
wiki.kriss vector: A submachine gun utilizing a unique bolt mechanism to reduce recoil manufactured by KRISS USA, formerly known as Transformational Defense Industries.
wiki.eggshell: The outer, inedible shell of an egg.
wiki.seed: The fetal form of a plant. Often planted into soil to grow new plants, or eaten as a form of nutrition.
wiki.diploma: An oftentimes decorated document that certifies that its holder has completed a specific course or lesson. May be stored in a tube or folder for storage or easier handling, or be put in a picture frame to be decorated on the wall.
wiki.cattail: A plant of the Typha genus.
wiki.aburaage: A Japanese food that consists of thin slices of deep-fried tofu.
wiki.rina-chan board: The sketchbook or digital mask used by Tennoji Rina from Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club.
wiki.toothpaste: A paste or gel consisting of fluoride, abrasives and flavorants that is placed in a tube and squeezed out onto a toothbrush for brushing teeth. These components assist in oral hygiene and aesthetics, but toothpaste should not be consumed due to the fluoride.

wiki.canopy (aircraft): Transparent enclosure covering the cockpit section of an aircraft. Sometimes also found on other vehicles (mostly fictional mecha) and can be likewise tagged such.

wiki.mousepad (object): A thin, flat pad on which a computer mouse is used.

wiki.mailbox (incoming mail): A physical receptacle outside a home or business where mail is delivered by a postal carrier. Also known as a letterbox, letter plate, letter hole, mail slot, etc.

wiki.stacking: The act of building a tower, human or otherwise.

wiki.suikawari: Suikawari (lit. watermelon splitting) is a traditional Japanese game that involves splitting a watermelon with a stick while blindfolded.
wiki.pov across bed: When a character is lying on a bed while looking at the viewer, and the viewer is assumed to also be lying on the bed with them.
wiki.cat on lap: A cat sitting, lying or standing on someone's lap.
wiki.cross-body stretch: A type of shoulder stretch. One arm is placed horizontally across the chest at shoulder height, then pulled in at the elbow by the other arm.
