wiki.stirring: The act of rotating a spoon, a stick or even a drinking straw within liquid in order to consistently disperse ingredients or to keep it at an even temperature.
wiki.en pointe: The technique of balancing on the tips of one's toes, usually seen in ballet. Unsafe without wearing ballet slippers.
wiki.faceplant: When a character falls to the ground face first.
wiki.adjusting another's clothes: One character is fixing another's worn clothing so it fits properly or looks neat.
wiki.ear cleaning: Cleaning another's ears, usually with a mimikaki. The latter character's head is almost always in the cleaning character's lap, often as they sit seiza. This usually displays a great amount of comfort or trust between the two characters.
wiki.head on arm: Resting the head on one arm.
wiki.toasting (gesture): A social custom in which a drink (usually of alcohol) is taken to honor a person or to celebrate an occasion. A toast may involve two people touching their drinking glasses together, or simply raising their glasses in the air.
wiki.at gunpoint: When a character is threatening someone with a gun.
wiki.uppercut: A swinging upward punch, usually aimed at the chin.
wiki.flower over mouth: A flower over a character's mouth.
wiki.rock paper scissors: A simple game played between two players. Each player must choose either rock, paper, or scissors. Rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, and paper beats rock, with a tie if both players choose the same.
wiki.on innertube: Resting or floating on an innertube.
wiki.pinky swear: When two people link their pinky fingers, typically to signify that a promise has been made, or as a way to show affection in a less obvious manner.
wiki.spraying: Spraying water or a liquid at a target, such as by spray can or hose.
wiki.drawing on another's face: Drawing, painting or writing that has been or is being done on another person's face, sometimes as a prank.
wiki.waist hug: A hug that is done at the waist area of the other person.
wiki.arm pillow: Using one's arms as a makeshift pillow, most often by crossing the arms together on a surface in order to then lay the head down on.
wiki.picking up: Picking something up that has dropped on the floor.
wiki.peeking through fingers: A person covering their face with their hands, but with the fingers spread out so that they can peer through. Typically a sign that they don't want to see what's going on, but curiosity gets the better of them.
wiki.paper on head: A sheet of paper on a person's head, usually positioned so that it would lay over a person's face like a mask.
wiki.one arm handstand: A handstand on a single hand.
wiki.gunbuster pose: The Gunbuster Pose, also known as the Gainax Pose, is an iconic pose often appearing in anime franchises produced by Gainax. It consists of a person standing confidently with crossed arms and feet wide apart.
wiki.taking shelter: The act of going underneath something in order to protect oneself from bad weather, most often rain or snow. One could take shelter under a bridge, an awning, a bus stop shelter, or a tree, among other possible locations or objects.
wiki.thumb sucking: The habit of putting a thumb in one's mouth and sucking it in rhythm. Done by babies as a reflex, the same one responsible for breastfeeding.
wiki.sweeping: The act of using a broom in a back and forth motion on the ground to push dirt and dust aside.
wiki.tasting: Consuming a very small portion of food for the purpose of testing its flavor.
wiki.slouching: The less extreme form of bent back. Drooping of the shoulders and upper spine. Often done when a character is defeated or lazy.
wiki.delivery: A person delivering some sort of package to a destination as a job.
wiki.finger counting: A hand gesture where a character indicates a number with their fingers raised. Some artists use this for countdowns, anniversaries, and milestone celebrations.
wiki.three quarter profile: Almost a profile shot, but a portion of the character's other eye and/or brow is distinctly visible.
wiki.snapping fingers: A character performs a flicking motion with their thumb and middle finger so that they produce a snapping sound.
wiki.glove in mouth: Holding a glove in the mouth.
wiki.mudra: Mudra are symbolic or ritualistic gestures in Hinduism and Buddhism that typically involve the hands.
wiki.collar tug: Pulling the collar of one's own shirt slightly down or out, often because of feeling hot or as a sign of nervousness.
wiki.kung fu: One of the fighting styles that have developed over the centuries in China, along with wushu. Kung Fu (or Kenpo) focuses on quickly and swiftly defeating the opponents and countering their moves.
wiki.after battle: The aftermath of a battle. Evident either by the defeated/dead combatants, the injury on the character, or the damaged landscape and/or surroundings.
wiki.partially shaded face: When only one side of a character's face is shaded.
wiki.clown nose: A spherical, usually red, costume accessory made of foam or rubber worn over the nose by circus clowns.
wiki.wall-eyed: When both eyes point outward, in opposite directions. The opposite of cross-eyed.
wiki.furious: An emotion of deep, unbridled anger. A character who is furious is consumed with rage and is often past rational thinking.
wiki.despair: A crushing abyss of sorrow, where all hope is lost. For characters that display spirit-breaking emotional turmoil much greater than simple sadness.
wiki.diamond mouth: A diamond-shaped mouth, with the upper lip similar to :< and the lower lip similar to :>.
wiki.aquiline nose: An aquiline nose, also called a Roman nose or hooked nose, is a type of nose which has a prominent bridge, giving the appearance of being bent or curved. Aquiline comes from the Latin aquilinus, meaning "eagle-like", alluding to the curved beak-like shape of the nose.
wiki.evil eyes: A character giving someone a malicious, aggressive, sinister, etc. glance.
wiki.horrified: For when a character displays an expression of immense horror, generally some mixture of shock, fear, or revulsion. This tag should not be used for images that are meant to be horrifying for the viewer; that would be horror (theme).
wiki.holding skewer: Holding a skewer. If a character is holding a skewer with food on it, you might consider using the holding food tag alongside this one.
wiki.holding ice cream cone: When a character is holding an ice cream cone. Actual ice cream may or may not be present.
wiki.holding gem: A character is holding a gem.
wiki.holding whisk: A character is holding a whisk.
wiki.holding crowbar: When someone is holding a crowbar.
wiki.holding flask: Someone is holding any type of flask.
wiki.holding reins: Holding the reins of an animal.
wiki.holding necktie: Ambiguous tag, use one of the following instead: • holding unworn necktie • adjusting necktie • neckwear grab • necktie grab • loose necktie • unworn necktie
wiki.holding handcuffs: Someone is holding a pair of handcuffs.
wiki.holding whistle: Holding a whistle in the hands.
wiki.holding mahjong tile: A character holding a mahjong tile.
wiki.holding flower pot: When a character is holding flower pot(s).
wiki.holding pregnancy test: Someone is holding a pregnancy test.
wiki.holding pocket watch: Someone is holding a pocket watch.
wiki.instrument on back: A musical instrument being worn on someone's back, usually for transport.
wiki.holding milk carton: Someone is holding a milk carton.
wiki.holding racket: Holding a racket, whether a tennis racket or a badminton racket.
wiki.ofuda between fingers: Holding one or more ofuda between the fingers.
wiki.holding pumpkin: Someone is holding a pumpkin. This can include pumpkins that are carved into jack-o'-lanterns.
wiki.holding butterfly net: For use on posts which depict someone holding a butterfly net.
wiki.holding bass guitar: A character is holding a bass guitar.
wiki.holding star: Someone is holding a star (symbol), whether it'd be an actual ornament shaped like one, or simply an intangible star.
wiki.sitting on throne: Someone is on the throne. Usually they're sitting on it, but can include any other poses.
wiki.propeller fighter: A type of military fighter aircraft powered by piston-driven propeller. Being the main form of military aircraft until the end of World War II, when it was replaced by jet fighter.
wiki.sparkling aura: Multiple sparkles surrounding an object or character. If the sparkles are indicating beauty, romance, or a dream-like state, they may be bishie sparkles.
wiki.happy aura: An aura that depicts happiness, usually with multiple lines radiating outward from a character, or with floating flower symbols. This can be used along with notice lines.
wiki.aqua flower: A flower that is colored aqua.
wiki.poppy (flower): A normally red flower often considered a weed. The flower has overlapping petals in a circle, surrounding a black core. In the former British empire it is commonly associated with remembrance of the first World War, due to the poppies that grew in the no man's land.
wiki.black bird: A bird that is black. In many cases this will be a crow or raven, but not always.
wiki.blue bird: A bird that is blue. The bluebird (one word) is a specific species.
wiki.black hole: A cosmic phenomenon consisting of a massive collapsed star's core.
wiki.cerise bouquet: One of three units formed within the Hasu no Sora Jogakuin School Idol Club, passed down through tradition in the club's history.
wiki.red butterfly: A butterfly that is colored red.
wiki.on tank: Sitting, standing, lying, or otherwise resting on the outside of a tank. This includes looking out of a tank hatch.
wiki.orange cat: A cat whose fur is mostly or entirely orange. A popular character is Garfield (character) by Jim Davis.
wiki.multiple unit train: A self-propelled Train composed of one or more carriages joined, which when coupled to another multiple unit can be controlled by a single driver, with multiple-unit train control. It is also possible for 2 Locomotives Attached in Front and rear of the Train. For Example the BR Class 43 HST.
wiki.loving aura: An aura that depicts love by multiple floating hearts, usually in a circular motion around the character's head.
wiki.static: A random pattern of colored or black-and-white pixels displayed on a television or other screen when no signal is present.
wiki.queen of spades symbol: A black spade (shape) symbol, typically with the letters "Q" or "QoS" in it. A common symbol of "blacked" race fetishism content, it indicates a woman with an interracial sexual preference for black men. Women with this preference are called "Queens of Spades".
wiki.bellflower: Bellflower is the common name for flowering plants of the Campanulaceae family, which comprises around 2,400 species. They vary greatly in color and details. The leaves are simple and alternating, while the flowers are bell-shaped and consist of a narrow lobed corolla.
wiki.lotus leaf: A round leaf of the Nelumbo family (lotuses).
wiki.pink fire: Fire that is predominately pink in color.
wiki.cosmos (flower): Cosmos are annual plants of the Asteraceae family with daisy (flower)-like flowers that sit atop long, slender stems with lacy foliage. Their colors and numbers of petals vary depending on the species, though most varieties have eight broad, usually notched or serrated petals.
wiki.gleam: See: • Bloom - visual effect in which the edges of bright objects appear blurred. • Glint - a singular flash emitted when a solid object reflects light. • Light particles - small orbs of light that appear to be suspended in the air. • Sparkle - a momentary flash of light.
wiki.diorama: A miniature scene that appears 'cut out'; a scene enclosed in a 3D shape, or with a partial background made up of props.
wiki.lgbt pride: An image whose main focus or theme is LGBT pride.
wiki.white rabbit (animal): A rabbit with white fur, rabbits with pure white fur and red eyes can be a result of albinism.
wiki.wall lamp: A lamp that is affixed to a wall.
wiki.stop sign: A red road sign with the word "STOP" written in various languages. It's usually in the shape of an octagon in most countries, but can sometimes be in other shapes such as an inverted triangle (in Japan's case).
wiki.lampshade: A fixture that covers the lightbulb on a lamp to diffuse the light it emits.
wiki.greek cross: A type of cross (+) with arms of equal length.
wiki.sprout: A young plant that has just begun its development process, typically represented by two green leaves connected to a small stem. For the tree version, see sapling.
wiki.racetrack: A purpose-built course for car or motorcycle racing, usually with seating for fans to watch. For racetracks built specifically for horse racing, see horse racing track. For the type of track used for track and field events, see running track.
wiki.piano bench: A wooden bench used by piano players. Some are long, but most are short. Sometimes they are cushioned.
wiki.cryokinesis: The ability to psychically control cold and ice.
wiki.tall grass: Grass that appear to have notably tall, standing foliage rather than just green patches on the ground.
wiki.shared blanket: A character sharing a blanket with someone or something else.
wiki.aztec: A group of ancient cultures located in modern day Mexico. Often the term "Aztec" refers exclusively to the Mexica people of Tenochtitlan (now the location of Mexico City), situated on an island in Lake Texcoco, who referred to themselves as Mexica Tenochca.
wiki.blue blood: Blood that is colored blue instead of the traditional red.
wiki.nemophila (flower): Nemophila, commonly called baby blue eyes, is a genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae. Commonly represented by Nemophila menziesii.
wiki.iris (flower): A flowering plant belonging to the genus Iris.
wiki.dome: A roof-like architectural element similar to the hollow upper half of a sphere.
wiki.horn flower: One or more flowers being worn as a horn ornament.
wiki.carnation: A popular flower, Dianthus caryophyllus, that somewhat resembles the rose, except the petals are ridged and less distinct in shape.
wiki.hay: Dried grass or other plants, such as clover or alfalfa, cut and dried for animal feed. After being harvested hay is stored in hay bales or loosely piled in haystacks. Often seen on farms around livestock or in the middle of fields.
wiki.brown cat: A cat whose fur is mostly or entirely brown.
wiki.red sun: A red circle is drawn mainly in the background of Japanese New Year's greetings. It is sometimes depicted in combination with Mount Fuji or cranes .
wiki.crosshair: Guide lines seen when looking down the scope of a sniper rifle or similar gun.
wiki.garland (decoration): A rope-like decoration strung at festive celebrations. Typical garlands are made from tinsel, flowers, or evergreen leaves and are commonly associated with Christmas. They often have a fuzzy or fluffy appearance.
wiki.tile roof: A rooftop made of ceramic or clay tiles.
wiki.conch: A spiral seashell used by sea snails. If held up to the ear, the echo sounds like the ocean. It can also be used as a horn (instrument)-like wind instrument.
wiki.seaplane: A airplane designed to land or takeoff from water. They generally come in two forms: Flying boats that utilize a boat-shaped hull, and floatplanes that rely on external pontoons.
wiki.swing set: A type of playground equipment consisting of a metal or wooden frame that supports one or more swings. Use this tag when both the swing and the frame are in the image. If only the swing itself is pictured, just use the swing tag.
wiki.stone walkway: A type of sidewalk comprised of large stones placed next to each other.
wiki.snow on head: Snow resting on top of someone's head.
wiki.mazda: A Japanese automaker founded in 1920. Particularly notable for their usage of the rotary engine, the main engine used for their performance vehicles.
wiki.crocodile: A large scaly reptile with a long body and powerful jaws that lives in rivers and eats meat.
wiki.fiery background: A background mostly filled with fire.
wiki.swan: A large waterbird with a long flexible neck, short legs, webbed feet, a broad bill, and typically all-white plumage.
wiki.super saiyan 2: A level beyond Super Saiyan 1 which looks remarkably similar to the original, but with subtle visual changes and more power, depicted as electricity appearing around the fighter.
wiki.sail: A piece of fabric that provides the motive power to propel a sailing vessel.
wiki.pansy: A popular, decorative garden flower hybridized from Viola tricolor with other Viola species. Popular for use in flower beds.
wiki.starfighter: A common type of combat spacecraft designed to be small and fast, and often manned by a single pilot. Frequent in many science fiction works.
wiki.underground: Pictures that are set under the surface of the earth.
wiki.crater: A bowl-shaped pit on ground (planetary surface). It is usually caused either by a meteorite impact, powerful explosion, or by geological activity on the planet. On Earth, craters are generally the results of volcanic eruption.
wiki.meteor: A rock or similar object, of any size from a grain of sand to a small moon, descending into a planet's atmosphere, usually while burning up dramatically. If the object can't be identified as anything other than a trail of light in the sky, use the shooting star tag instead. See forum topic #5294.
wiki.lavender (flower): A purple flower from the Lamiaceae (mint) family, with a whorl shape. If the flowers hang down, it's most likely wisteria instead.
wiki.saturn (planet): Sixth planet of our solar system, between Jupiter (planet) and Uranus (planet). It is best known for its visible planetary rings that orbit around it.
wiki.invisible floor: When a character is standing or sitting even though there is no visible ground. This is to draw the character without drawing a background.
wiki.sacabambaspis: Extinct genus of prehistoric jawless fish from the Ordovician period. Images of a poorly reconstructed model of Sacabambaspis janvieri present at Helsinki Natural History Museum have since gone viral online.
wiki.pinecone: A seed-bearing organ on a pine tree that contains the reproductive structures. They are divided between male and female cones, with the males producing pollen and the females producing seeds. The female cones are the more recognizable ones for their large woody appearance.
wiki.tyrannosaurus rex: A large theropod carnivorous dinosaur. Often referred to as "T. rex" for short, from the type specimen's scientific name Tyrannosaurus rex.
wiki.energy barrier: A barrier created out of any sort of energy, including magical and psychic energy. Frequently the energy produces a transparent wall, screen, or bubble, but may also be used for creating things such as surfaces for walking on. Energy barriers are a common feature in science fiction and fantasy.
wiki.multicolored sky: A sky that has at least two or more colors. This is especially prevalent during a sunset or sunrise.
wiki.orchid: The second largest flowering plant family in the world, with ~28,000 accepted species. Which makes this an umbrella tag for a very wide variety of plants, often with very divergent appearances.
wiki.entrance: Ambiguous tag. Please tag the specific kind of entrance. → cave, doorway, genkan, gate, getabako, moon gate, POV doorway, school gateway
wiki.eurasian tree sparrow: A species of sparrow with a distinctive black patch on its cheeks. It is found throughout most of Europe and Asia, and is the most common sparrow species in Japan.
wiki.body pillow: A long pillow used for full-body support while sleeping, often by hugging it.
wiki.pony (animal): A pony is a smaller breed of horse. They typically have stouter proportions than horses.
wiki.lobster: A large marine crustacean with stalked eyes, long antennae, and five pairs of legs, the first pair of which are large pincer claws.
wiki.falling flower: A flower that appears to be falling. Not to be confused with falling petals.
wiki.flower bed: A section of soil or a raised planter set up in a garden or public space for growing and displaying flowering plants.
wiki.glowing petals: Petals which appear to be glowing or radiating light in some way; often white, pink or blue and with a ghostly somewhat transparent look.
wiki.giraffe: The tallest living land animal in the world, with extremely long legs and neck. It lives in the savannahs of Africa.
wiki.biplane: An airplane with two pairs of wings, one above the other.
wiki.on boat: Sitting, standing or resting on a boat. The boat may be still or being driven.
wiki.getabako: A Japanese shoe locker or shoe cubby. Commonplace at the entrance of schools.
wiki.boom barrier: A barrier to prevent people from crossing a road or intersection. Common at security checkpoints and railroad crossings, and usually has either yellow-and-black or red-and-white hazard stripes.
wiki.pixel heart: Pixelated heart symbol. Commonly associated with health bars in video games.
wiki.hot air balloon: A balloon that flies because of the buoyancy generated by heated air trapped in a gas-tight envelope or bag; passengers and freight are usually carried in a basket suspended underneath it. The envelope or bag may be simple or complex in design.
wiki.ant: Social bugs known to form colonies, with each ant assigned to a role. While their size may vary, they have mandibles and antennae. Females might have wings.
wiki.black butterfly: A butterfly that is colored black.
wiki.rose bush: A bush that has roses growing.
wiki.postbox (outgoing mail): A physical receptacle into which members of the public deposit outgoing mail for delivery by the postal service. Also known as a collection box, drop box, etc.
wiki.traffic mirror: A traffic mirror (or convex safety mirror) is a curved, wide-angle mirror installed at blind spots, sharp corners, intersections, and driveways to improve visibility of oncoming traffic.
wiki.handrail: The circular portion attached to the top of a railing to make it safer and more convenient to grab. Commonly seen near stairs and escalators, but can also be fixed to a wall on its own.
wiki.mistletoe: A plant with rounded leaves and white berries. It's often associated with Christmas, where there is a tradition of kissing under branches of mistletoe.
wiki.planetary ring: A ring of debris orbiting around a planet. The rings of Saturn (planet) are the most famous example in our solar system.
wiki.blood spray: Blood gushing out or spraying from some location.
wiki.in orbit: A scene set in orbit around a planet or other celestial body in space.
wiki.crustacean: Group of mostly aquatic arthropod invertebrates (possess jointed legs, body segments, exoskeleton). A feature distinguishing them from other arthropods, such as bugs and spiders, is that their jointed limbs form branched appendages.
wiki.tokyo big sight: A popular nickname for a Japanese convention center near Odaiba in Tokyo mostly represented by its iconic Conference Tower with its inverted four-pyramid design. Many anime and manga-related conventions, such as Comiket, are held here. Tokyo Big Sight's formal name is the Tokyo International Exhibition Center.
wiki.mother's day: A holiday to honor the mother of the family.
wiki.broken wall: A wall that has been broken through by an external force.
wiki.grate: A frame with bars running through it. Commonly see over prison windows and vent (object)s to allow light of fluids through without allowing larger objects through.
wiki.mexico: Anything related to the country and culture of México.
wiki.string of light bulbs: Long strands of usually globe-shaped light bulbs suspended between two or more points for decorative illumination.
wiki.food-themed background: A background that consists of food. It can be a repeating pattern or a large variety of foods.
wiki.bishie sparkle: An aura surrounding beautiful characters in anime, representing a dreamlike state of beauty, love, or romance.
wiki.empty picture frame: A picture frame without a canvas or photo.
wiki.ship turret: An armored enclosure for cannon(s), usually found on warships. They allow cannons to swivel to fire in multiple directions.
wiki.food wrapper: Paper or plastic wrapped around food. Often used for either preservation, or to allow for easier handling. Paper food wrappers are commonly used with fast food.
wiki.polaroid photo: An instant on-the-spot photograph, which typically has a square photo inside a white rectangular frame. See polaroid camera for the camera itself.
wiki.fender stratocaster: Solid body electric guitar, made and produced by American instrument maker Fender since 1954.
wiki.food packaging: Packaging used to display food for sale in a shop (such as a supermarket).
wiki.narutomaki: A small fish cake with a red spiral. It is often used to garnish ramen.
wiki.lead pipe: A pipe made of lead (or any other metal), which is often used as an improvised bludgeoning weapon.
wiki.wok: A bowl-shaped cooking vessel. It used in a range of different Chinese cooking techniques, including stir frying, steaming, pan frying, deep frying, poaching, boiling, braising, searing, stewing, making soup, smoking and roasting nuts...
wiki.inflatable whale: An inflatable toy with a whale design.
wiki.chocolate syrup: Liquid chocolate that has been thinned to the consistency of syrup, often seen drizzled over ice cream or desserts.
wiki.circular saw: A saw consisting of a circle of serrated metal and powered with electricity, unlike more traditional hand saws. Commonly found in workshops and factories all around the world.
wiki.cherry tomato: A miniature tomato, usually 1-2 inches (2.5-5cm) in diameter. Commonly used in salads or eaten individually.
wiki.strawberry slice: A cut portion of a strawberry.
wiki.on box: Something or someone is on a box.
wiki.pin: Sharp, slender objects used to fasten things together. Unlike sewing needles, which have a hole used for drawing thread, pins have a head like a nail (hardware), but smaller, round, and usually made from plastic. They are commonly used to secure fabrics for sewing or stick papers and photos to bulletin boards.
wiki.waffle: A flat pastry pressed with a grid pattern. Frequently served with syrup and/or fruit.
wiki.strawberry cake: A cake that uses strawberry as a primary ingredient.
wiki.asahi breweries: The largest of the four major brands of beer in Japan (the others being Kirin, Sapporo, and Suntory).
wiki.stuffed bird: A stuffed animal modeled after any kind of bird.
wiki.wooden box: A box made of wood, such as a crate.
wiki.barcode scanner: A barcode scanner is a device designed to read printed barcodes, decode the data contained in the barcode, and send the data to a computer. Commonly seen used at the checkout counter of stores.
wiki.chocolate chip cookie: A type of cookie distinguished by morsels of chocolate mixed into the dough.
wiki.keyring: A small ring designed to slot multiple keys into so they can be kept bunched together. It may also have decorative charm (object)s connected to it with small chains.
wiki.jiaozi: A type of dumpling commonly eaten in China and other parts of East Asia.
wiki.egg yolk: The 'yellow' part of an egg, containing all of the egg's fat and cholesterol. If left intact while cooking eggs, it will result in the distinctive appearance of fried eggs. If mixed together with the egg white and cooked, it will result in omelets or scrambled eggs.
wiki.bell pepper: A vegetable with a hollow inside that has numerous little seeds that should be removed before cooking or eating. Unlike spicy peppers like habanero and jalapeno, bell peppers are sweeter in flavor and come in many different colors. Sliced bell peppers are a popular topping for pizza.
wiki.spork: A spoon with three or four short prongs at the end to resemble a fork. The word is a portmanteau of 'fork' and 'spoon'. The spork is most popularly used for eating ice cream.
wiki.cue stick: The long, thin stick used in playing billiards. It is used to poke at a billiard ball in order to knock balls against each other and send them rolling into pockets on the table.
wiki.kebab: Ambiguous tag. → shish kebab, doner kebab, doner sandwich, doner wrap
wiki.shopping basket: A plastic basket found in supermarkets to accommodate shoppers carrying their groceries.
wiki.beretta 1301: An Italian 12 gauge gas-operated semi-automatic shotgun manufactured by Beretta. Major variants are available in both single-piece buttstock and one with pistol grip. It is the signature weapon of Hoshino from Blue Archive.
wiki.basketball hoop: In basketball (sport), the hoop is the object one must throw the ball into in order to score. Typically accompanied by a backboard.
wiki.floating sword: A sword floating on its own with no apparent propulsion system or force applied, usually next to a character.
wiki.pon de ring: A Japanese-style donut characterized by its mochi-like chewy texture and beaded ring shape. Made popular by Mister Donut in Japan.
wiki.cymbals: A concave plate of brass or bronze that produces a sharp, ringing sound when struck. They are commonly played by being hand-held and clashed together or seen with drum sets being struck by drumsticks.
wiki.animal-themed food: Food that is shaped like or themed after an animal.
wiki.double scoop: When there are two or more individual scoops of ice cream on top of an ice cream cone or in a bowl.
wiki.fighting game: A video game genre where the player controls an on-screen character and engages in close combat with an opponent. These characters tend to be of equal power and fight matches consisting of several rounds, which take place in an arena (or "stage").
wiki.spiked ball and chain: A variant of the ball and chain (weapon) with spikes on the ball.
wiki.cd case: Case for carrying and storing compact discs.
wiki.puzzle piece: The single piece of a jigsaw puzzle.
wiki.kite: A light frame covered with thin material flown in the wind at the end of a long string, especially for recreation.
wiki.pitchfork: A multi-pronged agricultural tool used to lift and pitch (throw) loose materials such as hay, grass, manure, or other such materials.
wiki.iv stand: The pole for hanging the bag(s) for an intravenous drip or blood transfusion. The stereotypical IV stand generally has a distinctive pair of curlicued hooks at the top, and is usually wheeled so that the patient can bring it along when moving about. Some are height-adjustable for use when sitting or standing.
wiki.snowboard: A wide board which attached to the bottom of both two ski boots through the skateboard bindings. Shorter and wider than skis.
wiki.strong zero: Strong Zero is a brand of chuuhai (an alcoholic beverage) produced by Suntory. It comes in many different fruit flavors.
wiki.crumpled paper: A piece of paper that has wrinkles (formed from folding) or has been crushed into a ball.
wiki.grease (mechanical): A fluid used for lubricating mechanical parts. This tends to be commonly depicted in images as being smeared on a mechanic's face and/or clothing.
wiki.nori (seaweed): An edible type of Japanese seaweed, used as a wrap for foods like sushi, onigiri and senbei, as well as a garnish in soup and noodle dishes.
wiki.ballistic shield: A ballistic shield (also called a tactical shield) is a modern heavy duty shield used by police and military to block bullets and other projectiles. It is made of metal or other solid material, giving an opaque appearance. A viewing slot is often present.
wiki.board eraser: A type of fibrous eraser designed to wipe off chalk writing from a chalkboard or marker from a whiteboard.
wiki.beam cannon: An energy cannon that fires energy beams.
wiki.character-themed food: Food that is shaped like or, less-commonly, printed with an image of a character. Common forms include pancakes, cookies, ice cream bars, and chocolate or other candies, but many other foods may be character-shaped as well.
wiki.wooden spoon: A type of spoon made of wood. Generally more utilized in food preparation than in consumption.
wiki.eotech: A line of holographic firearm sights produced by the eponymous EOTech company, intended for close-quarters combat use.
wiki.boomerang: A curved piece of wood or other similar material, most of which are designed to return to the thrower. Probably the most well known is the Australian version, although boomerangs in other shapes (and from other cultures) also exist. Boomerangs are used mainly as toys and hunting weapons.
wiki.lighting cigarette: When a character is seen lighting a cigarette, be it their own, someone else's, or several at once. See lighting cigar for cigars.
wiki.saxophone: A brass musical instrument that is popular in jazz, classical, and funk music. Comes in four popular sizes (listed from smallest to largest): soprano, alto, tenor, and baritone. Smaller and larger variations than the soprano and baritone exist, but they are very rarely used.
wiki.boombox: A portable stereo system with a carrying handle that plays music from CDs, cassette tapes, or the radio using builtin speakers.
wiki.flower basket: A basket used to hold flowers.
wiki.razor: A bladed tool used for shaving. See razor blade for the individual disposable blade itself.
wiki.heart wand: A wand or staff that has a heart shape affixed at the top.
wiki.ice cream cup: Ambiguous tag. See: • Disposable ice cream cup • Sherbet glass • Sherbet cup • Milkshake glass • Parfait glass • Pilsner glass → Disposable ice cream cup, Sherbet glass, Sherbet cup, Milkshake glass, Parfait glass, Pilsner glass, drinking glass
wiki.melon soda: A green soda flavored like melon, popular in Japan. It is frequently seen as an ingredient for an ice cream float.
wiki.in bowl: Used when a living thing is depicted inside a bowl.
wiki.liquor: An alcoholic beverage made by distillation rather than by fermentation.
wiki.target: An object, generally with a marked surface, used for target practice.
wiki.metal baseball bat: A baseball bat made of metal instead of wood.
wiki.tako-san wiener: A wiener or hot dog that has been cut to look like an octopus, often seen in children's bento boxes. Kani-san wiener is the crab-shaped variant.
wiki.nunchaku: Nunchaku, more commonly known as the "nunchucks", is a traditional East Asian weapon that consists of two sticks connected at their ends with a short chain or rope.
wiki.gelatin: A translucent and colorless powder derived from collagen inside animal skin and bones. It is added to water to firm it up and provide texture, and tends to jiggle if moved around.
wiki.pastry box: A box designed for carrying pastries such as cupcakes or doughnuts, usually either a half dozen or a whole dozen.
wiki.radar: Equipment or displays for using wireless technology for tracking different types of things.
wiki.medicine: A drug or herb used to maintain health or treat a health issue.
wiki.fire extinguisher: A portable device that discharges a jet of water, foam, gas, or other material to extinguish a fire.
wiki.heavy machine gun: A type of machine gun that use large caliber ammunition (but less than 20 mm). Primarily designed to provide a continuous suppressive fire and pierce through light cover and unarmored vehicles. Usually mounted instead of being handheld due to heavy weight and large size.
wiki.paperclip: A simple tool used to hold sheets of paper together, usually made of wire bent to a looped shape.
wiki.tank shell: A large explosive projectile fired by a tank.
wiki.rpg (weapon): RPG, short for ручной противотанковый гранатомёт/Ruchnoy Protivotankovy Granatomyot in Russian, which translates to "hand-held anti-tank grenade launcher", refers to a hand-held weapon originally developed to destroy tanks and bunkers and comes in a variety of shapes, designs, purposes, and types.
wiki.taiko drum: A Japanese percussion instrument played with taiko sticks. They are commonly seen as wide-bodied and with a membrane that is either tacked or sewn to the body at both end.
wiki.tupet: A juice drink contained inside a tube made from plastic.
wiki.fishing hook: A small metal hook attached to a fishing line that is used to catch fish.
wiki.lunchbox: A small box filled with prepared food to eat at lunch.
wiki.stuffed whale: A stuffed animal resembling a whale.
wiki.gunpla: A model kit for building a Gundam mecha. Produced by Bandai.
wiki.coffee maker: Any type of appliance used to brew coffee from coffee beans.
wiki.milkshake: A drink made by blending milk, ice cream and other flavorings together in a blender.
wiki.battery: A container consisting of one or more cells, in which chemical energy is converted into electricity and used as a source of power.
wiki.nigirizushi: A type of sushi consisting of a slice of raw fish (food) over pressed vinegared rice.
wiki.pliers: A tool used for gripping something round like a pipe or rod. Some are used for twisting or cutting wires.
wiki.alcohol carton: Alcohol such as sake or wine packaged in a drink carton or box.
wiki.mayonnaise: A condiment made by emulsifying oil and eggs.
wiki.oden: A Japanese winter dish consisting of several ingredients such as hardboiled eggs, daikon radish, konnyaku (food), shirataki noodles and processed fish cakes stewed in a light, soy-flavoured dashi broth.
wiki.shot glass: A smaller tumbler glass, designed to serve high-alcohol content drinks such as spirits or liquor.
wiki.rice cooker: A kitchen appliance designed to cook rice automatically. It usually has a removable bowl and is provided with a shamoji and a measuring cup. Rice cookers can be electric- or gas-powered, with a capacity measured in liters.
wiki.tank turret: A type of turret designed to be mounted on a ground military vehicle, often but not exclusively a tank.
wiki.salt shaker: A shaker used to dispense salt. Almost always partnered with pepper shaker.
wiki.incoming drink: A character giving a drink to the viewer or pouring a drink into a cup held by the viewer.
wiki.ocarina: An egg-shaped woodwind instrument, relative of the whistle.
wiki.hamburger steak: A food item which consists of ground meat clumped together in a round shape and cooked. Unlike a meatloaf, neither a mold nor oven are used, and it is mainly cooked on a frying pan.
wiki.billiard ball: The small, hard ball used in billiards. The number, type, diameter, color, and pattern of the balls differ depending upon the specific game being played.
wiki.m16a1: An early version of the M16. Distinguishable by its triangular grip and 20 round magazine.
wiki.kayari buta: Kayari-Buta, also known as Katori-Buta, is a ceramic, pig-shaped incense burner in which insect-repelling incense is burned, usually in the form of a mosquito coil. Evocative of summer.
wiki.chocolate cornet: A trumpet shell-shaped bread item with chocolate filling. Izumi Konata's favorite food and Inugami Korone's namesake.
wiki.canister: A canister is a cylindrical container, frequently made of metal, for holding a specific object (such as film) or substance, especially a gas or liquid.
wiki.marionette: A puppet controlled by puppet strings.
wiki.pink innertube: A type of recreational swim ring used to float in the water, especially by young children and people who cannot swim. So called because it resembles (and in earlier times, usually was) the inner tube of a car tire.
wiki.disco ball: A multifaceted mirrored sphere that reflects light directed at it in many directions, producing a complex display. Its surface consists of hundreds or thousands of facets, nearly all of approximately the same shape and size.
wiki.stuffed fish: A stuffed animal based on a fish.
wiki.euphonium: Euphonium (from the Greek word εὔφωνος, meaning "well-sounding" or "sweet-voiced") is a conical-bore, baritone-voiced brass instrument. The euphonium is a valved instrument; nearly all current models are piston valved, though rotary valved models do exist.
wiki.queen (playing card): A playing card rank situated between the jack and the king, considered to be the middle of the three "court" ranks.
wiki.stuffed sheep: A stuffed animal that looks like a sheep.
wiki.turntable: A turntable is a modern phonograph, also known as a record player or record machine. They are a popular machine commonly used by Disc Jockeys. Turntables are distinguished from older phonographs by the fact that they have electrical pickups instead of a purely mechanical one.
wiki.ipad: A tablet computer created by Apple Inc.
wiki.tanghulu: A traditional Chinese snack of candied fruit. Tanghulu are often mistaken for regular candied fruits; however, they are coated in a hardened sugar syrup. This sweet and sour treat has been made since the Song Dynasty and remains popular throughout northern China.
wiki.cheesecake: A type of cake consisting of a biscuit, sponge cake or pastry topped with fresh cream cheese flavored with different fruits, coffee, nuts, and/or chocolate.
wiki.puzzle: Various types of puzzles, including jigsaw puzzles, Rubik's Magic puzzle, puzzle rings, etc.
wiki.starting block: An object used by athletes in racing events as a starting point or as a place to brace their feet, such as in swimming competitions and track and field events.
wiki.shamisen: A traditional Japanese three-stringed instrument usually played with a plectrum called a bachi.
wiki.cupping glass: Holding a balloon-shaped wine glass by the underside of the bowl rather than by gripping the stem. Note that this speeds the transfer of body heat to one's drink and is usually regarded as bad etiquette as it defeats the purpose of a stemmed glass.
wiki.ammunition box: A box that stores ammunition. Some variants can be attached into a weapons like machine guns, serving purpose to hold ammunition belt, but completely different from magazine (weapon)s due to lack of a spring (object)-like structure that pushes cartridges into the chamber.
wiki.sledgehammer: A large hammer typically intended to be used with both hands that has a long shaft and a flat hammerhead, usually made of metal. They're frequently used for demolition, and are sometimes equipment used by police for raids for forced entry onto properties.
wiki.stuffing: Springy material that is filled inside plush dolls and stuffed toys.
wiki.horn (instrument): For any unspecified hollow tubed (funnel) object that is used by a character for musical or alerting purposes. Such as a makeshift horn from a goats horn or a plastic horn with no valves. Also, vuvuzelas.
wiki.red outline: An outline around a character or object that is colored red.
wiki.screenshot inset: A screenshot that is contained as a smaller inset within an image.
wiki.body horror: A subgenre of horror (theme) that showcases grotesque or psychologically disturbing violations of the human body. These violations may manifest through aberrant sex, mutations, mutilation, zombification, gratuitous violence, disease, or unnatural movements of the body.
wiki.game screenshot inset: When a screenshot from a video game is embedded in an image as a reference inset.
wiki.doodle inset: A doodle that only takes up a smaller portion of the image.
wiki.double exposure: The effect of superimposing two or more images together. Often utilized to frame one image within the contour or boundaries of another image.
wiki.orange border: An image that has an orange-colored border around its edges.
wiki.color contrast: An image with strongly contrasting or opposing colors, most commonly taking the form of warm-cool contrast.
wiki.low poly: 3D modelling that features very few polygons. Common in older and handheld game consoles such as the PlayStation 1 and Nintendo DS due to hardware limitations. Some artists intentionally create works in this style as a homage to games from those systems.
wiki.scanlines: An effect that mimics the raster scanning pattern of typical cathode-ray tube displays. Not to be confused with vector displays or color halftones from scanning.
wiki.cartoonized: A non-cartoon character drawn in a Western toon (style) style. This includes anime and manga characters, but also real people and characters from live-action media as well.
wiki.sprite: Sprites are game assets, usually small pieces of art, that are able to be integrated in larger scenes in 2D-based video games. For instance, a character that can be moved, or an object that can be picked up.
wiki.paper texture: An image with a paper-like texture. Does not matter if it is done with traditional media or faux traditional media.
wiki.grey outline: An outline that is colored grey.
wiki.revealing layer: The effect of treating an image as multi-layered paper, where ripping or removing one or more layers reveals something else (e.g. a successively less-dressed version of the character in the same pose, or the circuit board inside an electronic device).
wiki.fading border: An image with borders that fades out gradually, instead of meeting a sharp outline.

wiki.yukishiro honoka: A caring schoolgirl who only recently met Misumi Nagisa. Transforms into Cure White and is the more intelligent one in battle. Voiced by Yukana.
wiki.yukoku kiriko: A quiet but kind girl from Idolmaster Shiny Colors. She is in the unit L'Antica (idolmaster).
wiki.yukoku roberu: A VTuber and member of Holostars from the 2nd batch, SunTempo. Designed by Mebaru.
wiki.yume (blue archive): A character from Blue Archive. Former president of the Abydos High School Student Council. Her full name is Kuchinashi Yume.
wiki.yumehara nozomi: Yes! Precure 5 character. The civilian identity of Cure Dream.
wiki.yumekawa yui: Protagonist of Idol Time Pripara. Yumekawa Shogo's sister. As her name suggests, she is based on yume kawaii.
wiki.yumeko (touhou): A Touhou PC-98 character. Stage 5 boss in Mystic Square. Shinki (touhou)'s maid. Could be considered a sort of prototype version of Izayoi Sakuya, though she uses swords instead of knives, and her combat trick is manipulating space rather than time.
wiki.yumemi riamu: An idol appearing in Idolmaster Cinderella Girls, debuting on February 7, 2019. She is voiced by Hoshiki Seena.
wiki.yumeno himiko: Character from Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony.
wiki.yumi (senran kagura): Main supporting character in Senran Kagura. A Third-Year student and leader at the Gessen Academy.
wiki.yumizuka satsuki: Also known as "Sacchin", is a character that appears in Tsukihime and Melty Blood.
wiki.yuna (ff10): Playable character from FINAL FANTASY X, X-2 and Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy. In FFX, she is a summoner on a pilgrimage to defeat Sin. In X-2, she becomes a proficient Gunner-class warrior searching the world for Spira's legacies while uncovering a forgotten machina weapon called Vegnagun.
wiki.yunaka (fire emblem): A playable character from Fire Emblem Engage, known for her peppy attitude and tendency to use strange phrases, such as “hiya papaya” when greeting someone, or “zappy” to express interest. She’s also the initial user of Micaiah (Fire Emblem)’s ring after attempting to steal it.
wiki.yune (fire emblem): A character in Fire Emblem: Radiant Dawn. Yune appears in two forms, a bird form and a humanoid form as .
wiki.yuni (precure): Star Twinkle Precure character. An alien cat girl from Planet Rainbow who seeks the Star Color Pens to save her people. She has multiple personas that she utilizes for her mission, including the phantom thief Blue Cat (precure), the pop idol Mao (precure), and the feline butler Bakenyan (precure).
wiki.yuni (princess connect!): A character from Princess Connect! and Princess Connect! Re:Dive. She is a member of the Friendship Club (princess connect!).
wiki.yunli (honkai: star rail): Playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. A sword hunter from the Xianzhou Zhuming and granddaughter of General Huaiyan (Honkai: Star Rail). Voiced by Wakayama Shion in Japanese and Brenna Larsen in English.
wiki.yuno (hidamari sketch): Yuno (sometimes called "Yunocchi" by Miyako (hidamari sketch)) is a young girl and main character in Hidamari Sketch.
wiki.yunyun (konosuba): Yunyun is a main supporting character of the KonoSuba series and deuteragonist of the Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Bakuen wo! spin-off. She is a member of the Crimson Demons and daughter of the Village Chief, as well as former classmate and self-proclaimed rival to Megumin.
wiki.yura (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the Japanese light cruiser Yura. Character designed by Konishi (koconatu).
wiki.yura kai ni (kancolle): The kai ni/second remodel form of Kantai Collection's Yura (kancolle), as seen in post #2765212.
wiki.yuri (doki doki literature club): Yuri is a character in Doki Doki Literature Club. She has long purple hair and purple eyes. She is a quiet girl with a passion for horror novels.
wiki.yuri lowell: The main character of Tales of Vesperia.
wiki.yusa (angel beats!): Yusa is a character in Angel Beats!. She has brown eyes and long blonde hair tied into twintails with hair ribbons. She is usually seen wearing a headset to communicate the state of affairs to Yuri.
wiki.yusa emi: A character from Hataraku Maou-sama!. She is the half-human, half-angel Hero who defeated Maou Sadao and forced him to flee to Earth. She pursued him to Earth and like Maou, lost most of her powers and was forced to integrate into modern Japanese society. Her true form is Emilia Justina.
wiki.yusa kozue: An iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls character in the Cute (Pink Flower) category. Kozue is an innocent yet absent-minded girl recruited by the Producer. She is quite inquisitive, with slight hints that she's lived a somewhat sheltered life. She tends to elongate any end vowel and speaks entirely in hiragana.
wiki.yuubari (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the Japanese light cruiser Yuubari. Character design by Konishi (koconatu), voiced by Bridcutt Sarah Emi.
wiki.yuudachi (azur lane): Personification of the fourth ship of the Shiratsuyu-class destroyers, Yuudachi (夕立), in Azur Lane.
wiki.yuudachi (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the Japanese destroyer Yuudachi. Character design by Kujou Ichiso, voiced by Tanibe Yumi.
wiki.yuudachi kai ni (kancolle): The second remodel of Yuudachi from Kantai Collection.
wiki.yuugumo (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the Japanese destroyer Yuugumo. Character design by Fujikawa, voiced by Taketatsu Ayana.
wiki.yuuhi riri: A Nijisanji Virtual YouTuber, part of the 2nd generation (nijisanji) and designed by Nezumidoshi. Her name is displayed as Yuhi Riri on her YouTube channel but her name is meant to be read as Yuuhi Riri, rendered on her Twitter.
wiki.yuuka (blue archive): A character from Blue Archive. She serves as the treasurer for Millennium's student council, Seminar (blue archive). Her full name is Hayase Yuuka.
wiki.yuuka (track) (blue archive): The gym uniform costume of Blue Archive's Yuuka (blue archive).
wiki.yuuki (princess connect!): The main character of Princess Connect! and Princess Connect! Re:Dive. In the first game, he has no facial appearance, but in the second he does. He is a member of Gourmet Guild (princess connect!) and a former member of Twinkle Wish (princess connect!).
wiki.yuuki (sao): An ALfheim Online avatar from Sword Art Online (Mother's Rosario Story Arc).
wiki.yuuki aoi: Singer and voice actress. For artworks created by her, use this artist tag: Yuuki Aoi (Aoi Town)
wiki.yuuki haru: An iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls character in the Cool (Blue Diamond) category.
wiki.yuuki juudai: Known as Jaden Yuki in the English dub.
wiki.yuuki makoto (persona 3): The silent male protagonist from Persona 3.
wiki.yuuki mikan: Yuuki Rito's little sister. Good at domestic housework, and very reliable. Also close to Konjiki no Yami.
wiki.yuuki setsuna (love live!): A character in Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club. Her real name is Nakagawa Nana, with "Yuki Setsuna" being a stage name. She uses that name to hide the fact that she is Nijigasaki's Student Council President (until she is succeeded by Mifune Shioriko later in the story) and from her family.
wiki.yuuki yuuna: The protagonist of Yuuki Yuuna wa Yuusha de Aru.
wiki.yuuno scrya: A character in Mahou Shoujo Lyrical Nanoha who also appears in Mahou Shoujo Lyrical Nanoha A's and Mahou Shoujo Lyrical Nanoha StrikerS, but less in the latter.
wiki.yuuri (shoujo shuumatsu ryokou): One of the two main characters of Shoujo Shuumatsu Ryokou, alongside Chito. She is impatient, selfish and energetic, caring more about food and other immediate pleasures than complex things like history or future planning. She is illiterate but a good marksman, often carrying a gun.
wiki.yuzu (blue archive): A character from Blue Archive. President of the Game Development Department (blue archive). Her full name is Hanaoka Yuzu.
wiki.yuzuki choco: A Virtual YouTuber and member of hololive's 2nd generation (hololive). A school doctor at a Makai school. She is a demon girl who looks like a succubus but isn't one. Designed by Masuishi Kinoto.
wiki.yuzuki choco (1st costume): The default costume of hololive's Yuzuki Choco,
wiki.yuzuki roa: A Nijisanji Virtual YouTuber. Character designed by Bekotarou.
wiki.yuzuki yukari: Yuzuki Yukari is a Japanese VOCALOID and VOICEROID developed by Vocalomakets and distributed by AH-Software Co. Ltd., and was released for the VOCALOID3 and VOICEROID+ engine on December 22, 2011. She is voiced by Ishiguro Chihiro.
wiki.yuzuki yukari (shizuku): A voicebank for Yuzuki Yukari for the A.I. VOICE engine.
wiki.yuzuriha (under night in-birth): Character who appears in Under Night In-Birth. She is a cheerful young lady whose family has ties to the faction, Night Blade. She uses a type of Iaijutsu technique that is learned by descendants of her family. She affectionately calls her sword "Ayame-chan".
wiki.yuzuriha inori: Yuzuriha Inori is the female protagonist of Guilty Crown, and a member of Funeral Parlour.
wiki.z1 leberecht maass (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the German destroyer Z1 Leberecht Maass. Character design by Shimada Fumikane, voiced by Endou Aya.
wiki.z23 (azur lane): Azur Lane's depiction of the German destroyer Z23, lead ship of the 1936A-class. In the game and the fandom, she is often referred to as Nimi in reference to the Iroha order of her number.
wiki.z3 max schultz (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the German destroyer Z3 Max Schultz. Character design by Shimada Fumikane, voiced by Endou Aya.
wiki.z46 (azur lane): Azur Lane's personification of the German destroyer Z46. Character designed by Kinjo Kuromomo, voiced by Chihara Minori.
wiki.zac (league of legends): Male Slime (creature) League of Legends Champion.
wiki.zaizen tokiko: An iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls character in the Passion (Yellow Sun) category. Tokiko is a forcefully direct woman who believes men are inferior and require painful punishment to keep them useful. Her initial interest for being an idol was that the idea amused her.
wiki.zaku ii: A mecha from the Gundam series. Notable because it has the distinction of being the first robot to appear in the original anime (and the entire franchise).
wiki.zaku ii s char custom: A legendary mobile suit from the Gundam universe. It first appeared in the original Mobile Suit Gundam anime TV series from 1979.
wiki.zange: A shrine maiden nun from the Kannagi: Crazy Shrine Maidens series.
wiki.zangoose: Pokémon #0335 in the National Pokédex, a Normal-type.
wiki.zara (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the Italian heavy cruiser Zara. Character design by Jiji (Aardvark), voiced by Akasaki Chinatsu.
wiki.zas m21 (girls' frontline): An android representing the Zastava M21 in Girls' Frontline.
wiki.zayne (love and deepspace): Character from the game Love and Deepspace.
wiki.zen'in maki: A supporting character in Jujutsu Kaisen and one of the main protagonists of its prequel, Jujutsu Kaisen 0: Jujutsu High. Daughter of Ogi and the elder twin sister of Mai.
wiki.zen'in maki (post-shibuya): After the Shibuya Incident, Zen'in Maki's appearance changed significantly due to severe burn scars from Jogo (Jujutsu Kaisen)'s flames, leaving extensive scars all over her face and limbs. Her hair is now ear-length, and she has developed a more muscular, robust physique.
wiki.zero (code geass): The alterego of Lelouch Vi Britannia, the main character from the anime Code Geass.
wiki.zero (drag-on dragoon): Main protagonist of Drag-On Dragoon 3. She normally has a flower over her eye and a mechanical prosthetic arm.
wiki.zero (mega man): One of the three main characters of the Mega Man X (series) series, as well as the protagonist of the Mega Man Zero (series) series. He is voiced by Okiayu Ryoutarou.
wiki.zero two (darling in the franxx): DARLING in the FRANXX character and its deuteragonist. Nickname is based on her designation as "Code:002". Has pink hair, green eyes, medium breasts, and has small red horns. Usually wears a white hairband.
wiki.zero two (young) (darling in the franxx): Her appearance in Darling in the Franxx as a child.
wiki.zeta gundam (mobile suit): The MSZ-006 Zeta Gundam is the first transformable lead Gundam-type mobile suit mecha in the entire Gundam franchise, and the titular mobile suit of Mobile Suit Zeta Gundam (1985). It also appears in the Gundam ZZ (1986) sequel series.
wiki.zhong lanzhu: A character in Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club. She's a transfer student from Hong Kong and fluent in 3 languages (Mandarin, Cantonese, Japanese). She is a very competitive and somewhat arrogant person, though it varies between the anime and ALL STARS.
wiki.zhu yuan: A playable character in Zenless Zone Zero. A member of New Eridu Public Security, she is the Captain of the Criminal Investigation Special Response Team.
wiki.ziche fuzhao: Ziju Fuzhao is a character in Touqi Guaitan. He is Li Yuting's coworker.
wiki.zidane tribal: Main character of Final Fantasy IX, sporting a monkey tail. A thief in the rogue group Tantalus, he fancies himself a ladies' man, and kidnaps Princess Garnet Til Alexandros XVII at her request. He fights with dual daggers or a swallow sword, and can steal from enemies.
wiki.zima (arknights): A playable Vanguard Operator in Arknights. An Ursus.
wiki.zooey (granblue fantasy): Granblue Fantasy character. Voiced by Koshimizu Ami. Also known as Primal Beast Grand Order, one of the Arbitrators who originated from Cosmos (granblue fantasy).
wiki.zorua: Pokémon #0570 in the National Pokédex, a Dark-type.
wiki.zuifeng tenkai: The "One of the Old Dictators". Extra boss of Reactivate Majestical Imperial.
wiki.zuihou (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the Japanese light aircraft carrier Zuihou. Character design by Konishi (koconatu).
wiki.zuikaku (kancolle): Kantai Collection's personification of the Japanese aircraft carrier Zuikaku. Character design by Konishi (koconatu), voiced by Nomizu Iori.
wiki.zuikaku kai ni (kancolle): For her kai ni forms, Zuikaku's is basically a hypothetical remodel where she survived the Battle of Leyte Gulf (October 25, 1944) and received aircraft catapults as originally designed. An alternate second remodel depicts her in a hypothetical armored carrier form a la Taihou.
wiki.zundamon: A character who was originally created as VOICEROID Touhoku Zunko's pet in 2017, but received an official personification and text-to-speech voicebank under the VOICEVOX software in August 2021. She later received a singing voicebank under NEUTRINO (software) on July 31, 2022.
wiki.children: A young person between infancy and puberty. This may be the character's actual age, or they may be aged down by the artist.
